title: John Spytek on Fernando Mendoza: His time is coming, but he's got to earn it
summary: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak hasn't made it official, but all indications have been throughout the offseason and training camp that Kirk Cousins will open the season as starting quarterback — despite the club drafting Fernando Mendoza at No. 1 overall.
full_text: '' Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak hasn't made it official, but all indications have been throughout the offseason and training camp that Kirk Cousins will open the season as starting quarterback — despite the club drafting Fernando Mendoza at No. 1 overall. Mendoza flashed his potential in the preseason, though the performance was ultimately up and down. On Tuesday, General Manager John Spytek noted that Mendoza has been the same kind of guy they got to know during the pre-draft process, so it’s not like the team has been surprised at the way the quarterback has gone about his business. “He's a tireless worker. He loves football. He loves his teammates. He's energetic on the field. He's self-critical. He's self-aware. He's very accurate,” Spytek said, via transcript from the team. “His time is coming, but he's got to earn it every day, and he knows that. I think we're all very pleased with the person and his work ethic and his commitment to being a great quarterback.” While the team wants to make sure Mendoza is ready before putting him on the field, Spytek cited several different quarterbacks to note that there’s more than one way to develop a young QB. “Tom Brady, Aaron Rodgers, Jordan Love, Patrick Mahomes, Jayden Daniels. Like you said, there's success stories and failures in both ways,” Spytek said. “We're just trying to build the best team we can and play the guys that are most ready to play, and have a constant competition in every room, not just the quarterback room, but every room. “The expectation always will be that the best person, the person that's earned it, the person that can do their job for the team, will be the one that plays.” Mendoza completes 25-of-45 passes for 240 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions in the preseason. The Raiders will open the season at home against the Dolphins on Sept. 13.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Shilo Sanders testifies in ongoing bankruptcy trial
summary: The Shilo Sanders bankruptcy trial continues in Colorado, as he tries to have a massive judgment of $11.89 million discharged.
full_text: The Shilo Sanders bankruptcy trial continues in Colorado, as he tries to have a massive judgment of $11.89 million discharged. Via Olivia Doak of the Boulder Daily Camera , Shilo Sanders took the witness stand on Tuesday. He disputed prior testimony that painted him as the aggressor in a 2015 altercation that left John Darjean, who was a security guard at Shilo's school, with serious injuries. Shilo said that Darjean was “getting aggressive” and “attacked and assaulted” Shilo. He added that Darjean choked him. Other witnesses said they did not see Darjean choke Shilo Sanders. The fight happened after Darjean attempted to confiscate Shilo's phone. Shilo did not testify at the proceedings that resulted in the $11.89 million verdict, because he didn't show up for the trial. Also on Tuesday, a doctor testified that Darjean's injuries required a fusion of the C3 through C7 vertebrae in his neck. A 2018 deposition of Deion Sanders also was played in court. He said that, on the day of the incident, Darjean called Deion and said he was dealing with a situation with Shilo. “My exact words were to handle it like you’d handle anybody else,” Deion Sanders said in the deposition. Shilo's testimony is expected to continue on Wednesday. Deion possibly will be testifying virtually on Friday, depending on whether Shilo's lawyers open the door to the question of why Shilo would have been intent on not relinquishing his phone. The overriding question is whether the injuries inflicted by Shilo on Darjean were "willful and malicious." If the judge finds that they were, the $11.89 million judgment will not be discharged through the federal bankruptcy laws.
author: Mike Florio

title: Dabo Swinney on NFL players going back to college: It's embarrassing, we have no rules
summary: Clemson coach Dabo Swinney is preparing to open the season on Saturday against LSU, which has been at the forefront of attempting to get players who were on NFL rosters back into college football.
full_text: Clemson coach Dabo Swinney is preparing to open the season on Saturday against LSU, which has been at the forefront of attempting to get players who were on NFL rosters back into college football. And Swinney made clear on Tuesday that he is not a fan of the way NCAA eligibility rules have changed to make that possible. "It's kind of embarrassing, honestly. It's just embarrassing that that's where we are. I don't blame the kids, people trying to take advantage of the system, I just think it's embarrassing where we are with college football, and we've been there for a while," Swinney said. Swinney said he'd like to see college football establish clear rules that won't get overturned by judges, as has happened repeatedly when players have sued to regain NCAA eligibility. "It's embarrassing. I mean, it really is. We have no rules. There's no governance. I mean, it's a joke. There's zero rules. And when you enforce rules someone just goes and finds a judge to say, 'No, you can't enforce that rule.' Never did I think we'd be living in an era like this, but that's where we are," Swinney said. LSU has been attempting to add pass rusher Jack Pyburn, who was in training camp with the Buccaneers, and tight end Dae'Quan Wright, who was in training camp with the Browns. Pyburn was claimed on waivers by the Chiefs and now plans to stay in the NFL. Whether Wright will play against Clemson remains to be seen. "I actually got to go watch practice in June with the Browns, so I'm probably going to get turned in for tampering," Swinney joked. "Been watching the preseason games with the Bucs and the Browns and all that."
author: Michael David Smith

title: Texans won't have extension talks with C.J. Stroud during season
summary: The Texans are taking a page from the Steelers' book on contract negotiations.
full_text: The Texans are taking a page from the Steelers' book on contract negotiations . The Steelers have long refused to engage in contract negotiations with players during the regular season and Texans General Manager Nick Caserio said that Houston will take the same approach with quarterback C.J. Stroud this year. Caserio said in July and again on Tuesday that the team has had talks with the 2023 first-round pick about a new deal, but that those talks will be put on hold when the Texans face the Bills in Week 1. "If we don't get it figured out before the season starts, then it'll be something we address in the offseason ," Caserio said, via DJ Bien-Amie of ESPN.com. The Texans have already picked up their option on Stroud's contract for 2027, so the quarterback will remain under contract regardless of how things play out on the field this year. A strong season would make it harder for the Texans to continue playing the waiting game, but anything resembling Stroud's postseason performance from last season would lead to a lot of questions about the future of the quarterback position in Houston.
author: Josh Alper

title: Aaron Donald's absence from Monday's practice "part of the plan all along"
summary: Aaron Donald officially came out of retirement and practiced with the Rams on Sunday, but the three-time defensive player of the year was not on the field with the team on Monday.
full_text: '' Aaron Donald officially came out of retirement and practiced with the Rams on Sunday, but the three-time defensive player of the year was not on the field with the team on Monday. Rams head coach Sean McVay said that Donald's absence had nothing to do with anything that happened during his first practice with the team. McVay said it was "part of the plan all along" for the defensive tackle and that the team will see where that plan takes them as they move toward their Week 1 game against the 49ers in Melbourne. "I wouldn't rule anything out yet," McVay said, via the team's website. "Sometimes when you put unnecessary parameters or guidelines on something, you can skew things. But what I think what's really good for us is if he's able to go, great, if not, that's kind of how we've been operating as is, and guys have done an excellent job of being able to do some really cool stuff in the meantime. So, if he's not ready, and that's not what's best for him and for the team, (we) absolutely wouldn't have him play in Australia." Donald's participation as well as that of defensive end Myles Garrett will continue to be closely monitored as the football world waits to find out when we'll see the duo on the field at the same time.
author: Josh Alper

title: Max Brosmer will stick with Vikings on practice squad
summary: As it turns out, Max Brosmer won't be departing the Vikings.
full_text: As it turns out, Max Brosmer won't be departing the Vikings. While Minnesota waived the quarterback on Monday, Brosmer has cleared waivers and will return to the club on its practice squad, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports. Brosmer entered the league as an undrafted free agent last year after five collegiate seasons with New Hampshire and one with Minnesota. He appeared in seven games with two starts as a rookie, completing 66.2 percent of his passes for 328 yards with no touchdowns and four interceptions. The Vikings still have Carson Wentz and J.J McCarthy behind starting quarterback Kyler Murray on their roster.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Brian Gutekunst: Packers haven't seen the Josh Jacobs video
summary: The misdemeanor battery case against Packers running back Josh Jacobs includes surveillance video from a camera in his garage.
full_text: The misdemeanor battery case against Packers running back Josh Jacobs includes surveillance video from a camera in his garage. The police report strongly suggests that the video includes images of the alleged assault. On Tuesday, Packers G.M. Brian Gutekunst was asked at a press conference whether the team has seen it. " We have not seen the video ," Gutekunst said, via Rob Demovsky of ESPN. "Again, those are legal things going on right now, so we'll let those play out. That's really not for us, but in the appropriate times, if those things become available, we'll figure that stuff out when that time comes." Gutekunst also was asked whether the team needs to see the video before making a decision about Jacobs's future with the team. "Again, we're going to lean on the legal process and let that happen, but we'll take things as they come," Gutekunst said. The situation brings back memories of the weeks preceding the release of the notorious Ray Rice elevator video. The league, as of August 2014, had not seen the video. We argued that it would be easy for the league to get it. It was part of his case file, and Rice ultimately controlled his case file. If the league told Rice he couldn't play until his lawyer made the video available for review, the league would have quickly gotten it. It sparked a somewhat spirited debate by phone with a league official. The conversation ended with this prediction: "If you don't get that video, TMZ eventually will." (By early September, TMZ had gotten it — and then all hell broke loose.) In this case, it would be even easier for the league or the team to inspect the video. It came from Jacobs's house. He owns the footage. Why wouldn't the Packers want to see it? Coach Matt LaFleur recently said regarding Jacobs, "[W]hat he tells me, I believe him and I trust him. I'm going to do that until proven otherwise." One way to be proven otherwise, or to have LaFleur's current belief confirmed, would be to tell him to produce the video.
author: Mike Florio

title: Kyle Van Noy joins the Vikings' practice squad
summary: Kyle Van Noy is staying in purple.
full_text: Kyle Van Noy is staying in purple. The veteran linebacker is signing with the Vikings’ practice squad , via Tom Pelissero of Netflix. The move reunites Van Noy with defensive coordinator Brian Flores. They spent four years together in New England, winning a pair of Super Bowls. In 2020, Van Noy signed with the Dolphins, when Flores was the head coach. The move comes after three years for the 35-year-old Van Noy in Baltimore. A second-round pick of the Lions in 2014, Van Noy has appeared in 173 regular-season games with 115 starts. He has 57.0 career sacks. He brings to Minnesota a thorough knowledge of the Flores system, which will make it easy for him to get up to speed — and to help some of the younger players figure out how to run it the way Flores wants it to be run.
author: Mike Florio

title: Darius Slayton: I didn't pay much attention to rumors I was on roster bubble
summary: Prior to last Sunday's cutdown day, there were rumors about the roster security of a number of players around the league and Giants wide receiver Darius Slayton was on that list.
full_text: ' Prior to last Sunday's cutdown day, there were rumors about the roster security of a number of players around the league and Giants wide receiver Darius Slayton was on that list . It turned out to be smoke rather than fire as Slayton remained with the team through the cut to 53 players and there's no sign that the team is planning to make a move involving the veteran wideout at this point. On Tuesday, Slayton was asked his thoughts regarding the speculation about his future. "Nothing really. It's not the first time, probably won't be the last time," Slayton said, via a transcript from the team. "But I really don't pay it too much of mind, honestly. I just take it day by day. . . . At the end of the day, you control what you can control and let the rest fall where it may." Slayton is heading into his eighth season with the Giants and he was their top receiving target for much of that time. Malik Nabers now occupies that slot and the team will hope he's healthy enough to ensure that Slayton, Odell Beckham Jr. and the rest of the team's wideouts are left to complementary roles in the offense.
author: Josh Alper

title: Chargers will have 10 captains in 2026
summary: With 11 captains on the Rams, the Chargers had a chance to one-up them.
full_text: With 11 captains on the Rams, the Chargers had a chance to one-up them. In a perfect metaphor for the L.A. rivalry, they came up short to their landlords at SoFi Stadium. The Chargers have a mere 10 team captains for 2026 . They are, based on the order they appear on the graphic the Chargers posted: linebacker Daiyan Henley, linebacker Tuli Tuipulotu, tackle Joe Alt, quarterback Justin Herbert, cornerback Elijah Molden, receiver Ladd McConkey, safety Derwin James Jr., linebacker Khalil Mack, tackle Rashawn Slater, and long snapper Josh Harris. Unlike the Rams, which seemed to pick a captain from each position group, the Chargers have two tackles and three linebackers. They have five on defense, four on offense, and one on special teams. It should be three. Offense, defense, special teams. One for each primary component of the team. But each team has to make its own decision. If it wants to dilute the honor by taking a participation-trophy approach to handing out the "C" patches, so be it. Still, the first team that goes with three will receive high praise from this tiny corner of the media ecosystem. Which probably means none will.
author: Mike Florio

title: Reports: Browns plan to sign DE Sam Williams
summary: The Browns are planning to make an addition to their defensive line.
full_text: ' The Browns are planning to make an addition to their defensive line. Per multiple reports, they intend to sign defensive end Sam Williams to their active roster. Williams was released by the Cowboys on Sunday. Williams was a 2022 second-round pick in Dallas and had 8.5 sacks over his first two seasons. A torn ACL kept him off the field in 2024, but he played in every game last season and finished the year with 37 tackles, a sack, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery. The Browns were in contact with Za'Darius Smith before he signed with the Falcons, so they've been looking for more depth at defensive end for a while and it looks like they've settled on Williams as the person to provide it.
author: Josh Alper

title: Browns sign CB Noah Igbinoghene, DE Sam Williams
summary: The Browns announced the signing of defensive end Sam Williams on Tuesday and they also announced the addition of a veteran cornerback.
full_text: The Browns announced the signing of defensive end Sam Williams on Tuesday and they also announced the addition of a veteran cornerback. They have signed Noah Igbinoghene to their 53-man roster. Igbinoghene spent the preseason with the Seahawks, but was released on Sunday. Igbinoghene played in 32 games and made 12 starts for the Commanders over the last two seasons. He had 35 tackles and a sack last year. The Browns placed defensive tackle Kalia Davis on injured reserve and waived cornerback Michael Coats in corresponding moves. They also signed defensive tackle Sam Kamara, running back Jaleel McLaughlin, tight end Messiah Swinson, and defensive tackle Chris Williams to their practice squad.
author: Josh Alper

title: Todd Monken "absolutely not" bothered by fan backlash to Deshaun Watson being named QB1
summary: When Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson played in a preseason game in Cleveland last month, he was heartily booed.
full_text: When Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson played in a preseason game in Cleveland last month, he was heartily booed. It clearly bothered him . When head coach Todd Monken subsequently named Watson QB1 to start the season, fans found more ways to show their displeasure . While Watson didn't play in the Browns' preseason finale last Thursday, he was on the sideline and spent most of his time with a towel over his head — perhaps trying to be as incognito as possible. But does it bother Monken that Cleveland fans clearly have not wholly embraced his choice for starting quarterback? "Absolutely not," Monken said in his Tuesday press conference, via transcript from the team. "Would I prefer that we would all be on the same page? Yeah, but that has nothing to do with my decision, and it can never have anything to do with my decision. "My decision has got to be about what’s best for the Browns in Week 1 and all the way through the season, and as long as I’m the head coach here.” To that end, Monken said he has confidence Watson will be able to push the ball down the field to create explosive plays. “You’re not going to be elite on offense and score points if you can’t create explosives," Monken said. "It’s so hard to drive the football the length of the field without an explosive. You can look at the studies in terms of percentage of scoring a touchdown or getting a field goal with one explosive in a drive. Obviously, that comes after you’ve gotten the first first down. Every coordinator is going to say we’re chasing explosives, and everyone runs with, 'Oh [you're] chasing explosives.' Well, no shit. Everyone’s chasing explosives and trying to not to turn it over. And that’s what you’re trying to do. What’s the defense trying to do? Turn you over and not allow explosives. That’s really the big chess match is that. The ways that you win. "So, obviously having explosive players helps that. Being able to scheme it up against certain looks and then being able to execute because your protection has to hold up when you get those opportunities. I’m confident in Deshaun and our ability to push the ball down the field, otherwise we wouldn’t be starting him.”
author: Myles Simmons

title: Todd Monken hasn't watched much past film from Deshaun Watson
summary: Browns coach Todd Monken had a big decision to make at quarterback.
full_text: Browns coach Todd Monken had a big decision to make at quarterback. In settling on Deshaun Watson over Shedeur Sanders, Monken didn't spend much time looking at Watson's past performances. “I really, to be honest, haven’t looked at it," Monken told reporters regarding whether he studied Watson's film from past seasons. "To be honest, only from afar. When people say, 'You had to look at it,' well, not really. I looked at it from afar when I was down the road, right? In crossover film or something, but I try to take everything at face value. What I see, right? "It doesn’t matter what the player is, I think we owe that to our players, guys that are on the roster. I want to go into it thinking every player we have is elite, and all they have to do is prove me right. That’s all they have to do. That’s what I’m going to go into it — they’re on an NFL roster, I expect them to play well, and I just want them to prove me right. And so I really haven’t really looked at that, different staff, different system. We’ll let it play out. We’ll see where it goes starting a week from now.” Regardless of whether Monken did or didn't watch much Watson film, his performances from his time with the Texans are ancient history. It was six years ago. And while there's some value in looking for plays that he has run well in the past, the more pragmatic approach would be to ignore Watson's play from 2017 through 2020 and focus on things that will work now, with the 30-year-old version of Deshaun Watson.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: George Kittle, Nick Bosa will travel to Australia
summary: The 49ers hope to have both players in the lineup against the Rams.
full_text: 49ers tight end George Kittle's chances of playing in Week 1 are going up. Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that Kittle will travel to Australia with the team ahead of their matchup with the Rams in Melbourne. Kittle has practiced the last two days and, per the report, is trending in the right direction to play. Head coach Kyle Shanahan said earlier this week that he'd prefer not to take Kittle to Australia if it looked like he would not be ready to play on the Achilles he tore in January. Making the trip doesn't guarantee he'll be in the lineup, but it is certainly a good sign. Rapoport reports that defensive end Nick Bosa will also travel with the team on Wednesday. Bosa did not practice for much of training camp as he recovers from a torn ACL, but General Manager John Lynch said on Tuesday that he'll be ramping up his work with an eye toward playing in the opener.
author: Josh Alper

title: Dolphins LB Jordyn Brooks: We have to have "us against the world" mentality
summary: Linebacker Jordyn Brooks is an outlier on the 2026 Dolphins.
full_text: Linebacker Jordyn Brooks is an outlier on the 2026 Dolphins. Brooks is the rare established veteran on a team that is stocked with young players trying to find a foothold in the NFL. That roster construction has made player development the main priority and has led many to predict that the Dolphins will finish at the bottom of the league when all is said and done this season. During a Tuesday press conference, Brooks was asked if he feels that's led the team to take on the mindset of an underdog. “I don’t think we have a choice , honestly," Brooks said. "I don’t think there’s one outlet on social media, anybody that’s got us picked to win anything. Not that it matters, but it’s just what it is. I don’t think any of our opponents respect us. So, 100 percent underdog mindset and I think that’s always the best position to be in. We’re going to carry that mindset into the season, have that ‘us against the world’ mentality and do our best to win football games.” Some veterans would not want to be part of a rebuilding effort, but Brooks signed a three-year extension with the Dolphins in July and he'll be tasked with helping the team become a more imposing opponent before that deal is up.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jon-Eric Sullivan on Quinn Ewers: This is a performance business and it was not getting done
summary: The Dolphins traded Ewers to the Jaguars for a 2028 sixth-round draft pick.
full_text: '' At the end of last season, Quinn Ewers was the Dolphins' starting quarterback. At the end of this preseason, Ewers was traded to the Jaguars for a 2028 sixth-round draft pick. Dolphins General Manager Jon-Eric Sullivan says the decision to move on was based entirely on Ewers' performance in training camp and the preseason. "When I made the decision I was set," Sullivan said. "Wish Quinn the best, and think Quinn has an opportunity to play in this league for a while and do well. I think he needed a fresh start. I think we needed a fresh start. This is a performance-based business and it was not getting done at the level it needed to get done at. Quinn knew that. We had a lot of conversations. I think Quinn, if he was standing here, would tell you that. I think it was time for him to move on, get a fresh start, and us to start fresh with somebody else as well." When Ewers left Texas and entered the 2025 NFL draft, he reportedly turned down an $8 million NIL deal to stay in college for one more year. That looked like a mistake when he fell to the seventh round of the draft and signed a four-year, $4.3 million contract. Now Ewers has already had his first NFL team decide to move on. In Jacksonville, Ewers gets a fresh start, backing up Trevor Lawrence and hoping that if he gets the opportunity to play, he'll show he can get it done.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Saints rookie DB Lorenzo Styles Jr. lands on IR
summary: The Saints placed rookie safety Lorenzo Styles Jr. on injured reserve Tuesday.
full_text: '' The Saints placed rookie safety Lorenzo Styles Jr. on injured reserve Tuesday. The team needed the roster spot after claiming cornerback Decamerion Richardson off waivers. Styles injured his calf in the second preseason game. He will miss at least the first four games before returning. The Saints selected Styles with the 172nd overall pick out of Ohio State. He recorded 30 tackles and two pass breakups in 12 games for the Buckeyes last season, while also returning a kickoff 100 yards for a touchdown.
author: Charean Williams

title: Brian Gutekunst: Talks with Cardinals about Josh Sweat never happened
summary: The offseason consisted of a rumor that the Cardinals would be trading linebacker Josh Sweat to the Packers.
full_text: The offseason consisted of a rumor that the Cardinals would be trading linebacker Josh Sweat to the Packers. On Tuesday, the man in charge of the Green Bay roster denied that it was ever a possibility. "No one from our organization has had a conversation about Josh Sweat from anyone at Arizona," Gutekunst said, via Ryan Wood of USA Today . "That's coming out of thin air, someone is making stuff up , because that never happened." A report emerged in the offseason that the Cardinals were receiving calls about Sweat. And the Packers made sense on the surface; Sweat reunited with former Eagles offensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon after Gannon became the head coach of the Cardinals. With Gannon now the defensive coordinator in Green Bay, it's a logical connection of the dots. And to the extent the Packers had any interest in Sweat, it wouldn't have taken much to kick-start a conversation. The Brothers LaFleur coach the two teams. It would have been easy for Matt to gauge with Mike whether a deal would have been possible. Sweat is entering the second season of a four-year, $76 million deal with the Cardinals. In 17 starts last season, Sweat had 12.0 sacks.
author: Mike Florio

title: Nick Caserio: NFL players going back to college is "ridiculous," but "doesn't really impact our job"
summary: More and more NFL figures are addressing the current chaos in college football.
full_text: More and more NFL figures are addressing the current chaos in college football. And most of them don't like it. Texans G.M. Nick Caserio joined the chorus on Tuesday, with two observations. "First of all, it's ridiculous," Caserio told reporters. "Secondly, it doesn't really impact our job. The whole concept, we could spend an hour having that discussion. It doesn't necessarily materially impact kind of what we're doing specific to training camp and those types of things. If they are in college, if they go back to college, you just evaluate them as if you would through the college lens, through the college process. We didn't have any players that fell under that restraining order so it wasn't really going to affect us. Conceptually it's affected basketball as well. There was a kid that went back to Alabama that was in the G-League. Look, if you’re a professional player then you're a professional player. To go from being a professional player to a college athlete or amateur athlete, the whole thing is kind of ridiculous.” But is it really ridiculous to expect the NCAA to adopt a five-year rule while also denying a fifth year to those who didn't have access to one? Plenty of players who entered the draft would have stayed put if they'd known they'd have another year. All problems in college sports trace to a system that denied compensation to players for as long as possible and the problems the reckoning has created. The players are simply reacting to the circumstances, and attempting to secure fair treatment under the relevant rules. Regardless, the process of sorting out who will and won't be able to play college football this year after spending time on 90-man rosters continues. And the NFL will proceed unaffected by the situation, except for the fact that the players who return to college can't be signed by NFL teams during the 2026 season.
author: Mike Florio

title: John Spytek says Ashton Jeanty is in a "good spot" but offers no timeline on a return
summary: The Raiders running back sprained his ankle in an Aug. 23 practice.
full_text: '' Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty was not seen at Tuesday's practice as he works his way back from a sprained ankle. The Raiders have not offered specifics about Jeanty's injury since he sprained his ankle in an Aug. 23 practice. Head coach Klint Kubiak has said the Raiders are "counting on" Jeanty to play in Week 1. But General Manager John Spytek did not make any promises Tuesday. “I think he's in a good spot," Spytek said, via video from the team. "We see him every day. He's working really hard. He's on the mend, as Klint said. I think that's one of the things we all like and respect about Ashton is just the maturity he has and the spirit that he has, that it's hard to knock him down, and I think he attacks everything with a great mindset. And I don't think that this will be any different for him. I expect him to be back as quick as he can, maybe quicker than some people would expect. When that is, we'll see. But I think he's in a good spot, and I think he'll be ready to go when we get him back out there.” Jeanty, the sixth overall pick in 2025, played all 17 games last season and totaled 975 yards and five touchdowns on 266 carries. The Raiders drafted running back Mike Washington in the fourth round, and he rushed for 168 yards on 23 carries in the preseason.
author: Charean Williams

title: CBS has no comment about Tony Romo's statement
summary: On Tuesday, former Cowboys quarterback and CBS broadcaster Tony Romo issued a statement announcing his no-contest plea to OWI charges and expressing his intention to return to CBS, in time.
full_text: On Tuesday, former Cowboys quarterback and CBS broadcaster Tony Romo issued a statement announcing his no-contest plea to OWI charges and expressing his intention to return to CBS, in time. In response, CBS has nothing to say. And all that that implies. Via John Ourand of Puck , CBS had no comment about the Romo statement. CBS also referred to its prior statement on Romo — a perfunctory, one-line release announcing that he would be placed on leave " until further notice ." As Ourand observes, the fact that Romo's statement wasn't coordinated with CBS speaks to a wedge between the two sides, along with the possibly inevitable legal wrangling over the four years and $72 million left on his contract. And, as Ourand reiterates, "it still appears exceedingly unlikely" that Romo will ever return to CBS. CBS has done nothing to contradict the perception that it's moving on from Romo, after nine years on the network's No. 1 broadcast team. J.J. Watt has been bumped up to the top spot, and by all appearances he'll be given a full and fair chance to retain it beyond 2026.
author: Mike Florio

title: Former NFL assistant coach Kippy Brown dies at 71
summary: Former NFL assistant coach Kippy Brown died this week, Matt Young of the Houston Chronicle reports.
full_text: ' Former NFL assistant coach Kippy Brown died this week , Matt Young of the Houston Chronicle reports. Brown was 71. Brown spent 22 seasons as an NFL assistant, coaching for seven different teams. His final job was the wide receivers coach with the Seahawks on Pete Carroll's staff from 2010-14. The Seahawks' win in Super Bowl XLVIII gave Brown his only Super Bowl ring. Brown was Jimmy Johnson's offensive coordinator for two seasons with the Dolphins and served as the Lions' associate head coach under Rod Marinelli during Detroit's 0-16 season in 2008. He interviewed for the Texans' head coaching job in 2006 after Dom Capers was fired, but Houston hired Gary Kubiak instead. Brown coached Hall of Fame wide receiver Andre Johnson in his four seasons in Houston. In addition to the Dolphins, Seahawks, Lions and Texans, Brown also coached with the Bucs, Jets and Packers. Brown was head coach of the Memphis Maniax in the short-lived XFL in 2001. As a player, Brown became the first Black quarterback to play at Memphis during his time there from 1974-77.
author: Charean Williams

title: Report: Tony Romo's BAC was 0.15 percent, nearly twice the legal limit
summary: When former Cowboys quarterback and CBS broadcaster Tony Romo was arrested for OWI in Wisconsin, he initially indicated an unwillingness to submit to breath testing.
full_text: When former Cowboys quarterback and CBS broadcaster Tony Romo was arrested for OWI in Wisconsin, he initially indicated an unwillingness to submit to breath testing. Apparently, he changed his mind. According to WTMJ in Milwaukee, court records show that Romo's blood-alcohol concentration was measured at 0.15 percent — nearly twice the legal limit of 0.08 percent. The disclosure was made in connection with Romo's no-contest plea to operating while intoxicated. He'll pay $834 in fines, have his driver's license suspended for six months, attend and complete an alcohol assessment program, and install an ignition interlock device on his vehicle for at least one year after his license is reinstated. Earlier today, Romo issued a statement announcing the plea, explaining that he has developed an "over-reliance" on alcohol, and expressing an intention to return to CBS.
author: Mike Florio

title: Giants receivers pick numbers that bring back good memories
summary: Jalin Hyatt's decision, voluntary or otherwise, to surrender No. 13 to Odell Beckham Jr. wasn't the only back-to-the-future move when it comes to Giants receiver numbers.
full_text: ' Jalin Hyatt's decision, voluntary or otherwise, to surrender No. 13 to Odell Beckham Jr. wasn't the only back-to-the-future move when it comes to Giants receiver numbers. Rookie Malachi Fields shed No. 0, which he had worn during the preseason, for No. 88. And that got Giants fans thinking immediately about former Giants receiver Hakeem Nicks. A first-round pick in 2009, Nicks spent five years with the Giants, one with the Colts, and a final season with the Giants. He was a member of the Super Bowl XLVI championship team, catching 10 passes for 109 yards in the victory over the Patriots. But Nicks's number isn't the only one making a comeback. Hyatt picked No. 81 after giving up No. 13. That number was worn by Amani Toomer from 1996 through 2008. He was a member of the Super Bowl XLI-winning team, catching six passes for 84 yards in the victory over the Patriots. Before 2004, receivers typically wore numbers from 80 to 89. In 2004, 10 through 19 were added to the mix. Nowadays, they can also wear single-digit numbers.

title: Panthers place OL Brady Christensen on IR

full_text: ' The Panthers placed offensive lineman Brady Christensen on injured reserve Tuesday, the team announced. Christensen will miss at least the first four games as he works his way back from a hamstring injury. title: Nick Caserio: Tank Dell is close, but certain things we have to see
summary: The wait for wide receiver Tank Dell to return to the Texans lineup will last at least four more games.
full_text: The wait for wide receiver Tank Dell to return to the Texans lineup will last at least four more games. Dell was placed on injured reserve as the team moved to a 53-man roster on Sunday and that gives him more time to work on regaining his form after the knee injury that has kept him out since late in the 2024 season. On Tuesday, Texans General Manager Nick Caserio shared why Dell went on injured reserve after avoiding the physically unable to perform list to open camp. “I’d say he’s close ," Caserio said at a press conference. "He is not quite there, which is why he's in the category that he's in. I think we'll have a better idea with a lot of these guys after four weeks or four games, whatever it is. I'd say he's definitely closer now than he was — let's say in training camp. There's a little bit more work that remains. Overall, he's in pretty good spirits. There are certain things we just have to see. Some of this too, is honestly for him mentally to make sure he has enough confidence so that he can go out there and perform the way he's capable of, the way he knows how to.” The Texans traded for Kayshon Boutte after Jayden Higgins tore his ACL this summer, but the return of a healthy Dell would still be a needed boost to the receiving corps at some point this season. It will be several weeks before we have a better idea of when such a return might be possible.

title: Bucs claim CB Kevin Knowles off waivers
summary: The Buccaneers claimed cornerback Kevin Knowles off waivers on Tuesday, according to the NFL's personnel notice.
full_text: The Buccaneers claimed cornerback Kevin Knowles off waivers on Tuesday, according to the NFL's personnel notice. In a corresponding move, the Bucs waived undrafted free agent linebacker Caden Fordham. Knowles made the Chiefs' initial 53-player roster, but the team needed his roster spot on Monday after claiming two players, including linebacker Jack Pybrun, whom the Bucs waived on Sunday. Knowles, 23, entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent in 2025. He spent his rookie season with the Chiefs and played 13 games, seeing action on 82 defensive snaps and 231 on special teams. He totaled 15 tackles and two passes defensed.
author: Charean Williams

title: Joe Milton clears waivers, becomes a free agent
summary: Joe Milton is a free agent.
full_text: Joe Milton is a free agent. Milton, the quarterback waived by the Cowboys yesterday, cleared waivers today. That makes him free to sign with any team, either on an active roster or a practice squad. He's unlikely to sign to an active roster, because a team that wanted him on the active roster probably would have claimed him on waivers. The Cowboys want Milton on their practice squad , but it's possible that he'll accept an offer from another team. The 26-year-old Milton spent three college seasons at Michigan and three at Tennessee before the Patriots took him in the sixth round of the 2024 NFL draft. After one year in New England, he was traded to Dallas last year. Although he hasn't done much on the field yet, he has size, speed and a strong arm, and there may be more than one team interested in his services.

title: 2026 NFL Rookie of the Year rankings: Why Jeremiyah Love offers OROY value, Rueben Bain Jr. deserves DROY edge
summary: Love and Bain are the favorites, but don't sleep on a shifty Browns receiver and an explosive Cowboys pass rusher
full_text:
The NFL regular season is upon us. Reflecting on the rookie class and the role each player is expected to take on this season, CBS Sports examines the candidates to win Rookie of the Year honors.
It is important not to focus solely on the favorites. Neither Panthers wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan nor Browns linebacker Carson Schwesinger , the reigning Rookies of the Year, was the favorite to win the award prior to last season.
Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook .
Over the past 10 years, five quarterbacks, three wide receivers and two running backs have won Offensive Rookie of the Year. No tight end has ever won the award. A running back has not won since 2018, when Saquon Barkley of the Giants was crowned. The past eight winners were first-round picks.
A pair of former Notre Dame running backs are among the favorites to win the award this season. In a year when the two quarterbacks drafted in the first round may not play the majority of the season and wide receiver production is uncertain without a bona fide No. 1 option, Love should be viewed as the heavy favorite. He dealt with an ankle injury during the preseason but showed a willingness to play through those issues in college and did not miss time.
The only hesitation with Price is that Seattle used a platoon system last season even with a player of Kenneth Walker III's caliber. Will the rookie be able to produce at a level that moves Rookie of the Year voters without being the focal point of the offense?
There have been 13 running backs drafted in the first round over the past 10 years. Of those, 12 played at least 13 games -- Omarion Hampton was the exception -- and averaged 1,181.2 yards and 8.2 touchdowns on 265.4 carries. When Alvin Kamara and Barkley won the award in back-to-back years, they averaged 1,017.5 rushing yards, 773.5 receiving yards and 14 total touchdowns.
Neither Mendoza nor Simpson will start Week 1, and the outlook for either seeing the field during the first half of the season is meager. Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart and Saints quarterback Tyler Shough drew consideration last year despite playing 14 and 11 games, respectively.
Tate was the highest-drafted wide receiver, but his preseason was not all that inspiring, and Wan'Dale Robinson and Calvin Ridley may siphon targets from him. Saints wide receiver Jordyn Tyson is already dealing with soft-tissue injuries that disrupted his collegiate career.
Stribling is interesting because San Francisco has already lost Ricky Pearsall , creating a bigger opportunity for him within the offense.
KC Concepcion touched the ball on five of his 24 preseason snaps. Jerry Jeudy is a bigger name, and Denzel Boston has garnered the most buzz among Browns pass catchers this preseason, but Concepcion profiles as a high-volume target in Todd Monken's system. With Monken as the Ravens offensive coordinator last season, 53.4% of Zay Flowers ' targets were within 10 yards of the line of scrimmage, according to TruMedia.
Two deeper sleepers who are, at the very least, good values are Caleb Douglas (+7500) and Chris Bell (+6000), both with the Dolphins . Someone has to get targets in Miami's offense, and the primary competition right now is Jalen Tolbert and Malik Washington .
What does an Offensive Rookie of the Year season look like for a wide receiver over the past 10 years? McMillan, Garrett Wilson and Ja'Marr Chase averaged 78 receptions for 1,191 yards and eight touchdowns.
Over the past 10 years, six edge rushers, two linebackers and two cornerbacks have been named Defensive Rookie of the Year. A defensive tackle has not won the award since Aaron Donald of the St. Louis Rams in 2014. A safety has not won the award since the turn of the century. Pass rushers are the overwhelming favorites to win the award, and those six players averaged 8.6 sacks as rookies.
Eight of the past 10 winners were first-round picks.
When sorting through the pass rushers, Bain plays on a better team and may get more opportunities to rush the passer than Bailey, who showed more during the preseason.
Downs, Styles and Reese all played at Ohio State. As a safety, it is difficult to build an impressive stat line over the course of a season. Downs could very well be the best at his position and still not get fair consideration for the award. Styles is interesting because his athletic potential is immense. Playing for defensive coordinator Daronte Jones, a disciple of Brian Flores' attacking front, he may have a greater chance to accumulate sacks and create turnovers.
Reese is equally gifted but does not play for a coordinator as fond of using his linebackers to rush the passer. There is also less of a need with Abdul Carter , Kayvon Thibodeaux and Brian Burns already filling that role.
Malachi Lawrence looked good during the preseason and showed multiple ways to get after the quarterback. One factor weighing against him is playing time. The UCF product will share time with Rashan Gary and Donovan Ezeiruaku . If he needs to reach nine sacks to build a case similar to those before him, will he receive enough pass-rush snaps?
Chiefs edge rusher R Mason Thomas (+6500) showed glimpses of his potential throughout the preseason. Defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo is aggressive as well. Thomas is expected to serve in more of an auxiliary role rather than as a three-down starter.
