title: Betting the Broncos in 2026: See how Denver's win total, Super Bowl odds are trending and our best bets
summary: We're breaking down Broncos futures in our 2026 betting preview, featuring odds, trends, schedule and more
full_text:
The 2025 Broncos were about as unassuming a No. 1 seed as you'll find, with many expecting at various points throughout the year that teams like the Chiefs and Ravens would finally shake off the cobwebs and take over the top of the conference, or a team like the Bills would run through the postseason. However, Denver topped Buffalo despite losing starting quarterback Bo Nix early in overtime, and then almost made it to the Super Bowl the following week with backup Jarrett Stidham in a close loss to the Patriots. While the offseason was relatively quiet, the Broncos did make one major move by acquiring receiver Jaylen Waddle to give their offense a boost.
We're taking a look at everything you need to know before making Denver Broncos futures bets below, including odds, trends, 2026 schedule, offseason changes and more before sharing our preseason betting strategy for the team. Odds are via DraftKings.
Fans interested in betting on NFL and Super Bowl futures should check out the latest DraftKings promo code .
The market is treating the 2025 Broncos as somewhat of a fluke, with the 2026 version not only slightly favored to make the playoffs but sitting third in division odds behind the Chiefs and Chargers. Twelve teams have shorter odds than the Broncos to win the Super Bowl despite how close they came to making the title game last year.
The Broncos have massively exceeded win total expectations in each of the last two years. However, those seasons have been mirror images of each other in the AFC, where the Broncos had the third-best point differential in the AFC and the best in their division in 2024 while barely making the playoffs as the No. 7 seed before posting the fifth-best point differential in the conference last year as the No. 1 seed.
If you want to wager on NFL futures, you have to check out the latest FanDuel promo code .
It's no surprise to see the Broncos with the best defense on a per-play basis, and the unit was elite against both the pass and run, finishing first per play against the former and third against the latter. The defense also had the top sack rate and red-zone success rate in the league. While the offense was average, it ranked just 25th in yards per pass play but also had the top sack rate on that side of the ball.
The Broncos lost a few contributors but mostly decided to address those losses internally, starting with offensive coordinator where Davis Webb earns a promotion from passing game coordinator. The one exception was at receiver, where the Broncos traded their first-, third- and fourth-round picks this year for Waddle to give Nix a better set of weapons entering his third year.
Before you wager on NFL or Super Bowl futures, head over to our BetMGM promo code to see a great offer.
While the Broncos have to play a first-place schedule, they get a break with their Kansas City trip set for Week 1 as Patrick Mahomes races to make it back for Week 1 after tearing his ACL in December. The AFC East and NFC West brings several tough opponents mixed with a few games where the Broncos should be clear favorites against the Dolphins and Jets, which they'll play back-to-back in Weeks 13 and 14, as well as the Cardinals. Their non-common opponents also could be much worse with matchups against the Steelers, Jaguars and Panthers on tap.
If you want to tail R.J. White and other SportsLine and CBS experts, check out the latest Caesars Sportsbook promo code .
While the Broncos certainly overperformed a bit last year on their way to the No. 1 seed, this was still a strong team by all measures that has only gotten better heading into 2026 with Waddle joining the offense. It's possible Nix's ankle injury continues to be an issue once the season starts, but I generally have less concern for that type of injury than I do players coming back from ACL and Achilles tears. Plus, the roster around Nix is so strong that I could see a limited Nix or even Stidham having success. The schedule is particularly brutal early, so it may be smarter to wait and bet the Over during the season, potentially after the Broncos play the Seahawks in Week 6.

title: Thoughts & Jots: From the Cardinals’ final cuts to the practice squad to Kedon Slovis
summary: The last two days went pretty quickly for the Arizona Cardinals, their coaching staff, plus the front office. After their final preseason game, the Cardinals’ GM Monti Ossenfort had plenty of decisions to make. But here is the thing: a lot of these decisions had nothing to do with the preseason games. Why? None of […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - JULY 28: Trey McBride #85 of the Arizona Cardinals talks with head coach Mike LaFleur during a team practice ahead of the NFL season at State Farm Stadium on July 28, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The last two days went pretty quickly for the Arizona Cardinals, their coaching staff, plus the front office. After their final preseason game, the Cardinals’ GM Monti Ossenfort had plenty of decisions to make. But here is the thing: a lot of these decisions had nothing to do with the preseason games. Why? None of the Cardinals players faced the starting offensive and defensive units of any of the 31 NFL clubs. How is an evaluation done for any player who dominates against another team’s second team? The answer comes from practice sessions against a first-string offense and defense. RELATED: FINAL 53-MAN ROSTER Here are some things on my mind regarding the last few days. 1 . First, let’s get to the elephant in the room: Seven receivers? It was crazy that so many had a tremendous preseason, namely Simi Fehoko, Jalen Brooks , and the rookie Reggie Virgil . Apparently, the Cardinals coaching staff couldn’t make a decision on which to cut, so they kept them all. One-handed over the shoulder the catch by Reggie Virgil! @azcardinals Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/WPUxSt5TCY — NFL (@NFL) August 14, 2026 To be fair, keeping Devin Duvernay was expected since he is the team’s designated returner in both punts and kickoffs. But most teams that keep a receiver who is also a return man only retain six in this room. Arizona is keeping seven. That means they dumped a guy who they may need in another group. 2 . The act of releasing B.J. Ojulari was not exactly a shock, but yes, it was. After all, the franchise spent a second-round pick on him back in 2023. Every team expects at least four years with every guy they draft in the first four rounds. Mike LaFleur on BJ Ojulari: "I feel for BJ. If you guys saw the work that he put in behind the scenes to try to get back to the level that he knows he's capable of, you'd root for him too. His journey and his story's not over. But that was a rough injury that he went through." — Theo Mackie (@theo_mackie) August 31, 2026 Even though he gave it a gallant effort in this year’s training camp, he just hasn’t been the same athlete since his ACL injury from last year. He showed some flashes in preseason games, but keep in mind that was against the other team’s second-string offense. The crazy part about his release is that the Cardinals need a second pass rusher opposite Josh Sweat . So, it’s not like he wasn’t in a position of need. It was. 3 . What to do with RB James Conner was creative. He was placed on IR with a return designation, which means they are putting off how to keep him, as well as Bam Knight . Conner will miss the first four weeks of the season at a minimum. And then? 4 . Defensive back depth seemed to be an issue in the final days of training camp. As long as the starting group of the big four – Will Johnson, Max Melton, Garrett Williams , and Denzel Burke – remain healthy, and that’s a big “if”, this group will do good things. The NFC West is full of great receivers and even better quarterbacks, so the cornerbacks will need to ball out and stay off any injury list. The #Cardinals are also expected to release cornerback Starling Thomas, sources tell @CBSSports . 26-year old who was a starter for Arizona in 2023 and ‘24. Missed last year due to an injury. https://t.co/t8KtAO3PFW pic.twitter.com/Ki3pQOLikw — Matt Zenitz (@mzenitz) August 30, 2026 But their backups had plenty of issues. While playing second-team defense against their opponent’s second-team defense in preseason, the advantage each game was to the other team. Too many plays out of position, or taking shoulder dips that ended up being fooled on good routes. So, when Sean Murphy-Bunting and Starling Thomas were released, did anyone shout their displeasure? Or perhaps say out loud, “About time.” Thomas had two seasons of starting experience, but last year’s ACL injury sidelined him. Murphy-Bunting restructured his contract to remain with the team, now being featured in the slot. Both needed to show out, and didn’t. As a key backup, Kei’Trel Clark looked better and has great recovery speed. 5 . OG Matt Pryor being cut wasn’t what I expected at all. Not that he has starter written all over him, but he was a good resource in the event of an injury along the offensive line. He can play four positions, so the versatility is there and was going to provide insurance. Did he play well in the preseason with the second-string offense? Not really. He was signed in free agency, and the Philadelphia Eagles fans couldn’t wait to see him go. Pryor does have some weight maintenance issues and can struggle with arm-over specialists while playing guard. And who is listed as the backup right guard behind Isaiah Adams on the depth chart? Well, not a soul. At least Pryor is now on the practice squad and can be recalled at any point. 6 . Ossenfort worked out a trade with the Jacksonville Jaguars for tight end Hunter Long , who is a big dude at 6’-5”, 243 pounds. But don’t expect his size to instantly become a red-zone target. He hasn’t been to date. He is strictly a skinny offensive lineman, meaning a tight end who can block. He has been in the league for five years and has caught just 20 balls for 153 yards. But his blocking stats are ideal for Mike LaFleur’s offense when they are in 12 or 13 personnel. Trey McBride and Elijah Higgins will handle the receptions. When Long comes into a game, it is strictly to move the chains with another good run. No telling when Tip Reiman will return. 7 . Two offensive linemen who benefited during camp were backup center Jon Gaines and backup tackle Josh Fryar . Each player showed they are ready for starting roles, although neither is situated as such. Just yet. Gaines played quite a bit of offensive guard and looked natural there. The few plays he pulled, he attacked just like it was drawn up, taking on the first player he interacted with, regardless of whether it was the man he was supposed to block. A lot of times, guys will zone in on a player when they pull because that is what the diagram said would happen. But guys filter through, and with Gaines, he could improvise. Fryar has shown quite a bit of development. He appeared in 12 games with five starts during his 2025 rookie campaign, filling in effectively late in the year. He is able to handle speedier edge rushers mainly because of his arm length, which has allowed him to get a hand on his defender first. He is a name to watch, although he is the primary backup at RT behind Elijah Wilkinson. Both players have solidified the backup positions along the offensive line. What a huge plus to have quality guys waiting. 8 . The Cardinals kept three quarterbacks on their final list. That was expected. But what hasn’t been expected is that QB Kedon Slovis has not been signed to the practice squad after the team has signed 14. Why? That has just been assumed all during training camp: keep three, stash away one. Did Ossenfort just not make the call, or did he contact his agent, and Slovis wants to keep shopping for a place where he might have a better chance of landing on the main roster? Because right now, as long as the injury bug doesn’t affect the Cardinals’ QB room, Slovis would most likely sit on the PS all year. It became apparent to Slovis when Carson Beck balled out in the Hall of Fame Game. 9 . Okay, look at your Cardinals bingo card and see if you had safety Wydett Williams, Jr. (6’-2”, 200 pounds) on it, because this undrafted rookie out of Ole Miss made the final roster. I had to look up who this cat was. One thing he is? A hitter. Former Ole Miss player Wydett Williams makes the Cardinals! Boom!! https://t.co/cHVesZX4z2 — Everything Ole Miss (@EverythingRebs) August 30, 2026 He had 73 tackles last year and…

title: Ravens Discussion: Which roster cut was the biggest surprise?
summary: The Baltimore Ravens finalized their initial 53-man roster on Sunday following several highly competitive positional battles throughout the summer. The Ravens were faced with some difficult decisions to cut ties with certain players and gauge the short-term and long-term ramifications of which players to keep. As always, this process did not conclude without some controversial […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MD - DECEMBER 21: Corey Bullock #67 of the Baltimore Ravens looks on before the game against the New England Patriots at M&T Bank Stadium on December 21, 2025 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens finalized their initial 53-man roster on Sunday following several highly competitive positional battles throughout the summer. The Ravens were faced with some difficult decisions to cut ties with certain players and gauge the short-term and long-term ramifications of which players to keep. As always, this process did not conclude without some controversial results. Which roster cut decision comes as the biggest surprise? Some of our staff writers give their take below. Be sure to join in on the conversation and share your thoughts as well! The most surprising cut to me was any of the offensive lineman not named Andrew Vorhees. Gerard Litchenhan and Diego Pounds absolutely outplayed him this preseason and Corey Bullock offered more versatility as a center/guard player. It looks like Vorhees starting experience won him the role. I just hope it’s not a move the Ravens come to regret if he’s needed in a game after his performance last year. — Zach Canter I can’t say that any of the cuts particularly surprised me, but I guess I would go with Rayshaun Benny if I had to pick one. The defensive line room was simply too crowded this offseason, and choosing Peebles over Benny was the right decision in my opinion, but it is still unfortunate to see a rookie draft pick be released, especially after a solid preseason showing. Hopefully Benny will make his back to Baltimore’s practice squad, where he can continue to develop and be ready if the Ravens need an extra man on the defensive line at any point this season. — Dustin Cox The most surprising roster cut to me is offensive lineman Corey Bullock. Bullock was thought to be a legitimate candidate to compete for the starting center role this year but was hampered by an injury early in training camp, which set him back in the pecking order. He evidently didn’t do enough in recent joint practices and preseason games to retain his spot on the roster, after emerging as the team’s backup center last year. While he’s not a polished player and the Ravens don’t have draft capital invested in him, I am surprised they parted ways with Bullock instead of Andrew Vorhees. Bullock was performed better than the latter and possesses guard/center versatility that the Ravens usually covet. He was a nice story in 2025 as an undrafted prospect, locally out of Maryland, as well. — Frank Platko

title: Bills news: Brandon Beane feels ‘really good’ about roster
summary: Before Tuesday’s practice session, Bills general manager Brandon Beane met with the media to reflect on Buffalo’s roster going into the 2026 regular season and the decisions that informed who made the 53-man roster. Today’s edition of Buffalo Rumblinks leads off by recapping what Beane and head coach Joe Brady had to say about the […]
full_text: Brandon Beane, general manager of then Buffalo Bills, heads off the field at the end of practice at the Buffalo Bills training camp at St. John Fisher University in Pittsford on July 24, 2025. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Before Tuesday’s practice session, Bills general manager Brandon Beane met with the media to reflect on Buffalo’s roster going into the 2026 regular season and the decisions that informed who made the 53-man roster. Today’s edition of Buffalo Rumblinks leads off by recapping what Beane and head coach Joe Brady had to say about the roster, including why Beane feels “really good about what’s on the 53,” and why Brady is excited to see what Buffalo’s “unique tight end room” can do this year. Check out the assessments below and then let us know your thoughts on whether Buffalo’s roster is better than last year. How the Bills constructed their 53-man roster During his session with reporters, Brandon Beane addressed how he went about constructing Buffalo’s 53-man roster, along with several bigger-picture questions facing the team. When the roster cuts were made, some fans were surprised that Beane opted for three true boundary cornerbacks in Christian Benford, Maxwell Hairston and Davison Igbinosun, though it should be noted Jordan Hancock can also be deployed here. For as much as Beane said the Bills needed to add more talent to their cornerback room this offseason, Beane said he’s happy with the cornerbacks heading into the season. And when it comes to who starts opposite Benford, Brady has already named Hairston as CB2 while Beane expressed confidence in Hairston’s abilities. “We have a lot of confidence in (Hairston),” Beane said. “I think IGB has done a really good job. If we didn’t have confidence in him, we’d just sit him down and throw IGB in. He’s a young player that’s gonna continue to push his way, and Max knows that he’ll have to play at a certain level, or there’s a young man here that’s ready to showcase kind of what he can do.” Another surprise move was Buffalo’s decision to keep four tight ends—Dalton Kincaid, Dawson Knox, Jackson Hawes and Keleki Latu—on the active roster. Brady said the team is looking forward to utilizing “such a unique tight end room that you have the ability to build a lot of different structures and play 10 personnel sets, 20 personnel sets and do a lot of different things with that. So, that’s part of it.” Beane also addressed the inside linebacker position, why the team is happy to welcome back linebacker Shaq Thompson, how Greg Dortch could serve as a useful addition, and more! title: Plays That Defined 2025: Bills at Broncos, Divisional Round
summary: The 2025 Buffalo Bills season has been written, but the book is incomplete. Before we cast our full attention toward the 2026 season, let’s take one last glance back over our shoulder for our annual look at the Plays That Defined the prior campaign. For any newcomers, first and foremost; Welcome! When it comes to […]
full_text: DENVER , CO - JANUARY 17: Ja'quan McMillian (29) of the Denver Broncos rips an interception from Brandin Cooks (18) of the Buffalo Bills during overtime of the Broncos' 33-30 win at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colorado on Saturday, January 17, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images The 2025 Buffalo Bills season has been written, but the book is incomplete. Before we cast our full attention toward the 2026 season, let’s take one last glance back over our shoulder for our annual look at the Plays That Defined the prior campaign. For any newcomers, first and foremost; Welcome! When it comes to the “rules” of this exercise, we’re not voting for our favorite highlight necessarily, but the one that best captures the essence of the game. Put differently, if you had to choose just one play to show someone to explain as much of the contest as possible, which would you choose? Divisional Round: Buffalo Bills at Denver Broncos The Bills had survived a thriller in Jacksonville to earn the right to move on to the Divisional Round. Up next was the Denver Broncos and I’ll be candid right away for this entry into the series. With all due respect to the Broncos and their fans, no one watching this game should come away with the impression that the better team won. Buffalo turned the ball over five times. FIVE! One wasn’t really but it still counted as one. One turnover was a play that will likely haunt Josh Allen for eternity. Of Denver’s seven scoring drives, four of them came off of turnovers. The one that the Bills forced on defense was immediately negated by the offense turning the ball over. Again. Yes, the officiating left a lot to be desired. There’s no way to get around it though, Buffalo had every opportunity to put this game away and squandered like few teams have ever squandered. There will be no highlights to choose from for this game, only despair. AAAAGGGGGGHHH! (Q1; 8:30) Plays That Defined 2025 – Divisional Round – AAAAAAAHHHHHHGGGG pic.twitter.com/klPmyjKOEi — Kuebiko (@Kuebiko_Kami) July 15, 2026 With all the other bull**** from this game, I bet you forgot about this, didn’t you? Well yours truly, aka “The ***hole who spends way too much time on penalties” didn’t forget. This was on the Broncos’ first drive where they put up a field goal. Three-point swing from that little bit of Larry Ogunjobi’s hand going over the line pre-snap. Can anyone tell me again how close the final result was? Whatever the **** you want to call this (Q2; 0:16) Plays That Defined 2025 – Divisional Round – What the **** was this? pic.twitter.com/SkETps3IcH — Kuebiko (@Kuebiko_Kami) July 15, 2026 Let’s jump into the NFL Quarterback simulator (possibly assisted by Trent Edwards*). You have the ball. There’s 16 seconds left in the first half. You’re down by seven. The head coach wants to try one play and hope for a miracle. As you scramble due to the play being busted, you have a choice. Do you end the play and gracefully go into the half knowing you’re only down one score? Or do you recklessly and DELIBERATELY put the ball on the ground knowing the opponent will already be in field goal range if they recover? Easy choice right? I still love you Josh Allen, but once again remind me how close of a game this turned out to be? *Did you remember that Trent Edwards was co-founder of a virtual reality quarterback deal? This is the kind of thing occupying my brain rather than useful knowledge. The “Interception” (OT; 7:55) Plays That Defined 2025 – Divisional Round – The Interception pic.twitter.com/dbO5kNtUVB — Kuebiko (@Kuebiko_Kami) July 15, 2026 This is a catch in field goal range and while I know I’m supposed to be impartial I’m pretty confident this is going to win the whole darn thing this year and I’m not saying it’s the wrong choice but please at least pay attention to the other selections I’ve put out there this year because it was a lot of work and this is a run-on sentence and that’s fine because we all know how this is going to end, don’t we? Pass interference (OT; 6:09) Plays That Defined 2025 – Divisional Round – Pass interference pic.twitter.com/UqcX6LqSC2 — Kuebiko (@Kuebiko_Kami) July 15, 2026 Read my full penalty analysis here , where I also dive into the officiating a bit. The short version is that I don’t love the pass interference on Taron Johnson here and think it should have been offsetting if anything was called. There’s also the matter of Joey Bosa deciding to impact the game by getting a roughing the passer call on the same play so it’s all a convoluted mess. In the end, since they did call the defensive pass interference, yours truly feels they should have called the similar contact by the receiver and put the ball back where it was. That gives the Bills another crack at stopping this drive and we all know I prefer a shot to stop them vs. “flag putting them right in field goal range.” You stopped reading this article when you saw the last play didn’t you? Did you read any of this? You didn’t, did you? I bet you just scrolled down to the poll knowing that “interception” was on the list. Who am I even addressing here? None of you got this far. Maybe Matt B. or Chris felt obligated to read this far and edit to make sure I didn’t go off the rails. Nah. I bet even they tuned out. Anyway, go Bills! Time to start writing some content that isn’t overshadowed by such a downer of a play. Which play best defines the Bills’ crushing defeat?

title: Bills HC Joe Brady discusses Buffalo’s 53-man roster, practice squad for 2026
summary: Buffalo Bills head coach Joe Brady might not admit it this week, but much of One Bills Drive has likely begun preparing for their 2026 NFL regular-season debut in less than two weeks at the Houston Texans. In fact, Brady was certain to tell reporters gathered in the team’s media room that, for now, the […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - AUGUST 22: Head coach Joe Brady of the Buffalo Bills celebrates after a touchdown drive during the second quarter of a preseason game against the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field on August 22, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images Buffalo Bills head coach Joe Brady might not admit it this week, but much of One Bills Drive has likely begun preparing for their 2026 NFL regular-season debut in less than two weeks at the Houston Texans. In fact, Brady was certain to tell reporters gathered in the team’s media room that, for now, the team’s focus remains “Buffalo on Buffalo.”as they acclimate to the current 53-man roster and 17-man practice squad. That makes sense for Brady and Buffalo’s coaches as he said it’s about seeing the team “fly around now that their legs are back from a training camp.” It’s about leveraging important moments before the regular season begins, which come with a potentially more nuanced evaluation period this week where the key goal will be fielding the best starting units for their trip down to Houston. Many of Buffalo’s starting roles are well defined such that even a few good days of in-house work won’t upset the apple cart. In a perfect world, one might expect the Bills’ active roster to remain fairly or entirely consistent game to game. After all, these players have been hand-chosen by the coaches and those in premiere positions among the front office. Yet there are a handful of places where surprise efforts could capture the attention of those watching closely any given week. For example, when asked about the position of fullback, Brady revealed that despite the talent and work from that room this summer, roster decisions came down to building the best unit in terms of talent. That meant keeping four tight ends from a unique room on the active roster instead of a single fullback. But don’t let the team’s initial 53 catch you sleeping. Brady covets versatility and he understands the opportunity afforded to NFL clubs via the practice squad. Brady likes to say that iron sharpens iron, and it appears he’s looking to lean on that mantra within every corner of Buffalo’s roster. Look no further than a player like Frank Gore Jr. A player like Gore has seemingly done everything possible to crack the active roster, but he’s failed to do so simply due to the players ahead of him on the depth chart. There are many who claim running back to be among the most replaceable positions on a football field. That’s only true to an extent, especially when someone’s trying to leapfrog running back James Cook III, or even well-tenured and proven backs like Ty Johnson and Ray Davis. It doesn’t mean that Brady sees no path to playing for Gore and others on the practice squad. The unit’s term itself is perhaps a bit of a misnomer these days, simply due to the readiness asked of all 17 guys on that portion of the roster. That likely makes for really motivated guys who are hungry for their time to shine, and upset their stuck so far down the depth chart. Brady stated that he wants “a bunch of guys that don’t want to be on the practice squad,” instead preferring it if players get “pissed” when they’re denied a spot on the 53. That comes down to the requisite “personality and edge” as Brady shared. Yet Brady knows the mountain ahead of Gore, even though he managed to suit up for his first game during the Wild Card playoff game against the Jacksonville Jaguars last season. Gore (as well others on the current practice squad) appears more than capable at this point, and Brady revealed something interesting by saying: “(F)or all of these guys, they have to be ready. With these new rules, you know we get two call-ups every week. You know, there’s that potential (for a PS player to be elevated to the active 53.) And so just because a guy’s not on your 53 right now doesn’t mean he’s not going to be playing for you Week 1. And are these guys going to be ready when their opportunity gets called on. Right?” Brady then dove a bit deeper into his mindset when talking with players, saying of his conversations that it’s not necessarily delineated such that: “(Y)ou’re 53 and you’re practice squad, and you’re treated differently. Like, you know when we go into it and we’re talking about the depth chart and the roster each week, there’s going to be guys on our practice squad that are, you know, above guys on the active roster.” It’s unlikely this is a unique mindset, nor something entirely new to the NFL or even the Bills. It is, however, a slightly better peek inside the inner-workings of the team’s roster management. Though Brady is a familiar name and face in Buffalo now, it’s important to remember that this is a new regime. It may be wise to keep focused on the Bills’ practice squad this season.

title: 4 takeaways from Brandon Beane’s 9/01 Buffalo Bills media session
summary: Less than two weeks out from the Buffalo Bills’ Week 1 road game against the Houston Texans, president of football operations/general manager Brandon Beane took the podium on Tuesday, September 1 to answer a wide variety of questions in a presser that lasted over 36 minutes. Widely viewed as a straight shooter with the media, […]
full_text: ROCHESTER, NEW YORK - JULY 29: General manager Brandon Beane of the Buffalo Bills addresses the media following practice during training camp at St. John Fisher University on July 29, 2026 in Rochester, New York. (Photo by Joe Hrycych/Getty Images) | Getty Images Less than two weeks out from the Buffalo Bills’ Week 1 road game against the Houston Texans, president of football operations/general manager Brandon Beane took the podium on Tuesday, September 1 to answer a wide variety of questions in a presser that lasted over 36 minutes. Widely viewed as a straight shooter with the media, Beane dove into reporters’ queries with meaningful intent. What stood about about Beane’s latest comments on Buffalo’s roster? Here are a few key points to consider… NFL practice squad rules have changed for the better Beane was asked about navigating the practice squad and how things have changed in recent years. Interestingly, he pointed to COVID-19 as providing a boost toward a better practice squad situation. Where prior to the pandemic NFL practice squads were a paltry eight players deep, now that number has increased twofold to 16. Additionally, teams are allowed to call up two practice squad players ahead of each week’s game, which stands as a carryover from a then-necessary COVID reality. On trading Sedrick Van Pran-Granger to the Colts Beane had high praise for Sedrick Van Pran-Granger, who the team traded to the Indianapolis Colts during final roster cutdowns this past weekend. While noting that SVP-G dealt with an unfortunate injury sidelining him at the outset last season, Beane complimented his play in the team’s Week 18 finale against the New York Jets. Ultimately, Beane understood that it was a narrow path for SVP-G to play for the Bills on game day due to the overall makeup of the room. Beane felt it was unfair to SVP-G to languish on Buffalo’s roster as a weekly inactive, and, and decided it was best to give the former 2024 fifth-round pick a better shot at realizing his dream with a new opportunity on a different roster. What’s really going on with RB Ty Johnson? There’s no official injury report until early next week, but we’ve known for a bit now that running back Ty Johnson has dealt with a lower-body injury since the end of training camp. Given the roster moves, one might be led to believe that Johnson is healthy and ready to go for Week 1. Otherwise, it was reasonable to imagine a scenario where Johnson was sent to short-term Injured Reserve thus creating a more meaningful spot for running back Ian Wheeler. Of course, none of that happened. So is Johnson really healthy and ready to go, with the team simply taking utmost precaution in managing his health? I witnessed the play Johnson was injured on first-hand and directly, in fact sitting directly in front of the specific action during the annual “Return of the Blue & Red” practice (with photos showing the injury). Johnson was injured when reaching out for a pass, getting his foot caught up in the field/sod. It didn’t seem like a major injury at the time to me, but I’m as far from a medical professional as it gets — I haven’t even played on on TV. I’d like to believe that Johnson is fully ready to go, but I won’t deny that Beane’s latest comments gave me pause. When asked about the situation, Beane stated that the latest injury was “a bit different’ than the prior one. He said Johnson’s getting better, which, to me, implies he’s not quite ready. Beane also discussed how roster decisions for Week 1 will come into play when the time is right. The team has 12 days to get things right on this topic, which could mean giving running back Frank Gore Jr. a game-day check for Week 1. The Bills had been after Greg Dortch for a bit When asked about newly signed wide receiver Greg Dortch, Beane mentioned that he was a player on the team’s radar going back to last offseason during free agency. Ultimately, Dortch signed on with the Detroit Lions in 2025 — but Detroit released him this past weekend. Beane said that the numbers were similar between the Lions and Bills offers last season, but that they were thrilled to get another chance at bringing him into the fold at wide receiver. Now, Dortch could also get a massive look at winning the team’s punt return role. Dortch has a connection to current Bills special teams coach Jeff Rodgers, which undoubtedly played a key role in his arrival to Western New York. What else caught your attention during Brandon Beane’s latest media session? Dive into Beane’s full press conference in the video embedded below, and sound off in the comments section!

title: Braden Smith’s injury a big one for Texans before Buffalo Bills game in Week 1
summary: The Buffalo Bills will not be facing Houston Texans starting right tackle in Week 1, a development I don’t think can be understated in its importance. Although Braden Smith initially was placed on the Texans’ 53-man roster after cutdown down, GM Nick Caserio told reporters on Tuesday Smith will now be placed on IR after […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - JUNE 02: Braden Smith #71 of the Houston Texans arrives during OTA Offseason Workouts at Houston Methodist Training Center on June 02, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills will not be facing Houston Texans starting right tackle in Week 1, a development I don’t think can be understated in its importance. Although Braden Smith initially was placed on the Texans’ 53-man roster after cutdown down, GM Nick Caserio told reporters on Tuesday Smith will now be placed on IR after suffering an injury during a late-August joint practice, meaning he’ll miss (at least) the first four games of Houston’s 2026 regular season: Caserio: RT Braden Smith to be placed on IR; will miss 4-6 weeks. — Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) September 1, 2026 For the second-consecutive offseason, the Texans set out to rebuild the offensive line to protect C.J. Stroud and boost run-game efficiency. It’s felt like Houston’s main objective during the entire Stroud era. Agreeing to terms with free-agent right tackle Braden Smith was the first of two major blocking acquisition — the other being spending a first-round pick on guard Keylan Rutledge. During the 2025 regular season, Stroud was pressured on 36.4% of his drop backs, incidentally, the exact same percentage as Josh Allen. It ranked as the 22nd-highest figure out of 44 qualifying quarterbacks, per Pro Football Focus. Stroud’s 13.4% pressure-to-sack rate was the 10th-lowest in the NFL. Overall, Stroud went from a 8.9% sack rate in 2024 to a very respectable 5.1% last season. Houston’s first blocking reconstruction mostly worked. But veteran do-everything blocker Tytus Howard, who played some right tackle in 2025, signed with the Browns in free agency, and second-year pro Blake Fisher was a liability regardless of which edge of the pocket he protected. Veteran mountain of a man Trent Brown remained but Houston deemed it necessary to add a super-sturdy right tackle who’d serve as a longer-term upgrade at the position. Which is why Smith was signed on the first day of free agency to a two-year, $25 million deal. Smith, an unassuming yet ferocious blue-collar blocker, surrendered more than 40 pressures just once in his first eight seasons in Indianapolis and averaged playing 840 snaps each regular season. While protecting Stroud is priority No. 1, it’s safe to assume Smith’s run-blocking prowess can explain why Houston immediately targeting him in free agency. During his Colts career, Smith established himself as one of the premier run-blocking right tackles in football. And writing the Texans struggled mightily on the ground would be kind. They finished 30th in rush EPA per play and 32nd in Success Rate . Rookie Woody Marks led the team with 703 yards on the ground at just 3.6 yards per tote. While Houston made other transactions this offseason with run-game bolstering in mind — like signing David Montgomery — Smith (and Rutledge, a run-blocking specialist at Georgia Tech) was the investment with the most expected positive impact on that phase of the game for the Texans offense. And, of course, we’re fully aware of Buffalo’s shoddy run defense in 2025 — last in rush EPA per play and 28th in Success Rate . While an injury to a right tackle isn’t incredibly newsworthy in most cases — and Brown is a somewhat serviceable replacement — the Smith-to-IR news is clearly good for both the Bills pass-rushing and run-stopping efforts for the first game of the 2026 season.

Last year, Allen was listed at No. 3 on this very list. title: Bills eschew orthodox positional roster quotas with 53-man decisions
summary: Everyone tells you what they believe in, but actions speak louder than words. In 2012, a film called “Would You Rather” released in select theaters. An independent psychological horror film, the movie focuses on a dinner party conducted by a wealthy “philanthropist” Shepard Lambrick who organizes a set of games to test how far his […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - AUGUST 27: Keleki Latu #83 of the Buffalo Bills against the Pittsburgh Steelers during a pre-season game at Highmark Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images Everyone tells you what they believe in, but actions speak louder than words. In 2012, a film called “Would You Rather” released in select theaters. An independent psychological horror film, the movie focuses on a dinner party conducted by a wealthy “philanthropist” Shepard Lambrick who organizes a set of games to test how far his financially-strapped guests would be willing to go to obtain the money they so desperately need. In one notable scene, Lambrick tests the convictions of vegetarian character Iris (played by Brittany Snow) by offering her $5,000 to eat a steak and foie gras. When Iris (who attended the party to try to acquire money to help her ill brother) declines on principle, Lambrick ups the ante to $10,000. Iris caves, taking the money and eating the meat. Overall, I felt the strong premise of the film was damaged by the leaning towards gore and inconsistent character logic. However, it does do an excellent job of outlining the idea that people’s principles are far more fluid and situational than they will vocally acknowledge. The Buffalo Bills have their initial 53-man roster and practice squad set. General Manager/VP of Football Operations Brandon Beane and Head Coach Joe Brady have spent a lot of time discussing their vision for the team since their promotions were announce early this year. Ultimately, none of that matters. What they actually did says far more about their principles than whatever they said. And principle spoke loudest above all when the dust settled: the Bills picked organizationally perceived talent over traditionally perceived roster quotas. Armaj Reed-Adams. Kani Walker/Toriano Pride Jr. Ben VanSumeren. Mike Danna. In all three of these circumstances, players who the regime felt were roster-worthy players pushed the organization towards making a decision that pushed rigid positional numbers to the back burner. Offensive Line Reed-Adams played well in the preseason as a seventh-round pick, but as the likely 10th offensive lineman and a guard-only backup, traditional thinking would have meant he was destined for waivers and a practice squad spot. But the Bills decided to go heavy on the offensive line to keep him on the active roster and not expose him to other teams (an unorthodox stance for a player taken in the last 15 picks of the draft). Given the Bills have two players on expiring contracts that just finished a battle for the starting left guard position in Alec Anderson and Austin Corbett, having a cost-controlled player who’s been in the building developing as a potential option for a starting guard position in 2027 may be on the team’s mind as they elect to carry Reed-Adams. Cornerback Kani Walker and Toriano Pride Jr. were neck-and-neck when I most recently evaluated the positional battle. Where I (and others) got it wrong is in the assumption that there must be an outside CB4 from the two of them. Many, including myself, expected that for all actual logistical purposes, Dee Alford was your CB4. There was little change of having a situation come up on the field where Dee Alford would be in the nickel defender spot, Walker/Pride Jr. would be at outside corner, and second-year offseason star Jordan Hancock would be on the bench. In actuality, Alford would take on the outside corner spot if necessary and Hancock (who may be the team’s preferred dime defender) would slide in to play the nickel. But surely after all that talk from Beane about cornerback depth being a concern post-draft (as reasoning for the surprise second-round selection of Davison Igbinosun out of Ohio State), they wouldn’t have just five corners, right? They would, because talk is cheap, and they didn’t feel like Walker or Pride Jr. were rosterable NFL players at this time. Fullback Joe Brady said he wasn’t going to keep a fullback just to keep a fullback. He apparently meant it. The team released undrafted rookie Jackson Acker a few weeks ago, leading the roster down the path of “if they keep one, I guess VanSumeren.” They didn’t keep one, despite the Bills highly-ranked rushing attack featuring the league’s rushing yards leader employing a fullback in 2025. Despite the Sean Payton offenses historically (of which Joe Brady calls himself of “protege”) using the position. Despite the league-wide trend towards heavier personnel having the position (along with second and third tight ends) get a larger snap share than it did in the 2010s. The Bills didn’t think VanSumeren was a roster-worthy player, so they didn’t roster him (he has since signed to the Chiefs practice squad, so they didn’t secure him there either); positional checkmarks be damned. The Bills elected to keep fourth tight end Keleki Latu (inarguably more effective player than VanSumeran as exhibited throughout both of their respective careers) and already had a very strong tight end room in the 1-3 spots on the depth chart in another move toward maximizing the perceived talent on the roster. Edge Rusher The Bills elected to keep six edge rushers, including May signee Mike Danna. For comparison, Bills defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard’s former team (the Denver Broncos) currently has four edge rushers on their active roster. The Baltimore Ravens have five, the New England Patriots have four, The Los Angeles Rams have five, and the Green Bay Packers have four (not counting All-Pro Micah Parsons, currently on the Physically Unable to Perform list). Danna performed well this preseason after coming aboard later in the spring and has been a paid starter for a high-level defense in Kansas City previously, but the numbers weren’t in his favor as the team was always likely to keep Gregory Rousseau, 2026 free agent signee Bradley Chubb, 2nd round pick T.J. Parker, and Michael Hoecht coming off an Achilles injury but trending towards active roster status. Those four may have been where teams may have stopped, but Javon Solomon plays special teams and is a better fit in this defense than the previous one under former head coach Sean McDermott, so he had a chance if they kept five. Danna, like Reed-Adams and Latu already mentioned, appeared to be the victim of the numbers game. But the Bills decided the best way to win the game was to not play in 2026. Danna proved to be a roster-worthy player, so he made the roster. What seems so simple to many is actually a slap in the face on more traditional roster construction philosophies. This isn’t some magical or unique thing that Brady and Beane are doing, but it happened in multiple circumstances across the roster and creates a theme worth mentioning here. Time will tell if Beane and Brady made the right calls in each of these situations. That’s why I specifically used the word “perceived” in the premise of this article. The organization thinks they picked player talent over traditional position allocations. Does it work? No idea. Does it even stand or do the Bills make a set of roster moves in the next week that completely blow this entire premise to smithereens? No clue. But it’s something to put in the back of our minds as we have to partially reset our opinions of this partially new Bills regime. …and that’s the way the cookie crumbles. I’m Bruce Nolan with Buffalo Rumblings. You can find me on Twitter and Instagram @BruceExclusive and look for new episodes of “The Bruce Exclusive” every Thursday on the Rumblings Cast Network — see more in my LinkTree!

summary: With the benefit of an extra game thanks to the Hall of Fame game, the Carolina Panthers had the second best record in the NFC at 3-1. They were second only to the 3-0 Los Angeles Rams. While most folks discount preseason records as largely meaningless, most folks are also already crowning the Rams as […]
full_text: CANTON, OHIO - AUGUST 06: Head coach Dave Canales of the Carolina Panthers looks on during the first quarter of the 2026 Pro Football Hall of Fame Game against the Arizona Cardinals at Tom Benson Hall Of Fame Stadium on August 06, 2026 in Canton, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images With the benefit of an extra game thanks to the Hall of Fame game, the Carolina Panthers had the second best record in the NFC at 3-1. They were second only to the 3-0 Los Angeles Rams. While most folks discount preseason records as largely meaningless, most folks are also already crowning the Rams as Super Bowl Champions. I see no reason why we can’t go ahead and pencil the Panthers in as the #2 seed in the NFC for the 2026 playoffs. Right? All joking aside, this was the strongest performance the Panthers have had in a preseason since their ill-fated 2018 season. That shows how much the roster has recently recovered after years of mismanagement by former head coach and general manager combos. The Carolina Panthers may actually employ NFL-level talent. Huzzah. That’s all well and good, but it doesn’t necessarily change the fact that the Panthers have been notorious for slow starts to their seasons under the leadership of head coach Dave Canales and quarterback Bryce Young. Who is responsible and why that has happened at all is a complicated question without a simple answer. A deep roster, while hugely important, does not mean that the starters are going to be ready for Week 1. The limited action we saw from those starters in this preseason did not inspire a lot of confidence that 2026 was going to be a brand new year for the Panthers. A mixed bag is about par for the course for us. Which brings us to this week’s Reacts survey question. title: 2026 Season Opener Countdown: 11 Days Remaining
summary: Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to […]
full_text: Carolina Panthers defensive tackle Kris Jenkins (77) smiles as he heads to the team's bench following his sack of Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Ben Roethlisberger in the first quarter of NFL preseason football at the Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte, North Carolina, Thursday, August 30, 2007. (Photo by Jeff Siner/Charlotte Observer/Tribune News Service via Getty Images) Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to change that up a bit by counting down our own list of the Top 100 Panthers of all time. This does not correspond to jersey number, does not need to be somebody who wore a jersey, and will in no way be controversial. #11. Kris Jenkins We’re in the middle of the golden age of Carolina Panthers history in this countdown right now. The list is rife with players from the early to mid 2000s when the Panthers had a feared defense and were one of the least desirable teams to play in the NFL. We continue that trend with today’s topic of the countdown, the anchor of that defense, Kris Jenkins. The Panthers selected Jenkins in the second round of the 2001 NFL Draft while the team was in a hot streak of adding elite talent. He quickly solidified himself as a starter as a rookie, and built upon that in the subsequent seasons. In his second year, Jenkins racked up seven sacks and 15 tackles for a loss, earning Pro Bowl and All Pro honors. He followed that up with an almost identical season en route to his second Pro Bowl and All Pro nominations. He had two seasons derailed by injuries but was able to come back and contribute two more solid seasons in Carolina before he was traded to the Jets. He had one last dominant season in New York before ACL tears ended each of the next two years, and ultimately his career. Jenkins clocked in at 6’5”, 320 pounds at the combine, but he was often listed closer to 350 pounds during his career. He was a behemoth of a man that was practically immovable at the line of scrimmage. His sheer size allowed him to clog up space, and his length and strength further extended the range of his impact. He was able to generate decent pressure by nose tackle standards purely with his strength and ability to push the line. He used those physical attributes and motor to also pull off one of the most impressive special teams feats in league history. He blocked two field goals in one game against the Buccaneers. One of them was an extra point that would’ve won the game for Tampa. Instead, the Panthers ended up winning the game in overtime. Jenkins’ career probably didn’t reach the heights it could have due to injury. He tore his ACL three times during his time in the NFL, and the last two ultimately ended his career. His peak years were about as dominant as they come for an interior defensive lineman, and he was an essential part of the Panthers’ Super Bowl run in 2003. For that, he lands at number 11 on the list of top 100 Panthers of all time.

summary: Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA - JANUARY 18: Wide receiver Muhsin Muhammad #87 of the Carolina Panthers quiets the Philadelphia Eagles fans after catching a touchdown pass in the second quarter during the NFC Championship game on January 18, 2004 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Brian Bahr/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to change that up a bit by counting down our own list of the Top 100 Panthers of all time. This does not correspond to jersey number, does not need to be somebody who wore a jersey, and will in no way be controversial. #12. Muhsin Muhammad The Carolina Panthers took Muhammad in the second round of the 1996 NFL Draft. The big-bodied receiver out of Michigan State only played nine games his rookie year due to a lingering hamstring issue, but brought in over 400 yards receiving and one touchdown. The run-first offense in 1996 combined with the heavy reliance on Wesley Walls and Mark Carrier made it tough for Moose to break out. It wasn’t until the 1998 season, his third in the league, that he finally started to blossom. He started all 16 games for the Panthers, bringing in 68 catches for 941 yards and six touchdowns. The following season was Muhammad’s first Pro Bowl selection, which was well earned. He hauled in 96 passes for 1,253 yards and eight touchdowns, leading the team in the former two categories and finishing third in the latter. Muhammad eclipsed the 100 catch mark for the first and only time in his career during the 2000 season, finishing with just under 1,200 yards and six scores. He ended up leading the entire NFL in catches that year with 102. The 2001 season was disappointing for the entire franchise, and Muhammad was no different. He missed five games due to injuries, yet still finished second in catches and yards, which really hammers home just how bad the offense was in 2001. The 2001 Draft changed the Panthers franchise forever in many ways, including giving Muhammad a true running mate on the outside. Steve Smith Sr came into the league as mainly a returner, but by 2002 the Panthers had their dynamic duo at wide receiver. Smith and Muhammad shared similar target shares and success those two seasons. The 2003 season was a magical one for Muhammad and the Panthers, making a surprising run to the Super Bowl. Muhammad still owns the record for the longest receiving touchdown in Super Bowl history, and 85-yard bomb from Jake Delhomme. 2004 was Muhammad’s best individual season, which was good timing for him since he was in a contract year. An injury to Steve Smith left Muhammad as the main viable receiving threat, and he absolutely thrived. He caught 93 passes for a career high 1,405 yards and a still Panthers record 16 receiving touchdowns. He cashed in that offseason, signing a six-year, $30 million contract with the Chicago Bears. That may sound paltry by today’s standards, but in 2005 it was the equivalent of getting about $15 million per year in today’s cap. He never came close to living up to his contract, however, scoring fewer touchdowns in three seasons with the Bears than he did in just the 2004 season in Carolina. He returned to the Panthers in 2008 after the Bears released him, and he bounced back a bit, falling just short of the 1,000 yard receiving mark. He retired following the 2009 season. Muhammad has been around the team since, occasionally dropping in for color commentary on local broadcasts. He was inducted into the Panthers Hall of Honor in 2023 along with Hall of Famer Julius Peppers. To this point, Moose is the second best receiver in Panthers history, literally. He ranks second in franchise history in all major receiving categories: catches, yards, touchdowns, 100-yard games. His constant appearance in the record books and high performance on the biggest stage lands him at No. 12 on our countdown.
author: Daniel Belton

title: Zavion Thomas is already beating the Velus Jones allegations for Bears
summary: Chicago Bears third-round pick Zavion Thomas did something significant in my mind in Saturday’s preseason win over the Tennessee Titans. I mean, aside from leaving a poor defensive back’s ankles at the 15-yard line and walking away from an angle down the sideline for a 97-yard touchdown in his preseason debut. Or from putting up […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - AUGUST 29: Zavion Thomas #81 of the Chicago Bears carries the ball during a preseason game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on August 29, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images) | Getty Images Chicago Bears third-round pick Zavion Thomas did something significant in my mind in Saturday’s preseason win over the Tennessee Titans. I mean, aside from leaving a poor defensive back’s ankles at the 15-yard line and walking away from an angle down the sideline for a 97-yard touchdown in his preseason debut. Or from putting up 201 total yards on the day, including a couple solid routes and catches down the field. Thomas proved a lot of people wrong in the most basic of senses about one really silly comparison made by some fans and pundits after he was drafted 89th overall in the 2026 NFL Draft: He’s not another Velus Jones Jr. Bears rookie Zavion Thomas put his 4.28 speed on full display today⚡️🔥 5 REC, 140 YDS, 1 TD, 1 PR, 39 YDS, 1 KR, 22 YDS That’s 201 all-purpose yards for the 3rd round pick. pic.twitter.com/WIouHnP2OU — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) August 30, 2026 Now, it’s somewhat understandable on paper why one would be concerned after having watched Jones, another third-round receiver with meager college production drafted by general manager Ryan Poles, flounder in Chicago. About the only thing Jones could do on a football field was run fast in a straight line with the ball in his hands. Getting open, catching the ball—whether you were talking passes or punts—or finding running lines? Not so much. Eventually, Chicago was forced to cut the first offensive draftee of the Poles era last year, only to redux that decision (in peoples’ minds) with the Thomas selection. Except that comparison is terrible when you actually watch the two of them play football, which is the actually important part of evaluating a football player. (Weird, I know.) Have you ever seen Jones run a route—even something as simple as a stop-and-go—with anything resembling the precision of what Thomas did on that touchdown? Or seen Jones make a chain-moving grab away against tight coverage on an out route down the field like Thomas did on one of his four other catches from that game? Or seen Jones cleanly catch a punt?! (Okay, too much.) Now, to be fair, the bar for clearing Jones as a football player is on the level of that loose board sticking up from your floor that you always trip over. The difference matters materially because of the baseline skills Thomas already has in addition to 4.28 speed as well as who’s weaponizing him. "He gone be a problem" 😏 pic.twitter.com/YolAk4IrLO — Chicago Bears (@ChicagoBears) August 31, 2026 One big game in the preseason doesn’t guarantee any kind of success for Thomas once the games start for real. He’s probably not going to be a significant contributor on offense just yet, though we should expect a handful of snaps here and there. But what it does tell us is that Thomas has the raw materials to be useful immediately, even if just in a limited role. You can trust him to run decent routes and potentially make a catch or two. You can plan to get him the ball in space, whether on a screen or handoff, and actually envision a big play happening. You might even be able to put him back to return kicks and punts without fear that the ball will inevitably end up in the other team’s hands. Jones failed as a receiver/playmaking prospect in Chicago not because he lacked athletic ability but because he couldn’t execute—something that was a concern for the entirety of his six-year college career. Thomas, meanwhile, might have just been a player who needed a bit of coaching and a more intentional role to take off. Because from where I’m sitting, Thomas should never have been mentioned in the same breath as Jones as a prospect, whatever his numbers said. Hopefully, he and Ben Johnson make sure that comparison is dead by the time Thomas’ first year is over with. . @StaceyDales on speedy Bears rookie receiver Zavion Thomas: "Ben (Johnson) has a toy to play with. He's got like a motorcycle in the garage." pic.twitter.com/EYK33JUZrm — 104.3 The Score (@thescorechicago) August 31, 2026

title: Bengals film room: Defensive rookies shine vs. Eagles
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals finished off a perfect preseason, going 3-0 this year with a win over the Philadelphia Eagles 30-13 on Friday night. Let’s take a look at a couple of rookie standouts from the game that made the Bengals’ 53-man roster. Tacario Davis Davis has really emerged over the past couple of weeks. He […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OH - AUGUST 22: Cincinnati Bengals defensive tackle Landon Robinson (96) walks off the field at the end of the preseason game between the Chicago Bears and the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Cincinnati, OH. (Photo by Ian Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Cincinnati Bengals finished off a perfect preseason, going 3-0 this year with a win over the Philadelphia Eagles 30-13 on Friday night. Let’s take a look at a couple of rookie standouts from the game that made the Bengals’ 53-man roster. Tacario Davis Davis has really emerged over the past couple of weeks. He is stacking quality performances both in-game and during camp practices. DJ Ivey was once thought to be the first man up outside of the starters at outside corner, but Davis has made a strong case for that to be him. Davis has shown physicality and reliability as a tackler, has tremendous length and straight-line speed, and came up with his first interception on a pass that was intended for Philadelphia first round draft selection Makai Lemon. I would be lying if I wasn’t a bit skeptical of the Davis selection at the time it was made. It felt a round too early based on his recent injury history, and concerns about his change-of-direction ability to mirror faster receivers. While the latter is still a bit of a concern for me, I will gladly eat crow so far with how well Davis has performed. With both DJ Turner and Dax Hill entering contract years, Davis could be a full-time starter next year. LOVE the physicality of Tacario Davis pic.twitter.com/RnjYFRkc6D — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) August 29, 2026 A really impressive last two preseason games for Tacario Davis. The Bengals scouts and front office deserve a lot of credit for what looks like one of the best drafts in franchise history early on. Time will tell on that though. https://t.co/rCQFztZX1e pic.twitter.com/bhA8DOWvOm — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) August 30, 2026 Landon Robinson Robinson officially made the Bengals’ initial 53-man roster on Sunday. The Navy product finished the preseason with 10 pressures and 4 sacks, according to PFF. Both numbers were tops in the NFL during the preseason. He consistently flashes with quickness off the snap, a non-stop motor, and a guy who has massive power in his lower and upper body. Robinson might not have had the same flashy performance as the first two games, but he held up well overall throughout the night. He fully earned his spot on this 53-man roster, and now it just becomes a question of whether the Bengals will have him active on the 46-man roster against the Buccaneers. His ability to come in on goal-line as a fullback could help make that a reality. However, if he is inactive early on, he still will end up playing meaningful snaps for this team at some point this year. Landon Robinson played pretty well again last night. Maybe it wasn’t as flashy as the first two preseason games, but this guy has done everything he could to make the 53-man roster this year. pic.twitter.com/rEmeiGGeUE — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) August 29, 2026
author: Dale Altman

title: Bengals film room: Offensive rookies vs. Eagles
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals defeated the Philadelphia Eagles 30-13 in their third and final preseason game of the year. Now, we’re taking a look at how the offensive rookies performed in Philly. Connor Lew Lew was the Bengals’ first selection on the offensive side of the ball this past draft. While that didn’t come until the […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals defeated the Philadelphia Eagles 30-13 in their third and final preseason game of the year. Now, we’re taking a look at how the offensive rookies performed in Philly. Connor Lew Lew was the Bengals’ first selection on the offensive side of the ball this past draft. While that didn’t come until the 4th round, Lew was widely projected as a top-50 prospect before tearing his ACL in late October of 2025. While he is still regaining his form, he showed he has a really bright future in the Queen City. There were a couple of bad reps where he struggled handling pure power, but I chalk that up to still getting back to full strength. Overall, it was another quality performance from the recently turned 21-year-old rookie. Lew played 33 snaps during his second preseason action of the year. That was important for him to show that he can handle starting the season on the active roster. While Lew may not be asked to play a ton this season, he is incredible depth and a player that is set to be the center of the future in Cincinnati. Connor Lew looked good again on Friday night versus the Eagles. Just turned 21 years old today (Happy Birthday) and is the center of the future in Cincinnati. pic.twitter.com/mbh4QIwdwG — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) August 30, 2026 Colbie Young The Bengals’ second fourth-round draft selection, Young didn’t impress nearly as much as he did during the first couple of preseason games. He finished with just 1 reception for 9 yards on the night. He played in 19 total snaps, which were 10 more than fellow wide receiver Dohnte Meyers. Meyers ended up with 3 catches for 51 yards on his 9 snaps. Colbie Young is still a big part of the future here, but I can see him being a game-day inactive early in the season. The reason being that Meyers has earned a larger role over him to start the season. Regardless, both players will get opportunities throughout the year. It will be up to them to make the most of it. Brian Parker II Parker was the Bengals’ sixth-round draft selection out of Duke this year. He played mainly right tackle for the Blue Devils, but has transitioned to the interior offensive line in Cincinnati. I thought he shined throughout the preseason. He showed his versatility by playing significant snaps at both left and right guard, along with playing some center during the first week of the preseason. Unfortunately, Parker was rolled up on late in the preseason finale. The Bengals decided to place him on IR to begin the season. This means he will miss at least the first four weeks of the season to begin the year. While that is a bummer for him, it doesn’t change his long-term projection in Cincinnati. This is a player who will likely be next in line to start at right guard whenever Dalton Risner’s time in Cincinnati is over. The future looks really bright with an interior offensive line trio of Dylan Fairchild, Connor Lew, and Brian Parker II. Brian Parker II has taken extensive snaps at both left and right guard this preseason. Also, he had some playing time at center during the first week. Valuable depth and a future starter in my opinion. What a steal to land him in the 6th round. pic.twitter.com/bLkqwBMijZ — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) August 30, 2026 Jack Endries It was another quiet game for Endries on Friday night. He finished the game with just 2 catches for 11 yards. While there were some concerns he could be squeezed off of the 53-man roster, the Bengals elected to keep him as the 5th tight end on Sunday night. I think Endries will be a big part of the future at the tight end position, but he is still coming along as a blocker. For that reason, I think we will see Endries start the season as a game-day inactive early in the year. Jamal Haynes Haynes and fellow undrafted free agent running back Kentrel Bullock were both impressive for the Bengals during the preseason finale. Bullock had 14 carries for 85 yards and scored a touchdown during the game. Haynes finished with 7 carries for 78 yards and a score of his own. I chose to highlight Haynes for this one. He looked extremely shifty in the open field. He is built naturally low to the ground, and his footwork is so fun to watch. The converted wide receiver adds value as a pass catcher and displayed good vision throughout the night. It was an electric performance to end the preseason. Sadly, Haynes was not kept on the 53-man roster and has not been signed to the practice squad, so he’s a free agent. Jamal Haynes was ELECTRIC against the Eagles last night. He ran for 78 yards and a touchdown. Averaging 11.1 yards per carry. He was patient, elusive, and displayed good vision. A player I liked as a former receiver, that should be able to develop into an all-around talent at… pic.twitter.com/7jObSzTsj5 — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) August 29, 2026

title: Bengals News: Banged-up receivers
summary: The preseason is over, and the Cincinnati Bengals have trimmed their roster down to the 53 men they hope will win them the city’s first Super Bowl. Now that training camp and the offseason program are officially over, the Bengals are getting to work on preparing for their first game that actually matters, against the […]
full_text: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'marr Chase (1) takes a seat as he’s examined by the training staff after a collision with cornerback DJ Turner II (0) during Bengals training camp practice at the Paycor Stadium practice facility in downtown Cincinnati on Tuesday, Aug. 25, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The preseason is over, and the Cincinnati Bengals have trimmed their roster down to the 53 men they hope will win them the city’s first Super Bowl. Now that training camp and the offseason program are officially over, the Bengals are getting to work on preparing for their first game that actually matters, against the Buccaneers at home on September 13. As part of getting ready for the game, head coach Zac Taylor talked to the media about the health status of a few players, including two bona fide star wide receivers—Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. “He’ll be limited throughout the week, but I feel good about him,” he said about Chase . “Shemar will be on the rehab field this week. Tee has a little heel contusion that’ll limit him this week.” It obviously sounds like both will be back in time for the team’s Week 1 game in a couple of weeks, which is great news. Hopefully Shemar Stewart isn’t far behind them. Here’s what else is going on: The Bengals signed quarterback Josh Johnson to their practice squad on Monday . Both he and fellow backup quarterback Sean Clifford are on the practice squad, and this means the Bengals now have two quarterbacks on their roster who are 40 years of age or older—Johnson and Joe Flacco. Cincinnati Bengals Double Down on Swing Tackle Battle With 2 New Additions “I feel like we added two guys to the mix, one on the 53, one on the practice squad, that have come in here and compete,” head coach Zac Taylor said. “We want to give all those guys a chance to continue to develop our depth that way.” Charlie Jones, who was selected by the Bengals in the fourth round of the 2023 NFL Draft, was released by the Bengals during final cuts. He had been the team’s return specialist when he was on the field, and was in the running for the WR6 spot with Ke’Shawn Williams and Mitchell Tinsley. The team went with Williams, and now Jones has been signed to the New York Giants practice squad . Early returns from Dexter Lawrence are promising for Bengals “There are big people all around the league,” Perine said, “but usually when they’re that big, they have a little give because they’re a little bit fluffy-ish. But with him, it’s just like a massive ball of muscle and there’s no moving him.” New Nameplates Mean A New Bengals Locker Room: ‘We’ve Got A Real Chance’ “We’ve got a real chance. We’ve got to play to it. A deep team. We’ve got to play to it. It’s an easy team to lead. A lot of guys that want to do the right thing all the time. High energy guys, too. One of the toughest (offensive line) rooms I’ve ever been a part of. Comes to work every day and fights through things.”

full_text: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Charlie Jones (15) walks between sessions during practice at the Paycor Stadium practice facility in downtown Cincinnati on Monday, Aug. 3, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Since being drafted in the fourth round of the 2023 Draft, Charlie Jones has been the Cincinnati Bengals’ primary punt returner. title: Bengals get great news on Erick All Jr. ahead of 2026 season opener vs. Bucs
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals have maybe the highest expectations in franchise history this season. After overhauling their defense in the offseason, their always-dangerous offense will look to keep carrying the load, with a solid defensive unit to fall back on. Something that should help the offense is tight end Erick All Jr. being back and healthy. […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 13: Erick All Jr. #83 of the Cincinnati Bengals in action during the game against the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium on October 13, 2024 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cincinnati Bengals have maybe the highest expectations in franchise history this season. After overhauling their defense in the offseason, their always-dangerous offense will look to keep carrying the load, with a solid defensive unit to fall back on. Something that should help the offense is tight end Erick All Jr. being back and healthy. During the 2024 season, All was looking to establish a consistent role in the Bengals’ offense before tearing his ACL nine games into his rookie season. Complications from the surgery to repair that tear wound up costing him the entire 2025 season. When speaking to the media on Tuesday, head coach Zac Taylor gave a promising update on All, who didn’t play this preseason. Taylor said that All is not only fully cleared, but will be involved in the game plan. All told reporters during training camp that he felt ready to play, noting that he got hit by a small truck while vacationing overseas. All said that after that happened, he knew he was ready for football. All’s injury history dates all the way back to college, so injuries will always be a concern. Even knowing that, it doesn’t appear that Taylor is planning to ease All back into game action. In case you were wondering if the unleashing of Erick All is coming, I offered two options for an early season vision to Zac Taylor. 1) Full workload, no reservations. 2) Touch and go to see how he responds. “The first one. The first one.” End of answer. Zero hesitation. — Paul Dehner Jr. (@pauldehnerjr) September 1, 2026 All has shown flashes as a receiver, but brings a great blocking element to the Bengal offense as well. Look for him to be on the field plenty this season.
author: Drew Garrison

title: Josh Johnson is signed to Bengals’ practice squad
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are set at quarterback with starter Joe Burrow and backup Joe Flacco, arguably the best QB room in the league. So it was always going to be tough for 40-year-old veteran Josh Johnson to make the roster. Still, he did everything he could to show he’s still got it, absolutely balling out […]
full_text: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Josh Johnson (11) looks on from the backfield during Bengals training camp practice at the Paycor Stadium practice facility in downtown Cincinnati on Tuesday, Aug. 25, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Cincinnati Bengals are set at quarterback with starter Joe Burrow and backup Joe Flacco, arguably the best QB room in the league. So it was always going to be tough for 40-year-old veteran Josh Johnson to make the roster. Still, he did everything he could to show he’s still got it, absolutely balling out in his last two preseason games against the Chicago Bears and Philadelphia Eagles. Johnson finished the preseason completing 27 of 42 passes (64.3%) for 312 yards, two touchdowns, and zero interceptions. He was in command and accurate those last two games. But that wasn’t enough for him to get signed to another squad’s roster. Now we learn that he’ll remain in Cincinnati after being signed to the Bengals’ practice squad. Veteran QB Josh Johnson is signing with the Bengals practice squad. pic.twitter.com/yO5zutcek1 — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) September 1, 2026 If Burrow were to go down, Johnson would provide great insurance behind Flacco, allowing the Bengals to keep a level of consistency at QB that they hadn’t seen before they traded for Flacco in the middle of last season.
