full_text: Aug 28, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Dohnte Meyers (81) makes a catch against the Philadelphia Eagles during the first quarter at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Training camp and the preseason are finished, and the Cincinnati Bengals have trimmed their roster down to the 53 men required to start the regular season, which begins in about a week and a half. Between now and then, it’s possible the Bengals add someone or move a few things around, but what we have right now is likely pretty close to what we’ll see in Week 1. There weren’t a ton of HUGE surprises, but there were a few. Here are some thoughts on the Bengals’ 53-man roster: I was happy to see Landon Robinson make the final 53, but I don’t think there was ever much doubt that he would. He’s the kind of kid you love to root for, and I have a feeling we’ll be seeing a lot of him, even though the Bengals’ defensive tackle rotation is very deep. I waffled back and forth over the last few days on what would happen with Tanner Hudson. It’s not that he didn’t deserve a spot; I just didn’t know if the Bengals would keep five tight ends, and I was confident he’d be the first one out the door if they chose to keep only four. In the end, I was right and wrong. They kept him initially, then dropped him to pick up offensive tackle Myles Hinton. The biggest surprise came at wide receiver. I was pretty shocked to see Ke’Shawn Williams make it over Mitchell Tinsley and Charlie Jones. I figured the final wide receiver spot would go to either Jones, because of his ability as a return specialist, or Tinsley, who turned a lot of heads last season. In the end, it went to neither. That means Williams is the new return specialist. I was also somewhat surprised to see Jones clear waivers and not even sign with a practice squad (as of this writing). Tinsley, meanwhile, was quickly claimed by the Texans. Josh Newton’s addition is likely a result of Ja’Sir Taylor being placed on IR with a designation to return because of a hamstring issue. Newton spent much of the preseason in the doghouse, but now he has at least the next four weeks to prove he belongs on the roster for good. Speaking of IR, it’s great news that Shemar Stewart avoided it. It’s not that there was much conversation about him being placed there, but it was still a relief knowing that, even if he isn’t ready for Week 1, we won’t automatically be waiting until Week 5 to see him. What is the thinnest position now that the roster is set? I’d have to go with linebacker and running back. What say you? Is there anything the Bengals can realistically do about either position right now? I’m not sure there’s anyone sitting around who could help them in a meaningful way. Bobby Wagner is still out there, but I feel like if that were going to happen, it probably would have happened by now. So, for the most part, I think this roster is set. Still , even with the lack of depth at running back and linebacker, I am very excited about this team. Offensively, the Bengals are a massive bomb ready to explode at any moment. There isn’t a defense in the NFL that can completely shut this offense down. There’s just too much talent. Sure, you can slow down Ja’Marr Chase, but then you have Tee Higgins to deal with. Take those two away, and there’s Mike Gesicki, Andrei Iosivas and the running backs. And, of course, Joe Burrow is the guy pulling the trigger. Good luck. And I’m just as excited about the defense. I wish they would have done more at linebacker, and I wouldn’t have complained about another veteran cornerback, but I think this has a chance to be the Bengals’ best defense since the 2021 and 2022 seasons. The defensive line is going to be so much better, and that improvement will trickle all the way back to the safeties. A defensive back’s best friend is a quarterback who doesn’t have time to throw. Remember how things worked when DJ Reader was soaking up blockers in the middle of the defensive line? It should be like that again. There are still plenty of variables. Health is a huge one, and there is little anyone can do to control that. A couple of key injuries can change the trajectory of an entire season overnight. Usually, when we reach this point in the offseason, I’m disappointed. I’ve almost always felt like the Bengals didn’t do enough to improve. That they left obvious holes unfilled. That they were counting too heavily on young players developing or injured players staying healthy. That too much was being left up to chance. I don’t feel that way right now. They took some big swings this offseason. They addressed major weaknesses. They added legitimate difference-makers. Are there still holes? Absolutely. But any complaints I have about this roster as it stands today feel more like nitpicking than legitimate grievances. For once, I’m not looking at the roster and thinking about what the Bengals should have done. I’m looking at what they actually did. And I like it. There’s a 14-3 team in that 53-man roster. Hopefully we get to see it. Relative Song Lyrics: 🦋 ‘Cause I can see the light of a clear blue morning I can see the light of a brand new day I can see the light of a clear blue morning Oh, and everything’s gonna be all right It’s gonna be okay

title: Browns HC taking a clean-slate approach to Deshaun Watson
summary: The Cleveland Browns are now less than two weeks away from the start of the 2026 NFL season.  When they take the field on the afternoon of September 13 against the Jacksonville Jaguars, quarterback Deshaun Watson will be leading the offense in his first regular-season game in almost two years.  Of course, missing extended periods […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - AUGUST 03: Head coach Todd Monken of the Cleveland Browns instructs Deshaun Watson #4 during the Cleveland Browns Training Camp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on August 03, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns are now less than two weeks away from the start of the 2026 NFL season. When they take the field on the afternoon of September 13 against the Jacksonville Jaguars, quarterback Deshaun Watson will be leading the offense in his first regular-season game in almost two years. Of course, missing extended periods of time is nothing new to Watson, a trend he started himself when he sat out the entire 2021 season in a contract dispute with the Houston Texans. After being traded to the Browns in 2022, he missed the first 11 games of that season while serving an NFL-mandated suspension, 11 more games in 2023 (shoulder injury), 10 more games in 2024 (torn Achilles tendon), and all 17 games in 2025 (re-tear of same Achilles tendon). All told, Watson has played in just 19 games in the past five seasons, which is not preferable. Worse, when he did play, he was the definition of not good, with an EPA/dropback of -0.14 in 2022, -0.09 in 2023, and -0.25 in 2024 . What’s more, that number in 2024? It was the lowest of any quarterback in the past two seasons. (The quarterback one spot above Watson? None other than Shedeur Sanders and his horrible rookie season of 2025! ) But we digress. Anyone who has watched Watson play since arriving in Cleveland knows he is not the same quarterback he was in Houston. And the numbers back up the idea that he will likely never be that quarterback. There is one person, two if you count Watson, who doesn’t care about that, however, which is head coach Todd Monken. It’s not that Monken is unfamiliar with Watson’s decline, as Monken has been coaching in the NFL for six of Watson’s eight seasons, including the past three when he was offensive coordinator of the division rival Baltimore Ravens. But this is Monken’s first year in Cleveland and first time as a head coach in the NFL, so he is taking a “clean slate” approach to Watson (and the rest of the roster), as he explained during his media session on Tuesday : “I really, to be honest, haven’t looked at it. To be honest, only from afar. When people say, ‘You had to look at it,’ well, not really. I looked at it from afar when I was down the road, in crossover film or something, but I try to take everything at face value, what I see. It doesn’t matter who the player is; I think we owe that to our players, guys that are on the roster. “I want to go into it thinking every player we have is elite, and all they have to do is prove me right. That’s all they have to do. That’s how I’m going to go into it. They’re on an NFL roster; I expect them to play well, and I just want them to prove me right. So, I really haven’t looked at that – different staff, different system. We’ll let it play out. We’ll see where it goes starting a week from now.” It is an interesting way to approach the situation. Whether he wants to admit it or not, Watson has to know on some level he has not been the same player since arriving in Cleveland. So having the head coach bring that up all the time is probably not very beneficial. But there is also some risk involved if Watson continues to play poorly and Monken remains stubborn about accepting that even if he isn’t looking at the past, Watson is done as an upper-tier starting quarterback in the NFL. Of course, the current quarterback room is void of anyone who is a viable starting quarterback at the NFL level, so even if it takes a few extra weeks for Monken to come to the realization, the Browns haven’t really lost all that much from an on-field perspective.

title: Thoughts on Browns roster cuts, practice squad, Luke Floriea and more
summary: What a whirlwind for the Cleveland Browns in the past two days. After their final preseason game, the Browns coaching staff and GM Andrew Berry had nothing but decisions to make. But here is the thing: a lot of these decisions had nothing to do with the preseason games. Why? None of the Browns players […]
full_text: Aug 15, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Cleveland Browns cornerback Michael Coats Jr. (39) intercepts a pass against the Chicago Bears during the first half at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: Mike Dinovo-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect What a whirlwind for the Cleveland Browns in the past two days. After their final preseason game, the Browns coaching staff and GM Andrew Berry had nothing but decisions to make. But here is the thing: a lot of these decisions had nothing to do with the preseason games. Why? None of the Browns players faced the starting offensive and defensive units of any of the 31 NFL clubs. How is an evaluation done for any player who dominates against another team’s second team? RELATED: 2026 53-MAN INITIAL ROSTER Here are some things on my mind regarding the last few days : 1 . First, let’s get to the elephant in the room: Luke Floriea . The talented receiver was the darling of the Browns’ preseason games , getting open frequently, juking out defenders, and scoring three touchdowns, including two in one contest. But hold on for a sec. All of that was against all three opponents’ second-team defensive units. Not a single defensive starter covered Floriea, so yeah, he looked great. Browns will not be adding WR Luke Floriea to the practice squad, per @JFowlerESPN . pic.twitter.com/sDwElnEK9W — ESPN Cleveland (@ESPNCleveland) August 31, 2026 The starters that did cover Floriea were the Browns’ defensive starters in practice, mainly Denzel Ward and Tytus Campbell . Remember, Cleveland’s defense was ranked #4 last year. What did Floriea do against those two corners? Get wide open, juke them out, and score a ton of touchdowns? Or get stifled? Here’s another thought. Greg Larvadain, Malachi Corley , and Tylan Wallace are all returners as well as receivers. With all the new bodies in the Browns receiver room this year, the final two guys in this group aren’t going to see the field much, unless they can offer the ability to return punts and kickoffs. My guess is that because both Corley and Wallace are returners, this aspect kicked Floriea out the door. Plus, Floriea cannot remain engaged in downfield blocking. Now, did Berry call Floriea back to be added to the practice squad? Or did the young receiver decide to move on after getting waived by two sets of Cleveland coaching staffs? Keep in mind, none of the other NFL clubs put in a waiver claim on him. And as the Browns proceed with Jerry Jeudy , KC Concepcion , Denzel Boston , and Isaiah Bond , if any of these were to be injured and end up on IR, all Berry has to do is claim Floriea off another team’s practice squad list. 2 . Another surprise cut was OG KT Leveston . I really thought he had found his groove after being moved from offensive tackle inside to guard. He did well in preseason against other teams’ second-string defensive units. In fact, the second-team offensive line looked great in all of the preseason games. Usually, bigger guys like Leveston (6’-4”, 335 pounds) don’t do well on the interior. But he has that versatility to move over if needed, or become a swing tackle. Leveston would have been the backup behind RG Teven Jenkins (or rookie Austin Barber ), who has not only been thrust into the starting lineup but has also missed time in camp with an injury and, early in training camp, complained of a stiff back. 3 . Okay, rookie offensive lineman Austin Barber really showed out in training camp. He was smooth in preseason games and is further along than the coaches thought he would be. Referring back to Leveston, Barber just might be the reason they let him go. Barber played a ton of snaps at offensive guard in preseason, but is listed on the depth chart at RT behind Tytus Howard . Thought Browns rookie 3rd round OL Austin Barber looked pretty comfortable at RG vs BUF. Played all RT last week vs CHI Loved this 3rd down rep… The initial punch vs 3T, passing off stunt – then snatching/finishing the looper. Shedeur had some nice pockets to operate! pic.twitter.com/TU3MtADNIE — Ben Fennell (@BenFennell_NFL) August 23, 2026 Barber is a guy who has had a slew of college offers since leading his high school team to the 3A State Championship. Barber started 33 games at left tackle and two games at right tackle for Florida and was a two-and-a-half-year starter. In his junior year, his pass-blocking grade was 70.9. He provides a quality blocker who has every opportunity to become the starter next year, but at this moment provides quality depth in the event of an injury. His ability to drop inside is a huge advantage. 4 . Another perplexing rookie is TE Joe Royer . He was earmarked to become a part of the final roster , but has been AWOL with a “personal issue.” What is this such a secret? Some digging has found nothing. Berry isn’t saying, nor is head coach Todd Monken. If it is a health issue with himself or a family member, then just tell us so that we will know and then quit asking. This happened when he played for Ohio State, and his mom became ill. He then transferred to the University of Cincinnati, his hometown. But everyone knew without prying. At least the Browns’ front office placed him on the reserve/non-football illness list to retain him, so they must believe he is coming back at some point. 5 . Well, the quarterback room issue worked itself out. Dillon Gabriel having a “back issue” is pretty suspect, but it keeps him in-house until the franchise can sort things out. Apparently, he became injured on a third-down run, yet he was seen on the field after the game interacting with friends and former teammates without any issue. He is slated to come off IR in four weeks. If you ask me, it just delays the decision to get rid of one of the four in this group, or at least have to deal with the logjam. Surely, the Browns are not going to keep four QBs , right? But here are my thoughts. The year when Deshaun Watson was suspended for 11 games is the only season he played in Cleveland where he did not get injured. Not to jinx Watson, but he is injury-prone. Perhaps the thought process with the coaches has been that at some point, he will end up hurt once again. Okay, then bring in Shedeur Sanders as the new starting QB. But here’s the rub: do you want Sanders’ backup to be the rookie, Taylen Green ? Great athlete, exceptional runner, horrible accuracy. Yeah, that Taylen Green. Just maybe, by the time the team is putting Watson on IR is when Gabriel will become available. And now, Sanders’ backup is the more experienced Gabriel instead of an unproven rookie or having to scour the free agent list for an experienced backup QB. 6 . Speaking of Green, he should be moved. In my interview with Hall of Fame receiver Paul Warfield , he told me he had played a bit of receiver in high school, but was a running back first and made All-State in that position. When he arrived at Ohio State, he was moved to the defensive backfield, but also played some running back up until he graduated. He was drafted as a cornerback. In his rookie training camp, Browns head coach Blanton Collier took him out of the defensive back group and asked him to play some receiver. In one day, Warfield became a receiver for Cleveland, where he won three rings and became a part of the NFL’s 100-year Team. That could be Green’s story as well. I saw him at this year’s Senior Bowl, and quarterback was on my list to interview. After seeing him run, dodge, and weave , I was excited for our impending talk. But then, seeing him in the 7-on-7s, he couldn’t hit anything: too high, too far, sailed this, behind the receiver, you name it. I scratched him off my list. But if Green was to be moved to receiver or tight end, with his athletic ability and running skills, he would excel. Now, can he catch? 7 . Monken’s offense usually keeps four tight ends on the roster. But with the addition of FB Michael Burton , that eliminated the need. Burton is not only a true fullback, but he is able to line up in traditional tight end…

full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - AUGUST 22: Luke Floriea #81 of the Cleveland Browns celebrates with teammates after catching an eight-yard touchdown pass during the first quarter of a preseason game against the Buffalo Bills at Huntington Bank Field on August 22, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images While we are monitoring the Cleveland Browns’ roster cuts as they get set to name their initial 53-man roster, all eyes will then shift to Monday, when waiver claims are processed, and then teams can start signing players to their 16-man practice squad. There will be some interesting decisions at quarterback and wide receiver in particular, with respect to who the team is able to retain on its practice squad. 53 + 16 players means the team has the opportunity to retain 69 players from training camp on their roster, but often what we see if that 10-12 of those players were from camp, while the remaining players are guys who were with other teams around the NFL. title: Cowboys betting on 2 former Top 100 draft picks to upgrade OT depth
summary: We all know all too well that where a player is ultimately drafted, or not, doesn’t always equate to success. We’ve seen former first-round picks turn out to be absolute busts and undrafted players become superstars with the Dallas Cowboys throughout the history of the organization. We’ve also seen top drafted players who were considered […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 6: Broderick Jones #77 of the Pittsburgh Steelers looks on during the game against the Dallas Cowboys at Acrisure Stadium on October 6, 2024 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images We all know all too well that where a player is ultimately drafted, or not, doesn’t always equate to success. We’ve seen former first-round picks turn out to be absolute busts and undrafted players become superstars with the Dallas Cowboys throughout the history of the organization. We’ve also seen top drafted players who were considered busts arrive in Dallas and completely turn their careers around. The Cowboys are hoping Broderick Jones and Wanya Morris, both former Top 100 draft picks, fall into that category. New Cowboys OTs Broderick Jones (77) and Wanya Morris (64) pic.twitter.com/ZFH8aJer6y — Tommy Yarrish (@tommy_yarrish) September 1, 2026 With concerns about the overall depth at the offensive tackle position, the Cowboys went out and acquired Broderick Jones via trade from the Pittsburgh Steelers. Jones was pick 15 in the first round of the 2023 NFL Draft and has started a total of 38 games at both left and right tackle in his three seasons in Pittsburgh. While his career hasn’t panned out the way he had probably hoped so far, the change of scenery hopefully works in his favor much like it did his former Steelers teammate, George Pickens. Jones’ arrival in Dallas puts a target on the back of Dallas’ current starting RT Terence Steele. Both players have been informed the starting RT job is up for grabs and to the victor go the spoils. With the 2026 NFL season opener against the division rival New York Giants quickly approaching, it seems highly unlikely Jones will overtake Steele for the starting job right away. But, considering No. 78’s struggles, it’s not completely out of the question either. While expectations probably aren’t as high for the other OT Dallas signed the practice squad, Wanya Morris is an intriguing prospect as well. A former teammate of LT Tyler Guyton in 2022 at Oklahoma, Morris was overall pick 92 (third round) in the 2023 NFL Draft by the Kansas City Chiefs. He started a total of 15 games in his career with the Chiefs, winning a Super Bowl as a rookie, before being traded a few months ago to the Atlanta Falcons for a sixth-round pick in 2026. Morris’ time on the practice squad is insurance for Dallas’ rookie OT Drew Shelton. Shelton needs more time to develop and doesn’t look pro-ready just yet. Morris acts as a stop-gap if injury and inconsistent play plague the tackle room. The additions of both Broderick Jones and Wanya Morris show the Dallas Cowboys knew of the concerns at the OT position and went out and attempted to address the issue. They are betting they can tap into the talent that made both of these players Top 100 draft picks and reap the rewards. Under the tutelage of Kayton Adams, a highly regarded former OL coach, and Conor Riley, a highly regarded OL coach from the college ranks, big things could be on the horizon and for both of these tackle prospects. Klayton Adams with his newest project: new RT Broderick Jones pic.twitter.com/i9S3h4aD0W — Joseph Hoyt (@JoeJHoyt) August 31, 2026 Apologies for the poor quality, but here’s Cowboys offensive line coach Conor Riley working with Terence Steele (left) and new Cowboys OT Broderick Jones (right). Jones has been given #77. Brian Schottenheimer said earlier today the two are competing for the starting RT job. pic.twitter.com/azhHc5KLiv — Tommy Yarrish (@tommy_yarrish) August 31, 2026

title: Cowboys news: Why Dallas picked Sam Howell as their QB2
summary: The Dallas Cowboys shocked the NFL world when they decided to release Joe Milton, opting for Sam Howell as their backup to Dak Prescott. Milton shined in the preseason, outperforming most quarterbacks statistically, and showed real growth from year one to two in Dallas’ offense. So why did Dallas opt for Howell over Milton? Brian […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - AUGUST 28: Sam Howell #16 of the Dallas Cowboys walks off the field after the 2026 NFL preseason game against the New Orleans Saints at AT&T Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys shocked the NFL world when they decided to release Joe Milton, opting for Sam Howell as their backup to Dak Prescott. Milton shined in the preseason, outperforming most quarterbacks statistically, and showed real growth from year one to two in Dallas’ offense. So why did Dallas opt for Howell over Milton? Brian Schottenheimer spoke on it today during his press conference, hoping to answer the questions surrounding the move. Here is the latest news around the Dallas Cowboys. Why the Cowboys chose Sam Howell as their backup quarterback – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com At the end of the day, Howell does have more experience than Milton at the NFL level. “I think when we looked at the whole body of work, we just felt like Sam had done a little bit more in terms of executing the offense in certain areas,” Schottenheimer said. “To have Joe Milton back would be incredible, we’ll see what happens with the claims, and then see what he wants to do. We’ve shown that we know how to develop him. I think him being in this system for another year would be amazing, but I also know that he should have choices. And so, we’ll see what happens, but in terms of wanting [Milton] back, absolutely.” Joe Milton Goes Unclaimed On Waivers as Cowboys Eye QB for Practice Squad – Paul Kasabian, Bleacher Report Will the Cowboys sign Milton back to the practice squad, or will he opt to sign elsewhere? Although the Dallas Cowboys waived quarterback Joe Milton, both COO/co-owner Stephen Jones and head coach Brian Schottenheimer expressed significant interest in having the signal-caller back in the mix via the practice squad. Jones made his remarks on the DLLS Cowboys podcast, and Schottenheimer revealed his feelings to reporters during his Tuesday press conference. Emari Demercado returns ‘home’ to Dallas, has reason to be excited with Cowboys – Patrik Walker, DallasCowboys.com The Cowboys newest running back has familiarity with OC Klayton Adams. He will also be placed, once again, under the watchful eye of Klayton Adams, the former Cardinals’ offensive line coach turned Cowboys’ offensive coordinator keenly responsible for crafting the rushing attack for Brian Schottenheimer’s offense. Adams immediately called Demercado once the trade was made official, and the elation is palpable from both player and coach. “Klay’s my guy,” he said of Adams. “As soon as my agent called me and told me it was Dallas, I just immediately thought about Klayton. And then he called me. I’m super excited to work with him again. Michael Irvin giving Dallas Cowboys 10 more years to prove they’re still America’s Team – Brandon Contes, Awful Announcing To Michael Irvin’s point, a whole generation of Cowboys fans have never seen their favorite team in a Championship game. “There’s some credence to what they’re saying,” Irvin admitted. “We cannot remain America’s Team if a whole generation of Americans never see us in a championship game. And in 10 more years – the bible calls 40 years a generation – we would have missed a whole damn generation. So the time is now.” Broderick Jones ‘pumped’ for fresh start with Cowboys, reunion with George Pickens – Patrik Walker, DallasCowboys.com The former first-round pick is happy the Cowboys have a plan for him at just right tackle. It goes without saying that Jones, also making it known exactly how thrilled he is to know the Cowboys will set him at right tackle and leave him there, feels exactly the same way as Pickens. “I’m pumped up, man. I’m just pumped up, you know?” he said. “They made it clear where they want me. I just gotta do my part and show up.” Making sense of Cowboys’ surprising roster cuts ahead of 2026 season: Joe Milton, Jaydon Blue and more – Garrett Podell, CBS Sports It feels like Dallas opted for players who can contribute now rather than developmental guys. RBs Jaydon Blue and Phil Mafah Now, both are gone for reasons that fall under the umbrella of “consistency” that Schottenheimer stresses his players possess. Both ended up being outworked in training camp and the preseason by undrafted veteran Malik Davis , with Davis showcasing his value not only as a runner but also on special teams. Last season, Davis spent some time as the punt protector while also being a factor in other phases of special teams. Daily discussion question: What is your biggest concern with the roster?

Former Cowboys QB Joe Milton cleared waivers today and is now a free agent. pic.twitter.com/63FzBtW57X — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) September 1, 2026 Just in: QB Joe Milton was not claimed off waivers, per today's NFL transaction wire. Given the state of QB play in the NFL, especially among second-stringers, Milton feels like one of the 64-best options in the league. But now that he’s cleared waivers, one must wonder what the whispers are among coaches and other decision-makers about him. Still, if what Schotty said is true, there is a spot on the Cowboys’ practice squad. Will Milton take it, or will he hope to find a new team with more opportunity?

title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 12
summary: It is Day 12 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like […]
full_text: Dallas Cowboys tight end Jay Novacek runs with the football after making a catch during the Cowboys 38-27 victory over the Green Bay Packers in the 1995 NFC Championship Game on January 14, 1996 at Texas Stadium in Irving, Texas. (Photo by Joseph Patronite/Getty Images) *** Local Caption *** It is Day 12 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. We’re now at Day 12 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff, when we revisit the NFC Championship Game that sent Dallas to Super Bowl XXX and completed the final title run of the 1990s dynasty. The Packers had just survived a difficult postseason road trip through San Francisco, but their next stop was Dallas, and the stakes were higher than ever. Sunday, January 14, 1996 Texas Stadium, Irving, Texas Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 38, Green Bay Packers 27 Green Bay struck first after Dallas punter John Jett had a punt blocked, giving the Packers possession deep in Cowboys territory. Chris Jacke converted a 46-yard field goal for a 3-0 lead, but Dallas answered almost immediately. Troy Aikman directed an 80-yard drive and found Michael Irvin from six yards out to put the Cowboys ahead 7-3. The defense then created another opportunity when Leon Lett intercepted Brett Favre on a screen pass and returned the ball deep into Green Bay territory. Aikman capitalized with another touchdown pass to Irvin, this time from four yards, giving Dallas a 14-3 advantage. Favre responded in explosive fashion. His first completion of the game became a 73-yard touchdown to Robert Brooks, cutting the deficit to 14-10. Early in the second quarter, Favre found tight end Keith Jackson for a 24-yard score, suddenly putting Green Bay ahead 17-14. Dallas settled the game down through its running attack. Chris Boniol tied the score with a 34-yard field goal, then the Cowboys produced one of the defining drives of the afternoon. Starting at their own one-yard line, they travelled 99 yards, with Emmitt Smith breaking off a 25-yard run to escape the shadow of the goal line. Smith eventually finished the drive with a one-yard touchdown to send Dallas into halftime leading 24-17. Green Bay refused to disappear. Jacke made a 37-yard field goal during the third quarter before Favre connected with Brooks for a one-yard touchdown. That score gave the Packers a 27-24 lead and placed Dallas behind entering the final quarter. That was when the Cowboys’ championship experience took over. Dallas responded with a 90-yard drive, pounding Green Bay with Smith until he finished it with a five-yard touchdown run. The Cowboys had regained the lead at 31-27, but there was still plenty of time remaining. The defense then delivered the pivotal stop. Favre tried to attack deep while escaping pressure, but Larry Brown intercepted him and returned the ball 28 yards to the Dallas 48. On the very next offensive play, Irvin made a 36-yard reception along the sideline, putting the Packers defense back under immediate pressure. Smith finished the job with a 16-yard touchdown run, stretching the lead to 38-27. Green Bay never answered, and Dallas closed out another NFC championship at Texas Stadium. This game belongs on the countdown because it continued the last great postseason statement of the Cowboys’ 1990s dynasty. Green Bay had an MVP quarterback in Favre, had already knocked off San Francisco on the road and actually carried a lead into the fourth quarter. Dallas responded exactly as a championship team should by controlling the line of scrimmage, forcing the crucial turnover and leaning on Smith when the game tightened. #Cowboys vs #Packers 1995 NFC Championship Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 38, Green Bay Packers 27 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/XOF00Zqr2r — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) September 1, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game Emmitt Smith carried a Cowboys playoff-record 35 times and finished with 150 rushing yards. title: Cowboys practice squad analysis for all signed players
summary: The majority of the Dallas Cowboys practice squad for 2026 is set for the moment, with the big name to watch as a potential returnee being backup QB Joe Milton. If the team is able to get Milton onto the practice squad, it would bring their total up to 15 out of a possible 16 […]
full_text: Jul 29, 2026; Oxnard, CA, USA; Dallas Cowboys defensive tackle Tommy Dunn (95) wears a Guardian helmet cap at training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The majority of the Dallas Cowboys practice squad for 2026 is set for the moment, with the big name to watch as a potential returnee being backup QB Joe Milton. If the team is able to get Milton onto the practice squad, it would bring their total up to 15 out of a possible 16 spots. Their extra international player pathway spot to potentially build the practice squad up to as high as 17 players is already filled with DE Adedayo Odeleye. We are tracking every move of the practice squad in real time right here , but now it is time for some quick analysis on the 15 players already confirmed to the PS, and how they could help this team on gamedays if/when they get the call up to the active roster. RB Israel Abanikanda The Cowboys’ initial 53-man roster had a real lack of running back depth, but the team has been hard at work remedying this ever since the initial cutdown deadline. Emari Demarcado is the newest addition to the active roster out of the backfield , and Israel Abanikanda has made it to the practice squad. Dallas keeping Javonte Williams and Malik Davis as their one-two punch paints a very clear picture of the type of back they want to feature the most, and Abanikanda in a lesser sense has some of the same physicality and north/south ability as this duo. This is exactly the type of reason practice squad positions exist, and having the ability to call on Abanikanda in an emergency situation is good work by Brian Schottenheimer and Klayton Adams to protect the depth of their offensive approach. LB Justin Barron Like Abanikanda, linebacker Justin Barron is also a returnee to the practice squad after spending time with the team in 2025. Barron, who did not flash as much as some fans had hoped for in the preseason, was left off the roster at linebacker in favor of DeMarvion Overshown, Shemar James, rookie Jaishawn Barham, and trade acquisition Dee Winters. Of these four current inside backers for the Cowboys defense, Barron likely profiles most similarly to Shemar James, who also hasn’t taken the strides to fully grasp a projected spot on gamedays. The most likely role Barron will help this team on a week-to-week basis will be in practice settings, as a smart coverage linebacker that can help the scout defense still play with structure and skill. Should a player like James struggle in his role or Overshown gets hurt though, look for Barron to be elevated and at very least see the field on special teams which he did for two games late in the season a year ago. DT Tommy Dunn The Cowboys want to play their money players at defensive tackle, which makes perfect sense seeing as they now have multiple such players after devaluing the position for so long. The trio of Kenny Clark, Quinnen Williams, and Otito Ogbonnia didn’t leave room for other ‘bucket of dirt’ type tackles to make this roster, but when it comes to needing a backup on the practice squad, Dallas opted for UDFA newcomer Tommy Dunn. Playing his college ball at Kansas, Dunn was a standout in the preseason, playing with a good motor, flashing the ability to move gap to gap, push the pocket a little bit, and most importantly not get knocked off the ball against the run. As all fans already know, the NFL season is a long battle of attrition, and depth in the trenches is going to need to be called on. While the Cowboys likely won’t feel great about their defensive interior if Dunn is playing extended snaps in a real game, he is certainly a player that could be in a rotation with enough physical traits to not get exposed. WR Jordan Hudson Another undrafted newcomer to the practice squad, Jordan Hudson now has an even cooler story coming out of the final preseason home game versus the Saints. Going from a relatively unknown, longest of longshots at wide receiver to star of the night, Hudson took on the Camden Brown role for one night and became the UDFA receiver that catches the eye. Doing so with his last preseason chance as a local prospect out of TCU and SMU would have been a cool enough way to end his story with the team for now, but instead it was enough for Hudson to continue developing with the hometown team on the practice squad. Both Brown and Jonathan Mingo made the active roster at receiver, so the journey for any PS pass catcher to make it to gamedays this season is an arduous one. Hudson should still help in plenty of practice situations as a quarterback friendly target that runs clean routes and flashed some contested catch ability. OT Marcellus Johnson When it comes to why some Cowboys fans are a bit worried about the state of the offensive line depth, the team could certainly use more experience in the backup positions across the board. Marcellus Johnson is a name some fans may be hearing for the first time right here and now, and for good reason as he’s never appeared in a regular season game. Johnson is a career practice squad member so far, playing collegiately for both Eastern Michigan and Missouri, and starting his pro journey with the New York Giants in 2024. Between 2024-25 Johnson bounced between the Giants and Vikings, and then the Colts at the end of 2025 before landing with the Cowboys, now returning to the PS for 2026. A player willing to fight things out for a chance at the dream of appearing in the NFL for as long as Johnson has is admirable, and while the Cowboys have explored all options at tackle this offseason including making a recent trade for Broderick Jones, Johnson could get a look at some point – but it would likely come in a dire situation for the offensive line as a whole. DB Derion Kendrick Derion Kendrick spent time with both the Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks and NFC championship participant Los Angeles Rams in 2025, before signing with the Cowboys this offseason. Kendrick looked like a natural fit in Christian Parker’s defense at times this training camp and preseason, capable of playing some cornerback, nickel, or safety. The Cowboys valued special teams ability in their final roster decisions in the secondary, and even though Kendrick has this, he’s positioned on the practice squad for now. Ameer Speed is the surprise of the active group at cornerback, and Caelen Carson is the carryover from past defensive schemes that feels a bit out of place, so there are potential paths for Kendrick to see the field this season. As cliché as it is to say, there really is no such thing as having too many capable cornerbacks, and the Cowboys have a good player to continue developing in this way with Kendrick. WR Anthony Smith This year’s seventh-round pick Anthony Smith came to his first training camp with the Cowboys and ran into a buzz saw when it came to making the roster. A top three of CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, and Ryan Flournoy is suffocating when it comes to how many snaps are available for others. Making matters worse for the rookie Smith, the Cowboys finally saw Jonathan Mingo have a bit of a breakout this offseason, as well as UDFA Camden Brown stealing the show of the preseason. The situation at WR has put Smith on the practice squad, where his speed will be valuable to practice certain looks. Smith has a long way to go when it comes to being a viable enough player to get touches in this ultra-experienced offense for the Cowboys, but is a capable gadget player with strong hands as a receiver that Dallas is willing to continue developing in hopes of hitting on one of just two 2026 draft picks spent on offense. TE Michael Trigg The Cowboys went with the chalkiest of chalk depth charts at tight end, with Jake Ferguson, Brevyn Spann-Ford, and Luke Schoonmaker and making the cut. The most serious contender to grab one of these spots away in the offseason came from priority UDFA Michael Trigg, but a late injury ended this…

title: Breaking down what Broderick Jones competing to start at RT means
summary: The Dallas Cowboys added to their offensive line last Saturday when they acquired offensive lineman Broderick Jones in a trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers. They sent 2027 third- and sixth-round picks to the Steelers and received a fourth-round pick in 2027 in return. Jones played three seasons in Pittsburgh after being selected in the first […]
full_text: The Dallas Cowboys added to their offensive line last Saturday when they acquired offensive lineman Broderick Jones in a trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers. They sent 2027 third- and sixth-round picks to the Steelers and received a fourth-round pick in 2027 in return. Jones played three seasons in Pittsburgh after being selected in the first round in 2023 after a stellar career on the collegiate level with the Georgia Bulldogs. He played in 45 games with 38 starts. During his time there, he got experience playing both left and right tackle, which made him a perfect candidate to be a swing option in Dallas. Once the transaction was made, an interesting thing occurred. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer made a call to right tackle Terence Steele to inform him that Jones would be competing with him for starting duties. According to Schottenheimer, Steele took the news like a pro and appreciated the communication on the matter. With that said, what does all this mean? The first thing is pretty obvious, and that’s that Schottenheimer has full control of what’s going on with the Cowboys’ roster. From the moment he got the job in Dallas, he expressed that guys would have to compete and that nothing was going to be given to anyone. Steele has a ton of experience with 91 starts in 96 career games. There have been some questions if he’s still the answer going forward, which makes it understandable why a guy like Jones, who’s experienced himself, would be brought in to provide some competition. Schottenheimer also said that Steele is still in the driver’s seat and Jones will be working to show that he is capable of being the guy as well. However, this move also puts Steele on notice that if he has any kind of slip up, Jones will undoubtedly be there to takeover as the starter at right tackle. Jones hasn’t quite lived up to his draft status, but he could easily replace Steele, and the latter certainly needs to take the competition seriously, which undoubtedly he will. Jones feels that part of the problem in Pittsburgh was his flip-flopping from the right to the left side. “For me, I would just say bouncing around positions, just not being able to get my feet set,” Jones said. “That was a challenge for me. Coming in, hopefully I can stick to one side. Compete for that job, get comfortable, get familiar with it, get familiar with who I’ll be playing next to and go from there.” Jones will play exclusively on the right side in Dallas as was made clear by Schottenheimer in a press conference. It also means, for now, the main backup at left tackle is Drew Shelton, a rookie who hasn’t exactly inspired confidence. Coming into training camp, offensive tackle was a position that was considered a bit of a question mark. It feels like it still is, but at least the Cowboys are trying. They also added veteran Wanya Morris to the practice squad. Holding competitions for positions is exactly how it should be. Everything is earned in the game of football, and every season you have to update your résumé. So, let the competition begin and may the best man win. By the end of this year, who do you think will be starting at right tackle?
author: Matthew Lenix

title: What new Cowboys RB Emari Demarcado brings to Dallas
summary: NFL cuts are in full swing, but with them comes player movement and an opportunity for players to make a name for themselves elsewhere. Among those searching for greener pastures is ex-Cardinals running back Emari Demarcado. The Dallas Cowboys picked up Demarcado off waivers. Let’s look at what he may bring to the Cowboys roster. […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 28: Running back Emari Demercado #25 of the Kansas City Chiefs is stopped by linebacker Power Echols #46 of the Seattle Seahawks during the 1st half of the preseason game at Arrowhead Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images NFL cuts are in full swing, but with them comes player movement and an opportunity for players to make a name for themselves elsewhere. Among those searching for greener pastures is ex-Cardinals running back Emari Demarcado. The Dallas Cowboys picked up Demarcado off waivers. Let’s look at what he may bring to the Cowboys roster. Upside for big plays At 5’9”, 215 lbs., Demarcado is a shifty, elusive and speedy back that hits gaps fast and is probably what the Cowboys were hoping to find in Jaydon Blue. The thing is, Demarcado has actually had some success in the NFL, particularly with Cowboys OC Klayton Adams. New Cowboys RB Emari Demercado running behind a Klayton Adams-coached offensive line. pic.twitter.com/kt9xqsXFtn — Mauricio Rodríguez (@MauNFL) August 31, 2026 Throughout his previous three years, Demarcado has averaged 6.5 yards per carry on the ground and per reception. He’s added three rushing TDs as well as a receiving touchdown throughout that time frame as well. The last time he was paired with Klayton Adams, Demarcado rushed for 507 yards on 82 carries. A healthy 6.1-yard-per-carry average, but in Adams’ last year in Arizona, Demarcado averaged 9.3 yards per carry. Needless to say, the potential is there. Third-down back If you’re going to be a third-down back in the NFL you need two things: pass-catching ability and pass protection ability. We already noted above that he can catch the ball and turn it into yards, but he also has some experience protecting his quarterback. He logged 47 snaps in pass-protection in 2023, 30 snaps in that role in 2024, and 27 snaps in 2025, spending at least 18% of his total snaps each season in pass-protection. In total, Demercado yielded just eight pressures on his 104 pass-blocking snaps for the Cardinals. Needs Improvement Most of us, however, remember Demarcado coughing up the ball as he blew a would-be touchdown last year when the Cardinals played the Titans. Si les sonaba el nombre se RB Emari Demercado…. #DallasCowboys pic.twitter.com/bygz7GNMwy — Cuentos Vaqueros ✭ (@CuentosVaqueros) August 31, 2026 A lapse of focus? Poor judgment? We may never know; either way, it cost the Cards a game, but to this day it is still the only fumble he has committed in his brief time in the NFL. What about his size? Demarcado is not the smallest back, but he certainly isn’t a bruiser either. What is compelling is that the Cowboys think he can block in pass protection better than Blue or Phil Mafah, and that it could still be an area of growth for him. There have been questions at times about inefficient footwork and his vision not operating quickly enough. In small sample usage, he creates big plays, but can he produce like that on a steady diet of carries? In Dallas, he may not have to but it seems to have held him back from full-time work. Big picture Obviously, Dallas was not satisfied with the running back room behind Javonte Williams. Blue and Mafah did not make the Cowboys’ 53-man roster for a number of reasons, and yes, Demarcado has a couple of years on Blue and Mafah, but he has shown more than either of those two ever have. Demarcado is the kind of back that can exploit a gap and get chunk yardage, a true change-of-pace back that Dallas has been seeking. He is also well-positioned to be a third -down back with his pass-catching skills and ability to hold up in pass protection.

title: Patrick Surtain II sheds light on Bo Nix; defense’s approach to forcing more turnovers
summary: In less than two weeks, the Denver Broncos will kick off their 2026 regular season in a primetime matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday Night Football. The Broncos had a good season in 2025. Alas, the way things ended made last year’s gridiron campaigns one of the greatest ‘What If?’ seasons in franchise […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - AUGUST 14: Pat Surtain II #2 of the Denver Broncos warms up prior to a NFL preseason game against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on August 14, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images In less than two weeks, the Denver Broncos will kick off their 2026 regular season in a primetime matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday Night Football . The Broncos had a good season in 2025. Alas, the way things ended made last year’s gridiron campaigns one of the greatest ‘What If?’ seasons in franchise history. This season, the Broncos are running it back with a roster loaded with continuity. However, they added a few fresh faces on offense at skill positions that hopefully can elevate that unit’s play to the next level. This year’s team might mostly be the same, but their drive and determination to get better has only been amplified over the offseason. How Denver fares this year will hinge a lot on the play of third year quarterback Bo Nix. Despite being the fifth quarterback selected in his draft class, the former Auburn turned Oregon standout has arguably been the best of the bunch. In fact, his total production the past two seasons has ranked near the top of all signal callers in the National Football League. With more than 60 total touchdowns, over 7,700 yards passing, 10 game-winning drives, and 8 fourth quarter comebacks to his name, Nix’s play to date is deserving of praise. And guess what folks? He is going to get better in Year 3. Yesterday after practice, All-Pro cornerback Patrick Surtain II talked about Nix’s growth this offseason and why he is poised for a huge season. “I think his cerebral approach to the game is off the charts. I always say he’s so poised, but he’s always had that calm demeanor going into his third year just bringing all the guys together offensively and just being a tremendous leader on the team. He’s got that dog attitude to him, and that’s what you want in a quarterback,” stated Surtain. Though it won’t be all on the shoulders of Nix to get the Broncos back to the promise land. The defense is going to have to step up in a big way and get better in a few facets they struggled with in ‘25. Late last season, Head Coach Sean Payton remarked during numerous press conferences about how the Broncos’ defense needed to step up and force some big turnovers. After hearing that feedback, the defense answered the call. In multiple December games, the Broncos were able to force two turnovers. Against the Buffalo Bills in the AFC Divisional Round, they were able to amass five—which played a key role in the team’s ability to advance to the AFC Championship game. That was significant progress, but consistency and improvement in that manner is an absolute must. All offseason, finding a way to create more turnovers has been a focal point of Defensive Vance Coordinator, the rest of his staff, and the players. Last year, Denver was in the bottom third of the league with respect to turnover differential— sporting a -3 . Even so, the Broncos still won 14 games last year. A lot of those being one-score games. With a gauntlet of opponents to start the season, they may have a harder time finding such luck [if you want to call it that] this year. The margin for error is seemingly quite a bit thinner this year. Surtain also gave his thoughts on the approach he and his teammates can create more turnovers. “I think it’s all about intention. It’s one thing to think about turnovers, but it’s being intentional at the same time. When you’re going to the ball, you’re intentional about stripping the ball out, about intercepting the ball. I think that’s what matters because we all have the ability. We all could get a takeaway, we all could pick the ball, but it’s all about a mindset going in towards a play and actually capitalizing on those opportunities,” remarked Surtain. There’s no doubt that coming away with more takeaways on a weekly basis will be critical for the Broncos’ chances at defending their AFC West title and making another deep playoff run to chase the franchise’s fourth Lombardi Trophy. The opportunity to put an offseason’s worth of work in focus comes up on September 14th against the Chiefs in primetime. If all goes as planned, Denver will find a way to rattle Patrick Mahomes and make some big plays that can earn them a notch in the win column to start the season.
author: Christopher Hart

title: Garett Bolles speaks on the importance of Offensive Coordinator Davis Webb
summary: One of the major storylines for Broncos Country to keep their eyes on as the regular season transpires is how this year’s offense performs. Over the past few seasons, the Broncos have ranked in the middle of the pack in most aspects on that side of the ball. In order to have a successful season […]
full_text: One of the major storylines for Broncos Country to keep their eyes on as the regular season transpires is how this year’s offense performs. Over the past few seasons, the Broncos have ranked in the middle of the pack in most aspects on that side of the ball. In order to have a successful season and reach their ultimate goal, taking a big leap forward offensively is an absolute must. A key focus for the team this offseason has been consistency in the run game. To help with that, they added rookie Jonah Coleman in the fourth round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Over the past few months, the offensive line has worked on their blocking techniques and some new schematic wrinkles. To bolster their passing attack, Denver swung a big trade to bring wide receiver Jaylen Waddle into the fold. Waddle’s talent and big play dynamic should increase the overall efficiency of the offense. Moreover, his presence should help open up things for other players at the position like Courtland Sutton and second-year wideout Pat Bryant—who has been touted as a potential breakout player for the franchise in ‘26. In addition to some new faces on offense, the Mile High City has a new play caller. That’ll be Offensive Coordinator Davis Webb who will be on the sidelines getting the play to Bo Nix and his teammates. Yesterday after practice, longtime left tackle Garett Bolles gave some insight on what Webb means to him and the offense. “I love him. He’s been here for years now, so nothing’s really changed. I think just the relationship status he’s had. He’s played early on, he’s played in this league just a couple years ago, then he just retired. To have him with us and to have that player-style of coaching and knows what we go through and puts us in situations. The feelings he has, the ups and downs of the games that he understands, are tremendous,” stated Bolles. Last season, many fans were perplexed by some of the offensive playcalling. There’s no doubt that Head Coach Sean Payton has a storied career as an offensive mind. During his time in New Orleans, he put together many top offenses with Drew Brees leading the way for the Saints. However, a penchant for screen plays, a lack of dedication to the run, and some puzzling situational down decisions left many fans wanting more. In a surprise move this offseason, Payton announced at the NFL Combine he would be giving up that duty and allow Webb to call the shots. Webb is considered one of the brightest young minds in football. A former third-round pick of the New York Giants in the 2017 NFL Draft, he spent six seasons in the league before retiring in 2022. In 2023, the Broncos hired him to be their quarterbacks coach, which he continued to do alongside his duties as offense’s pass game coordinator in 2025. Ascending to Offensive Coordinator just seemed like a natural progression. In the preseason, we have seen a few glimpses and early visions of things to come. Though there is no doubt a lot of what is in store for the Broncos’ offense this season has been under wraps. That’s what makes the upcoming season a bit more exciting than most. The mystery about what the Broncos’ offense will be and the heights they can reach if they put it all together. Bolles is steadfast in his belief that with Webb leading the way on offense—the best is yet to come. “I’m super grateful for him, and I think offense hasn’t skipped a beat. I think we’re just right where we need to be, and he just brings that juice that we need and that extra juice. To have a guy like that in our corner and to get us in the right situations is tremendous for us.”
author: Christopher Hart

title: The NFL doles out vacations with its Commissioner Exempt List
summary: The NFL is rife with players tarnishing the shield (to borrow a phrase from Commissioner Roger Godell). Josh Jacobs, Keenan Allen, Terrion Arnold, and our very own Jonathan Cooper find themselves missing opportunities to step onto the field and help their teams win football games. But honestly, that’s about it. Get accused of drinking and […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 07: Jonathon Cooper #0 of the Denver Broncos celebrates a sack against Cam Ward #1 of the Tennessee Titans during the second quarter during the game at Empower Field At Mile High on September 07, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Tyler Schank/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL is rife with players tarnishing the shield (to borrow a phrase from Commissioner Roger Godell). Josh Jacobs, Keenan Allen, Terrion Arnold, and our very own Jonathan Cooper find themselves missing opportunities to step onto the field and help their teams win football games. But honestly, that’s about it. Get accused of drinking and driving, domestic abuse, kidnapping, or battery, and you get a break from playing football. During this break, you are paid your full salary. The teams that have you on their roster don’t have to spend a roster spot on you while you are on this list. On one hand, I believe in people being innocent until proven guilty. I think that is a healthy baseline from which to find some semblance of justice when an arrest has been made. On the other hand, that’s something for the justice system, and the NFL is a for-profit business. If the NFL cared about their brand or their shield or whatever cozy little word they want to use for their supposed sterling reputation, why wouldn’t they dole out actual consequences? I love the football player Jonathan Cooper. He’s worked his ass off for this team for years. I hate that he’s been charged with domestic abuse, though. If I’m a juror, I would look at the details of the case from the baseline of him being innocent. But as far as football goes, I think there should be a penalty for at least being a distraction to your team if not a problem, given that you are not available to play on game days. Instead, the NFL gives them a vacation and a pat on the butt. What do you think about this, Broncos Country? Chime in in the comments and let us know if you think it is fair palyers get a penalty and can’t play football, but are still getting paid and don’t cost a roster spot. title: Former Broncos RB Jaleel McLaughlin has signed to the Cleveland Browns’ practice squad
summary: According to 850 ESPN Cleveland’s Tony Grossi, who covers the Cleveland Browns, former Denver Broncos running back Jaleel McLaughlin has signed to the Cleveland Browns’ practice squad. McLaughlin was waived by the Broncos on Sunday and, surprisingly, went unclaimed on the waiver wire. He was not among the 17 players the Broncos signed to their […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - AUGUST 28: Jaleel McLaughlin #38 of the Denver Broncos scores a touchdown in the second quarter of a preseason game against the Minnesota Vikings at Empower Field At Mile High on August 28, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Tyler Schank/Clarkson Creative/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to 850 ESPN Cleveland’s Tony Grossi, who covers the Cleveland Browns, former Denver Broncos running back Jaleel McLaughlin has signed to the Cleveland Browns’ practice squad. Browns have signed RB Jaleel McLaughlin to their practice squad. A 4yr vet released by Denver. — Tony Grossi (@TonyGrossi) September 1, 2026 McLaughlin was waived by the Broncos on Sunday and, surprisingly, went unclaimed on the waiver wire. He was not among the 17 players the Broncos signed to their practice squad and remained unsigned until today. The former Broncos back was a standout at Notre Dame and Youngstown State, both in Ohio, so it makes sense for McLaughlin to land in Cleveland. He joined the Broncos as an undrafted free agent during the 2023 NFL Draft and quickly made a strong impression on the coaching staff. A strong performance in the preseason helped McLaughlin make the Broncos’ 53-man roster, and he became a key member of their offense moving forward. He would go on to appear in 41 games for the Broncos and total 226 rushing attempts for 1,093 yards and 3 rushing touchdowns, as well as 59 receptions for 263 yards and 4 touchdowns. After the Broncos drafted rookie Jonah Coleman in the 4th round, McLaughlin’s roster spot was in danger. He was already inactive for a handful of games last season and only saw some playing time after veteran JK Dobbins went down with an injury. As the preseason went on, it became clear that McLaughlin looked unlikely to make the team, and ultimately, according to Head Coach Sean Payton, it came down to the kicking game. “Yes, you guys all saw the preseason. All of those guys really played well. The edge goes in the kicking game, which is important. We were still able to end up with five, but I think so much of this final equation comes down to special teams as we’re trying to project a vision when it’s close.” The Broncos kept four running backs on their 53-man roster. Veteran JK Dobbins, second-year back RJ Harvey, rookie Jonah Coleman, and special teams/third down guy Tyler Badie. They also signed preseason star Cody Schrader to their practice squad. McLaughlin will join a Cleveland Browns backfield that features second-year back Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson, as well as Raheim Sanders. If an injury were to occur, it appears that McLaughlin would be the next man up for the Browns.
author: Scotty Payne

title: Mike McGlinchey gives thoughts on run game; talks mindset of offensive line as season opener approaches
summary: With the preseason over and the initial 53-man roster set, the Denver Broncos now turn their focus preparing for the gridiron battles to come in the 2026 regular season. After a 14-win campaign in 2025, the Broncos have one of the toughest schedules in the NFL. To begin their quest for a fourth Lombardi Trophy, […]
full_text: CENTENNIAL , CO - JULY 30: Mike McGlinchey (69) of the Denver Broncos speaks after practice at Broncos Park in Centennial, Colorado on Thursday, July 30, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images With the preseason over and the initial 53-man roster set, the Denver Broncos now turn their focus preparing for the gridiron battles to come in the 2026 regular season. After a 14-win campaign in 2025, the Broncos have one of the toughest schedules in the NFL. To begin their quest for a fourth Lombardi Trophy, the Broncos will face a familiar and formidable foe in the Kansas City Chiefs. It doesn’t get any bigger than going head-to-head against a division rival in primetime—and that’s what the Broncos will under the bright lights of Arrowhead Stadium on Monday, September 14th. In order to make their Super Bowl aspirations become a reality, the Broncos’ offensive line needs to be dominant. Since Head Coach Sean Payton took over, the offensive front five have went from an underperforming unit to one of the league’s best. Across various rankings and metrics, the team’s pass blocking has been superb. However, they’ve been inconsistent in the run game. Over the past two seasons, Broncos Country has witnessed what happens when the rushing attack fades late in the season. So have the coaches and players, which is why focusing on improving in that regard has been a critical point of emphasis over the past two months. Yesterday after practice, right tackle Mike McGlinchey offered his thoughts on how his coaches and teammates have approached that issue. “I think just the understanding of what techniques we’re trying to apply on which plays, which looks, which leverages. Just kind of homing in on that. We had a pretty good grasp of all that before, and like I said earlier, we’ve done it a long time together,” stated McGlinchey. “Switching a couple of the techniques in and out depending on the scheme or the play or whatever it is, I think we’ve done a good job. It’s been a great camp. Our group is ready to go, and I’m excited to see where we can go as the season unfolds,” he added. With one of the league’s toughest schedules, it will be important for the Broncos’ offensive line and rushing attack to hit the ground running. The Broncos are optimistic J.K. Dobbins can stay healthy and show the flashes he did during the first part of last season. Additionally, second-year player RJ Harvey is poised for an increased role with the offense. He was a dynamic player as a receiver out of the backfield, but struggled on occasion with his vision and hitting the right lane. To bolster their ground game, the Broncos added Washington Huskies standout Jonah Coleman in the fourth round of the 2026 NFL Draft. He was one of the best collegiate backs in this year’s class in yard per carry average, yards after contact, and touchdowns. He sports elite vision with top-end contact balance which make him tough to bring down. His addition to the squad gives Denver the deepest trio of backs they have had in a long time. Over the next two weeks, McGlinchey and his offensive line counterparts will be locked alongside the coaching staff to develop the best gameplan possible to go up against Steve Spagnoulu’s defense. “I think it’s an incredible opportunity we have for the next three days to go and compete against each other for a couple more times here, home in on some of the small details, kind of the introductions to what we want to do in the gameplan against Kansas City and then hit the ground running,” remarked McGlinchey. In their first outing last season, the team had 21 carries for just 59 yards—a lowly 2.8 yard per carry average. In the second meeting, Denver was able to carve out 128 yards on the ground and averaged 4 yards per carry. While the Broncos did much better the second time around, they still leave a lot of yards on the field and can be better. McGlinchey knows that and is confident the team can take care of business on Monday Night Football . Moreover, stressed the importance of getting better as the season progresses. “You want to be your best on Week 1, but it’s more important to be your best in Week 18. Every single week, you have to be better than the week before. It’s not going to be perfect when we first go out and start, but it’s about continuing to improve on each rep and each game as the season unfolds,” the ninth-year veteran added.

title: Sean Payton highlights two players as breakout candidates for the Broncos
summary: The Denver Broncos have their initial 53-man roster set for the 2026 season. With two weeks to go before their regular season opener on Monday Night Football against the Kansas City Chiefs, there is still some time for some moves to be made. But for now, the Broncos are confident they have the best group […]
full_text: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - MARCH 21: Sean Payton, head coach of the Founders FFC looks on during the Fanatics Flag Football Classic at BMO Stadium on March 21, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/Getty Images for for OBB Media - FANATICS STUDIOS) | Getty Images for for OBB Media - The Denver Broncos have their initial 53-man roster set for the 2026 season. With two weeks to go before their regular season opener on Monday Night Football against the Kansas City Chiefs, there is still some time for some moves to be made. But for now, the Broncos are confident they have the best group of players in two to help them make their Super Bowl aspirations come true this season. This year’s Broncos team is one loaded with continuity. Very few outside additions were made, save for the blockbuster trade that netted wide receiver Jaylen Waddle last Spring. The team is hopeful his addition will help take their aerial attack led by Bo Nix to the next level in ‘26. But in order to secure the franchise’s fourth Lombardi Trophy, the Broncos will need to see progress and development from their young core of players. Yesterday after practice, Head Coach Sean Payton was asked about players he envisions being breakout candidates for the team this year. Without hesitation, he came up with two— defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike and wide receiver Pat Bryant. “There have been a number of players. Like who’s had really good camps? We’ll start with two guys. ‘Enyi’ has played really well, Pat has played really well,” stated Payton with respect to Uwazurike and Bryant. Uwazurike is entering his fourth year with the team. With the departure of Jonathan Franklin-Myers to the Tennessee Titans in free agency, the former Iowa State Cyclones standout will be first in line to see an increase in reps. He has the size, physicality, and ability to play all across the Broncos’ front. Last season, Uwazurike put together the best season of his career. He was a force against the run while occasionally flashing pass rushing chops. If he can take the next jump—opposing offensive lines are going to struggle to combat the tenacity and versatility of Denver’s defensive trench players. On offense, Bryant routinely turned heads for his playmaking ability. He was a frequent target of praise from Payton for his jump from Year 1 to Year 2. Moreover, he even told Kay Adams that the Broncos would have a ‘hard time’ keeping him off the field this season. But it wasn’t just Payton who had great things to say about him, Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph called him ‘ the complete package ’ early on in August. With the team’s two top coaches speaking so highly of him, it’s hard not to be bullish on Bryant’s upside and potential this season. However, Payton wasn’t the only member of the team to highlight Bryant’s’ impressive offseason yesterday afternoon. Safety Talanoa Hufanga remarked he was definitely the most improved player on the roster this offseason. “I would say Pat Bryant. Bryant is a guy that came in who was more of a role player last year and doing what he was asked. He was still learning Sean’s scheme at the time. But watching his leap—because you kind of could see it as the season went last year and getting late into the year. What he’s done this camp; he’s really solidifying himself and making a name for himself in this league,” stated Hufanga. If both Uwazurike and Bryant can take the next step in their careers and be more productive this season, the Broncos’ defense and offense will certainly be better than last. They’ll get their first chance to live up to the hype in two weeks when Denver travels to Arrowhead Stadium to battle the Kansas City Chiefs in their season opener on Monday Night Football .

However, he could be subject to further discipline and suspension by the league pending the […]
full_text: Dec 21, 2025; Denver, Colorado, USA; Denver Broncos linebacker Jonathon Cooper (0) before the game at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect A few days ago, Denver Broncos edge rusher Jonathon Cooper was placed on the NFL commissioner’s exempt list. Per 9News insider Mike Klis, Cooper is expected to miss anywhere from two to six games to start the 2026 regular season. However, he could be subject to further discipline and suspension by the league pending the outcome of his trial. Yesterday at his arraignment, Cooper plead not guilty to all [five] charges from domestic violence incidents back in June. The trial dates have been set from November 10th to November 13th—with a break on November 11th in observance of Veteran’s Day. The timing of the trial coincides with the Broncos’ Week 10 BYE. After Monday’s practice, Head Coach Sean Payton provided an update on the situation. “We wait on the league. In the meantime, the difference now is he’s in the facility, he’s lifting, he’s in the meetings. He can’t practice, and then we just wait for this process to play out,” stated Payton. In five years with the Broncos, Cooper has played in 81 games with 65 starts. To date, the former seventh-round pick has 266 tackles, 33 tackles for loss, 31.5 sacks, and 63 quarterback hits. With him being sidelined for the foreseeable future, the Broncos will turn to Jonah Elliss, Que Robinson, and Dondrea Tillman to keep their pass rush strong. Over the course of the offseason, the aforementioned trio has received praise from Payton, Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph, as well as General Manager George Paton. The past two seasons, the Broncos’ defense has led the NFL in sacks. In order to make that three in a row, Elliss, Robinson, and Tillman will have to put together the best seasons of their young NFL careers.

title: Horse Tracks: Countdown to MNF begins now
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! Training camp is done, preseason is over, and cuts have been completed. The 2026 season is officially here. WooHoo! And that means the Broncos’ two-week countdown to their opening game against the Chiefs on Monday Night Football is officially on the clock. And no one in the locker room, even the […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - NOVEMBER 16: Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs hugs Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos after the game at Empower Field At Mile High on November 16, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! Training camp is done, preseason is over, and cuts have been completed. The 2026 season is officially here. WooHoo! And that means the Broncos’ two-week countdown to their opening game against the Chiefs on Monday Night Football is officially on the clock. And no one in the locker room, even the rookies, needs a refresher on what this game will mean. “We know we’re playing a really good football team, a divisional opponent, Monday Night Football ,“ said Sean Payton after the first practice with the official 2026 roster. ”It’s not like Andy [Reid] and I have to go in and give our teams a pep talk.“ But it is still just Week 1, and while the stakes are always high with a division opponent — especially one that had won the AFC Championship in five of seven appearances since 2018 until a 6-11 trainwreck season last year — keeping perspective on the season is important, Payton says. “You really focus on the process leading up to the game,” Payton said, noting the logistics of a Monday night game and an extra practice day that week. “With a Monday night game, I spend more time thinking about the schedule to make sure that we’re ramping up to play our best and it doesn’t get stale because we’re not playing on Sunday, if that makes any sense. But our players will know the significance of the first game, and I think it’s the process and the details.” Veteran offensive tackle Mike McGlinchey knows the significance as well as how important the next two weeks of prep will be. “It’s huge. I think every week is about getting better,” he said. “We’ve done that since we started training camp. This week is no exception. You don’t want to go into a game week next week off of a three-day off day and not feel like you accomplished something the week before or get better at your job.” With two weeks before kickoff, McGlinchey said this week allows the new team to hone in on some details before specifically game-planning for the Chiefs. “I think it’s an incredible opportunity we have for the next three days to go and compete against each other for a couple more times here, hone in on some of the small details, kind of the introductions to what we want to do in the gameplan against Kansas City and then hit the ground running,” he said. “You want to be your best on Week 1, but it’s more important to be your best in Week 18. full_text: Detroit Lions defensive tackle Alim McNeill (54) walks off the field after practice during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Monday, August 3, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co On Tuesday, we discussed the biggest weaknesses on the Detroit Lions’ 53-man roster .
