With the Lions going light on wide receiver, Isiah Pacheco’s injury , and some questions about the tight end depth (before Tyler Conklin re-signed ), it’s a fair point. Of course, most teams don’t have the crazy amount of top-end talent that the Lions do at the skill positions, either. Speaking of crazy talent, the Lions do have a fair amount of that. So today, let’s focus on the biggest strengths on the Lions’ 53-man roster and practice squad. Today’s Question of the Day is: Where is the Lions’ roster the strongest? My answer: If we’re talking about the best room from top to bottom, I think it would be hard to match the talent in the defensive line room. For one, they have a bunch of high-end talent that this regime has spent top resources on: First-round pick Aidan Hutchinson First-round pick Tyleik Williams Second-round pick Derrick Moore Alim McNeill, given a four-year $97 million contract On top of that, the Lions have plugged resources into the depth. Be it former second-round pick Levi Onwuzurike, free agent signing DJ Wonnum, or late-round picks in Ahmed Hassanein, Mekhi Wingo, and Skyler Gill-Howard, Detroit clearly has wanted to improve that room for years. There are still a lot of questions about the unit. Can McNeill return to pre-ACL surgery form? How will Moore look in his rookie season? Can Williams take a Year 2 jump? Who amongst those late-round picks will emerge as regular contributors? Plugging resources into a position doesn’t necessarily guarantee success, but the early returns from training camp have been promising, and the vision is clear. title: 2026 Detroit Lions have one of the youngest rosters in NFL
summary: It’s no secret that the Detroit Lions attempted to get a little younger this offseason. And as a result, they have one of the youngest rosters in the NFL. According to Philly Voice, Detroit’s initial 53-man roster had an average age of 26.0 years old, good for eighth-youngest in the NFL. Bill Speros did his […]
full_text: From left, Detroit Lions guard Miles Frazier (71), offensive lineman Larry Borom (79), and tackle Blake Miller (76) practice during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Wednesday, July 29, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co It’s no secret that the Detroit Lions attempted to get a little younger this offseason. And as a result, they have one of the youngest rosters in the NFL. According to Philly Voice, Detroit’s initial 53-man roster had an average age of 26.0 years old, good for eighth-youngest in the NFL . Bill Speros did his own calculations, and the Lions placed seventh in youngest rosters . In both rankings, the Lions were just behind the Green Bay Packers. For youth and financials reasons, the Lions said goodbye to several veteran players, including Taylor Decker, Graham Glasgow, Alex Anzalone, Amik Robertson, DJ Reader, and Kalif Raymond. Their offseason approach was to replace those players with younger, cheaper options. “I look at myself, I look at the staff, and then certainly, the players. Where can we get better?” Campbell said at the owners meetings this year. “Do we need to get younger in some areas? (I) felt like we needed to get younger in some areas.” Youth brings plenty of advantages. It’s usually more cost-efficient, and it allows you to mold players into the kind of football players you want. Young players are also in the athletic prime of their careers. But Campbell was quick to point out that adding youth comes with its challenges, too. “Certainly we’re younger than we were and there are good things about that, the youth, and then there’s things about it that we’re going to have to work through,” Campbell said. “Because as you know, it’s about—there’s going to be a learning curve for some guys, development and how fast they can go.” Still, there’s a pervasive belief that the Lions’ window is shrinking, closing, or closed. And, sure, the talented core of their players are both aging and expensive. But Detroit is clearly doing everything in their power to complement that core with young talent, as well.

summary: The Detroit Lions announced another wave of moves as they attempt to finalize their roster ahead of their Week 1 game against the New Orleans Saints. Most notably, the Lions placed running back Isiah Pacheco on injured reserve. To fill his roster spot, the Lions have re-signed tight end Tyler Conklin (as previously reported). Detroit […]
full_text: Detroit Lions running back Isiah Pacheco (10) practices during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Wednesday, July 29, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Detroit Lions announced another wave of moves as they attempt to finalize their roster ahead of their Week 1 game against the New Orleans Saints. Most notably, the Lions placed running back Isiah Pacheco on injured reserve. To fill his roster spot, the Lions have re-signed tight end Tyler Conklin (as previously reported) . Detroit also signed Dominic Lovett to fill their final spot on the practice squad. Pacheco suffered a knee injury during training camp, but during the final week of practices, coach Dan Campbell revealed that the knee injury was no longer a concern. Rather, the veteran running back was dealing with a back injury. “It’s been a little touch and go right now,” Campbell said on Thursday. “He’s had a little bit of a back (injury) and we’re hoping he’s coming out of this as of yesterday a little bit.” Pacheco is now ineligible to play or practice for the team’s first four games of the season. Detroit has four other running backs on their roster to help them weather that storm: Jahmyr Gibbs, Sione Vaki, Jacob Saylors, and Jabari Small. Lovett, the Lions’ seventh-round pick in 2025, fills Detroit’s final spot in their 16-man practice squad. He is the third receiver on the Lions’ practice squad, joining Lucky Jackson and Tom Kennedy. Detroit made the surprise decision to roster just four receivers on their 53-man roster: Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, Isaac TeSlaa, and Tay Martin. Former Lions receiver Greg Dortch was released and signed to the Bills’ practice squad. You can see the latest Lions 53-man roster and practice squads here .

title: Report: Detroit Lions to re-sign TE Tyler Conklin
summary: The Detroit Lions are bringing back tight end Tyler Conklin, according to a report from CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz. Conklin had been repping as TE3 throughout training camp, and it was a surprise to see him released last Sunday. However, with him returning to the team just a few days later, it’s plausible that this […]
full_text: Detroit Lions tight end Tyler Conklin (83), center, practices during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Monday, August 10, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Detroit Lions are bringing back tight end Tyler Conklin, according to a report from CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz. Conklin had been repping as TE3 throughout training camp, and it was a surprise to see him released last Sunday. However, with him returning to the team just a few days later, it’s plausible that this was the plan all along. We reached out to Zenitz for clarification on whether Conklin was returning to the 53-man roster or taking the Lions’ last remaining spot on the practice squad, but we didn’t hear back before we published. If Conklin is being added to the practice squad, no corresponding move would be required. He could immediately start practicing with the team and would be eligible for a game-day roster elevation in Week 1. If he is returning to the 53-man roster, that would mean the Lions would need to make a corresponding move to make room. That could be as simple as cutting another player to create space, or placing an injured player on injured reserve. Regardless of where Conklin lands on the roster, his balanced skill set adds another layer to the tight end room, giving the Lions depth, security against injury, and opening up the playbook to include more heavy sets that include multiple tight ends—including running 13 personnel (three tight end sets). “If you have three tight ends that don’t have a multiple skill set, you’re not going to do it,” offensive coordinator Drew Petzing said of running 13 personnel. “Because the key is the matchups. When you have guys that can do a lot of different things, you can start to dictate things based on what the defense wants to do.” At this time, the Lions have not confirmed the move, identified where he fits on the roster, or announced a corresponding move (if necessary), but we will keep you updated as things progress.

summary: The Detroit Lions have made their first external addition since cutting their roster down to 53 players. Klein was drafted by the Buccaneers at the end of the sixth round of the 2024 […]
full_text: DETROIT, MI - OCTOBER 20: Tampa Bay Buccaneers guard Elijah Klein (79) walks off of the field at the conclusion of the NFL football game between the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the Detroit Lions on October 20, 2025 at Ford Field in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Scott W. Grau/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Detroit Lions have made their first external addition since cutting their roster down to 53 players. According to Buccaneers beat writer Greg Auman, the Lions are signing former Tampa Bay offensive lineman Elijah Klein to their practice squad. Klein was drafted by the Buccaneers at the end of the sixth round of the 2024 NFL Draft—10 picks after the Lions selected starting left guard Christian Mahogany. Over the next two seasons, Klein would make 26 game appearances for Tampa, but just one single start. The Bucs tried Klein out at several different positions throughout his time in Tampa. In his rookie season, he split his preseason playing time at left guard, right guard, and right tackle. In 2025’s preseason, he logged snaps at left guard, right guard, and—primarily—center. This past preseason, he went back to left guard, right guard, and right tackle. His one NFL start came last season, when he played 72 snaps in a Week 3 contest against the New York Jets. While he graded out fantastically as a pass blocker (79.0 PFF grade), he struggled in the run game, earning just a 32.4 grade from PFF. His overall performance this preseason was highly dependent on his position. He earned a 74.2 grade at left guard in preseason Week 1, a 64.0 grade at right guard and right tackle in Week 2, and a 43.4 grade solely at right tackle in Week 3. In that preseason finale, he particularly struggled, allowing three pressures and two sacks over 35 snaps. It will be interesting to see where Klein fits among the Lions’ depth. Beyond Detroit’s five projected starters, they have offensive tackle Larry Borom, backup center Seth McLaughlin, reserver guard Ben Bartch, utility lineman Miles Frazier—with guard Mason Miller and tackle Devin Cochran on the practice squad. While it seems like Klein’s best fit is on the interior, the Lions are a bit thinner at tackle. We’ll see what the Lions have in store for him when he’s officially signed and in the building. You can see the rest of the Lions’ 15-man practice squad (one current vacancy) with our 2026 Detroit Lions practice squad tracker.

title: Discussion: Where is the Detroit Lions’ 53-man roster’s biggest weakness?
summary: Forming a 53-man roster is a never-ending business in the NFL. The Detroit Lions may have settled on an initial 53-man roster and 15 of their 16 practice squad players, but general manager Brad Holmes and the rest of the Lions’ personnel department are not “finished.” The job of an NFL personnel employee is never […]
full_text: Aug 29, 2026; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell looks on from the sideline during the first half against the Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Forming a 53-man roster is a never-ending business in the NFL. The Detroit Lions may have settled on an initial 53-man roster and 15 of their 16 practice squad players , but general manager Brad Holmes and the rest of the Lions’ personnel department are not “finished.” The job of an NFL personnel employee is never done. The search for upgrades at every position continues throughout the entire season. Whether it’s free agency, the waiver wire, the NFL Draft, the trade deadline, or any other time of year, there is a humongous pool of football talent available, and opportunities abound. That job never ends, because no NFL roster is perfect. There are holes, depth issues, injury insurance is needed, and new players who just don’t end up working out. The Detroit Lions are no exception to this. You better believe that this week the Lions will continue to look across the NFL landscape and at hundreds of newly available players to see if they can upgrade their team. But before they do that, they need to evaluate the status of their own roster. So today’s Question of the Day is: Where is the Lions’ 53-man roster (and practice squad) the weakest? My answer: I think my answer is the same as it was when the Lions entered training camp: cornerback. While I’ve certainly been encouraged by the play of starters D.J. Reed and Rock Ya-Sin thus far, I haven’t had that same level of optimism with the depth. Ennis Rakestraw had a very up-and-down camp with more downs than ups. Roger McCreary, who I believed to be a savvy pickup, has had flashes (particularly in the first two preseason games), but has underwhelmed compared to my previous expectations. The most promising player amongst the depth is Nick Whiteside, and Detroit didn’t even believe he played well enough to warrant a spot on the 53-man roster, risking losing him by putting him on waivers before bringing him back to the practice squad. The situation at nickel may be even more dire. While things were trending toward Christian Izien winning the starting job before his injury, that felt more like no one winning the job than anything. McCreary didn’t stand out. Rakestraw was kept on the outside. And rookie Keith Abney is clearly still adjusting to being a full-time nickel after having more success on the outside in college. Not only do I not know who the starter at nickel will be in Week 1, but I’m also not sure who the best possible reserve is, either. I say all of this not to induce panic. I’m actually a pretty big fan of the rest of this roster, and if the Lions can get plenty of healthy playing time out of Reed and Ya-Sin, maybe they’ll hold up at cornerback, too. But if I were Holmes and company, I’d certainly keep my ears and eyes open to upgrading the cornerback room. title: Packers Practice Squad Tracker 2026: Follow all the reports & signings
summary: A 53-man roster isn’t the only thing that NFL teams need to decide on this week. The league’s cutdown deadline from 90 to 53 will come and go on Sunday afternoon, and on Monday it will be time for teams to begin assembling the other major piece of their rosters: the practice squad. Over the […]
full_text: DETROIT, MI - NOVEMBER 27: Green Bay player's helmets sit on the turf during an NFL regular season Thanksgiving Day football game between the Green Bay Packers and the Detroit Lions on November 27, 2025 at Ford Field in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Scott W. Grau/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images A 53-man roster isn’t the only thing that NFL teams need to decide on this week. The league’s cutdown deadline from 90 to 53 will come and go on Sunday afternoon, and on Monday it will be time for teams to begin assembling the other major piece of their rosters: the practice squad. Over the last several years, this component of the roster has expanded greatly in significance. Not long ago, teams could carry a maximum of 8 players on the practice squad, but that number has gradually increased, now doubling to 16 (plus an additional 17th spot if a team signs a player with an international roster exemption). Furthermore, a player can be elevated from the practice squad to the active gameday roster a few times per year without a full promotion to the 53, making the unit a more functional squad of backups and injury replacements. As a result, the NFL has expanded the eligibility rules for practice squads over the years as well. Now, a team can sign players with any level of experience to the squad. At least ten of the 16 spots must be taken up by players with two or fewer years of accrued NFL experience, but that leaves up to six slots that can be filled by players of any experience level. Notably, teams cannot begin signing players to the practice squad until the league’s post-roster cut waivers are processed. That will take place at 12 Noon Central Time on Monday, when waiver claims will be awarded. After that, any players who clear waivers become free agents and are eligible to sign with any team, either to a full 53-man roster spot or to a practice squad. Still, there will be reports during cutdown day on Sunday of players whom the Packers would like to bring back for the practice squad if they do clear waivers. Here, APC will keep track of those reports through Sunday, followed by the actual signings on Monday afternoon. The Green Bay Packers have used the practice squad heavily in recent years as rules have changed, often promoting players to the gameday roster to fill in for injured players or to contribute on special teams. As such, today is an important day for general manager Brian Gutekunst and his staff, who will surely be working hard to bring back several individuals whom the Packers waived as part of Sunday’s cutdown. Building out a deep squad can have a major impact on a team’s ability to withstand challenges over the course of the season, and the quality of players on that unit could be the difference between the Packers going over or under their projected win total of 9.5, which is the current number on FanDuel sportsbook . Keep it here throughout the next day or two as the squad fills out. Reports of Practice Squad Signings The following players have reportedly agreed to sign with the Packers’ practice squad. title: Packers Discussion: What does a gameday roster look like for Green Bay?
summary: A lot of focus has been put on the Green Bay Packers’ 53-man roster recently, and I don’t blame people for looking at it — since we just had roster cutdowns. To me, though, there are really three different versions of the roster: Today, I want to talk about the 48-man game-day roster. A lot […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - AUGUST 28: Anthony Campbell #60 of the Green Bay Packers tries to block a pass from Kedon Slovis #12 of the Arizona Cardinals during the fourth quarter of a preseason game at Lambeau Field on August 28, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images A lot of focus has been put on the Green Bay Packers’ 53-man roster recently, and I don’t blame people for looking at it — since we just had roster cutdowns. To me, though, there are really three different versions of the roster: There’s the 48-man gameday roster, which is how many players can play in an actual game, including practice squad call-ups (a call-up from the practice squad just means that the team needs to make another scratch from the 53-man roster). The 53-man roster, which I’m sure you’re all familiar with. The 70-man roster, which includes the 17-man practice squad (currently, the Packers have signed 14 players to their practice squad .) Today, I want to talk about the 48-man game-day roster. A lot was made about who the Packers would or wouldn’t be subject to waivers, which is the real conversation with the 53-man roster, but I sort of want to dive deeper into who will actually suit up for Green Bay in Week 1 against the Minnesota Vikings. Let’s take it position by position, and I’ll give my ruling on whether I think the players will have shoulder pads on for the game (and the reasoning why). Quarterback Jordan Love Tyrod Taylor This is simple. The team needs two quarterbacks. Guess : All are active. Running Back MarShawn Lloyd Chris Brooks Kaleb Johnson There’s a small chance that the Packers end up making Kaleb Johnson a healthy scratch to start, as he just got to Green Bay, but his experience at Iowa in a similar running game under former Packers analyst Tim Lester should mean that he can probably hit the ground running. If they scratch him, it would be to call up Pierre Strong Jr., who has been with the team for nearly a full year now, from the practice squad while Johnson gets more comfortable with the playbook. Guess: Three are active, be it Johnson or Strong on a call-up. Receiver Christian Watson Matthew Golden Jayden Reed Bo Melton Skyy Moore J. Michael Sturdivant The Packers have been extremely rigid at the receiver position this summer, with Savion Williams, Bo Melton and Skyy Moore being the direct replacements for Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Jayden Reed, respectively. If it matters to you, Watson is the Z, Golden is the X and Reed is the slot (backups play the same roles), but Green Bay has the verbiage to move these players around all over the field. It’s less about an area of the field that a player is going to line up at, in terms of the starters being matched to the backups, and more about similar body types filling these roles. What would make it really hard for the Packers to scratch any of these receivers is their contributions on special teams. I do not doubt that a Melton could play the slot role, if asked (he’s done it in years prior), but backup slot receiver Skyy Moore is probably in line to be the team’s number one punt returner and one of the two kick returners ( especially since Williams is starting the year off on the IR-designated to return list with a high ankle sprain ). Meanwhile, Melton is a key special teams contributor (he played 185 special teams snaps in 2025, and only one other offensive player — running back Chris Brooks — played more special teams snaps than the offensive linemen, who ranked 19th on the team in special teams snaps as contributors to only the field goal protection unit. Melton is a gunner on punts and a jammer on punt returns, probably the most premium positions on special teams other than the returners and specialists. Undrafted rookie J. Michael Sturdivant is not only set to be Watson’s backup while Williams is out, but he also plays similar roles to Williams on special teams, which I’m sure helped his case for making the 53-man roster. He got some work as a gunner (not likely to start in the regular season), lead blocker on punt return (GB plays with a single guy who roams around like a linebacker at times and that role was filled by both Williams and Sturdivant, Sturdivant might start there) and as a lead blocker on kick return (Melton also plays this role). Honestly, with the way this room shakes out, I think if someone is inactive, it’s going to be Moore, as he’s a true backup slot receiver (a role the Packers have not consistently rostered), and the team may have other options in the return game. With that being said, I still think when push comes to shove, all six are active against the Vikings. Guess: All are active, but if one isn’t, it’s probably Moore. Tight End Tucker Kraft Jonnu Smith Mark Redman Josh Whyle We’re only through three positions right now, but I’m setting up an outline for a roster pinch. It will make more sense down the line, but from a numbers perspective, I don’t think that the Packers can keep four tight ends on game days right now. It doesn’t help that the team only has four players at the edge defender position, a similar body type on special teams, and they don’t let the starting off-ball linebackers contribute on teams, the other “mid skill” position type. When push comes to shove, I think the team is going to need to sit one of Jonnu Smith (new, learning playbook) or Josh Whyle, because they sort of share the same skillset of being move tight ends who don’t contribute much on special teams. Meanwhile, Mark Redman is a true Y, an inline tight end, who might be able to help as a blocker on teams. He hasn’t played in a regular-season game yet in his career, so we’re TBD on the special teams front. Guess: A move tight end is inactive, either Jonnu Smith or Josh Whyle. Offensive Line Zach Bako-Bewele Jordan Morgan Sean Rhyan Aaron Banks Jacob Monk Jager Burton Anthony Belton John Williams Donovan Jennings Travis Glover The NFL rules state that you actually only get 47 players available on gamedays, but there’s an exemption for a 48th if you carry at least eight offensive linemen. In practice, this functions as a 48-man roster, since teams don’t turn down the extra roster spot. The team will probably have to keep just eight active on gamedays, but who those eight are is tough to project right now. We think Zach Bako-Bewele and Aaron Banks will be ready to go for Week 1, but we aren’t 100 percent sure. In an ideal world, I believe the Packers think their healthy starting offensive line is Jordan Morgan, Banks, Sean Rhyan, Jacob Monk and Bako-Bewele (left to right). Maybe Jager Burton will rotate in with Banks at left guard, as head coach Matt LaFleur hasn’t been scared to do a guard rotation in years past. In this scenario, the three guys off the bench to make up the eight-man unit on gamedays would probably be Burton (guard/center), Anthony Belton (tackle/guard) and John Williams (tackle/guard/center) with Donovan Jennings (guard/“center”) and Travis Glover (tackle/guard) inactive. Obviously, though, if Banks and Bako-Bewele aren’t good to go, we’ll end up with a starting line of Morgan, Burton, Rhyan, Monk and Belton to start the year with Williams, Jennings and Glover coming off the bench. Guess: The Packers will almost certainly only keep eight offensive linemen on gamedays. Defensive Line Devonte Wyatt Karl Brooks Javon Hargrave Warren Brinson Chris McClellan Jonathan Ford Anthony Campbell The Packers have a huge defensive lineman number right now, and I fully expect them to keep just six on the gameday roster. I expect the team to play about one-third of their snaps in their base 3-4 defense, as that’s the usual rate of facing multiple tight end or back looks in the NFL right now, and the team seems to be fine with matching offensive personnel with defensive personnel (basically the number of receivers match the number of corners on the field, if you include the slot defender). With that being said, there will probably be an…

title: Packers Injuries: Updates on IR’d players and Micah Parsons
summary: The Green Bay Packers’ brass spoke to the media on Tuesday for the first time since roster cuts. The deadline also came with some injury news, as both receiver Savion Williams and edge rusher Collin Oliver were placed on the injured reserve, with a return designation, to make room for other players to be retained […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 12: Savion Williams #83 of the Green Bay Packers in action against the Cincinnati Bengals during the game at Lambeau Field on October 12, 2025 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers’ brass spoke to the media on Tuesday for the first time since roster cuts. The deadline also came with some injury news, as both receiver Savion Williams and edge rusher Collin Oliver were placed on the injured reserve, with a return designation, to make room for other players to be retained on the active roster. According to general manager Brian Gutekunst, Williams has a high ankle sprain and Oliver is dealing wih an Achilles injury. Per the GM, they should only have a four-week stint on the IR before returning to the active roster, at which point the team will need to make room for their additions to the team. Gutekunst also said that Parsons could return to practice as early as Week 3, and it will be “pretty close” on whether or not Parsons will be able to suit up in Week 5 against the Chicago Bears, the first game that he’s eligible to return for following a mandatory four-week stint on the PUP list. This fits in well with the injury timeline that we laid out back in March . Based on the Christian Watson ACL recovery timeline, Parsons should be ready to practice sometime in mid-September. For whatever it’s worth, tight end Tucker Kraft also progressed, in terms of when he got on the practice field and when he became a full participant in practice, nearly exactly at the same speed as Watson did when he recovered from his ACL tear. The final bit of injury news is that defensive lineman Warren Brinson, who did not practice with the Packers after cutdowns, has a “good chance” of playing in Week 1. Brinson injured his calf in Week 2 of the preseason during warmups, forcing Devonte Wyatt, who had not planned to play against the Denver Broncos, into action. With seven defensive linemen on the roster, the Packers won’t be short numbers at the position, even if Brinson is ruled out. Head coach Matt LaFleur added that the offensive line situation is fluid right now, as it’s not clear whether or not left guard Aaron Banks (tendinitis) or right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele (patellar tendon) can play a full 60-minute football game right now. Currently, I would expect the preferred offensive line to be Jordan Morgan, Banks, Sean Rhyan, Jacob Monk and Bako-Bewele (left to right), potentially with Jager Burton rotating in at the left guard position with Banks. If Banks and Bako-Bewele can’t go, assume that Burton will take over at left guard and Anthony Belton will play right tackle against the Minnesota Vikings in the regular-season opener. Tight end Luke Musgrave (neck) is expected to be activated off the PUP list at some point this season to contribute to the team, but there has been no hard deadline established on when he will return to practice.

title: Packers Film Review: TE Mark Redman
summary: On August 30th, the Green Bay Packers traded a 2028 7th-round pick to the Los Angeles Rams for tight end Mark Redman. Given that the Rams had eight tight ends at the start of the month, it’s no surprise they’d be open to getting rid of one of them. (As currently stands, the Rams have […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 27: Junior Colson #25 of the Los Angeles Chargers tackles Mark Redman #83 of the Los Angeles Rams on a short pass play during the first half of a preseason game at SoFi Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images On August 30th, the Green Bay Packers traded a 2028 7th-round pick to the Los Angeles Rams for tight end Mark Redman. Given that the Rams had eight tight ends at the start of the month, it’s no surprise they’d be open to getting rid of one of them. (As currently stands, the Rams have five tight ends on their 53-man roster.) Before I went to the film, I took a peek at his RAS score. Mark Redman is a TE prospect in the 2025 draft class. He scored a 6.78 RAS out of a possible 10.00. This ranked 430 out of 1332 TE from 1987 to 2025.ras.football/ras-informat… — Kent Lee Platte (Mathbomb) (@mathbomb.bsky.social) 2025-04-06T13:02:41.864Z After seeing this – a 6’6”, 263 lb TE who ran a 4.95 40 – I said to myself, “Guess he’s a Y TE who will major in blocking.” But I wanted to go to the film to see what I could find. I went through all of his snaps from the three preseason games this season. Redman ran the occasional vertical route and had a little better speed than I had anticipated, but that’s not why the Packers traded for him. His longest reception in the preseason was working as the crosser on a boot concept. So why did they trade for him? What did they see that could potentially work in this offense? Redman has one very clear strength in his game. If you put him in-line and ask him to block down the line, buddy, he’ll block down the line. If you tell Mark Redman to move a man out of a gap on a run play, he’ll do it. If you’re looking for his superpower, that’s it. He’s also no slouch in pass protection. He was asked to hold his own against the EMOL (End Man On Line) and showed that he was up for the task. If you ask him to do much more than that, the holes in his game start to show up. I showed his big reception above, but that’s more about him working within the concept than doing any solo winning. (He also had a 22-yard reception on a vertical route where he just kind of got dropped in coverage.) He gives enough of a snap at the top of his routes to provide a little separation in quick game concepts, but he’s mainly going to be operating with 10 yards of the line of scrimmage. Even his blocking is somewhat limited at the moment. I just showed a bunch of nice in-line blocking clips, but if you ask him to block on the move, he struggles lining up his man. So what do we have in terms of this offense? We have a big strong man who can move men out of their gaps in the run game and hold up on the edge in pass protection. It’s a limited skillset, but he looks to be very good at both of those things. And you can work with that, especially if you’re going back to a more zone-oriented running game (and a lot of signs are pointing to that being the case). If the only thing he could do was block, you’d be telegraphing your intentions a little too openly, but he can do enough in the passing game to not be a total burden. We saw how good he is as a down-the-line blocker, which opens him up to working the Slam route on the boot passing game (blocking down, then releasing and finding space down the line to the boot side). The Packers offense is one that can work to Redman’s strengths when he is on the field. They don’t need him to be anything he is incapable of being. He’s still young (24 years old) so there’s still room to grow within his role. His lack of speed will likely always keep him in a somewhat limited role, but an elite blocking TE with a little nuance as a route runner is a welcome addition to any offense. I certainly don’t have high hopes for production this season, but, when he’s on the field, I’m going to be watching to see what he does. title: Green Bay Packers News: It’s time for Jordan Love to ascend
summary: Jordan Love is heading into his fourth season as the Packers’ starting quarterback, but in some ways, this feels like the first season where he’ll be asked to be the face of the franchise. 2023 was very much a trial period. (Photo by Jamie Schwaberow/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jordan Love is heading into his fourth season as the Packers’ starting quarterback, but in some ways, this feels like the first season where he’ll be asked to be the face of the franchise. 2023 was very much a trial period. Jacobs carried the load on offense while Love worked his way back. In 2025, the Packers seemed poised to just try to run back the 2024 outfit — but then they traded for Micah Parsons, and the whole season became a referendum on the Parsons move. But things are different this year. Parsons is out to start the season. Jacobs is suspended. The Packers’ revamped their wide receiver room to maximize the impact of their investments there, and they’ll welcome Tucker Kraft back to the fold this year as well. It’s all perfectly set up to make Love the load-bearing piece of their offense. In short, this year we should all be living in Jordan’s world. The stage is set. title: Packers will sign Kedon Slovis to practice squad as 3rd quarterback
summary: After trading Kyle McCord away ahead of Sunday’s roster cut deadline, the Green Bay Packers have decided on which player will be their third quarterback to start the 2026 season. That player is the one who got out-dueled by McCord in last Friday’s preseason finale: former Cardinals quarterback Kedon Slovis. General manager Brian Gutekunst said […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - AUGUST 28: Kedon Slovis #12 of the Arizona Cardinals takes the field before a preseason game against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field on August 28, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images After trading Kyle McCord away ahead of Sunday’s roster cut deadline, the Green Bay Packers have decided on which player will be their third quarterback to start the 2026 season. That player is the one who got out-dueled by McCord in last Friday’s preseason finale: former Cardinals quarterback Kedon Slovis. General manager Brian Gutekunst said in his Tuesday press conference that the team plans to sign Slovis to the practice squad, making him the team’s QB3 behind Jordan Love and Tyrod Taylor. Slovis had an up-and-down game last Friday, throwing for 223 yards and a touchdown against the Packers’ deep backups. He completed 21 of 35 passes in the game, but he also threw two interceptions, both of them on short passes to the Packers’ backup edge rushers, Nyjalik Kelly and Arron Mosby. Mosby’s pick was a crucial one for the game’s result, coming just after the two-minute warning and allowing McCord and the Packers’ offense to mount a go-ahead touchdown drive to win the game 42-38. In Arizona’s four preseason games (including the Hall of Fame Game), Slovis went 39-61 passing for 434 yards, two touchdowns, and those two picks. His total passing yardage placed him third among all NFL passers in the preseason, behind Baltimore’s Joe Fagnano (509) and McCord (446). Slovis went undrafted in 2024 and signed with the Indianapolis Colts as a free agent. He was released at final cuts after that year’s preseason, then spent the entirety of his rookie season on the Houston Texans’ practice squad. After Houston cut him this time last year, the Cardinals picked him up on their practice squad to start 2025 before elevating him to the active roster in October amid an injury to starter Kyler Murray. He suited up in two games and completed one of his two pass attempts for a loss of two yards. In college, Slovis bounced around between three schools. He started for USC as a true freshman in 2019, but was injured as a junior, eventually leading to a position battle with Jaxson Dart throughout the 2021 campaign. Both players transferred after that season, with Dart going to Ole Miss and Slovis landing at Pittsburgh. Slovis started 11 games for Pitt in 2022, then transferred again, playing a fifth and final year at BYU in 2023. Slovis brings athletic ability to the quarterback room, however. He posted exceptional times on his 40-yard dash at the 2024 Combine, going 4.55 in the full run with a 1.57-second 10-yard split. Both of those times rank above the 96th percentile for quarterbacks, according to RAS , which make him intriguing as both a developmental player and as a scout-team quarterback to help the Packers’ defense prepare for athletic signal-callers. Barring an issue on his physical exam, expect Slovis’ addition to the practice squad to be finalized when Tuesday’s transactions are formally filed this afternoon.

title: Value of Things: The meaning of the 53 man roster
summary: I have to hand it to the NFL. They could market ice to an Alaskan. Little things like the release of the schedule, scouting combine, and now the final cut downs of rosters are turned into huge media events. Fans are so thirsty for football that they eat it all up. In point of fact, […]
full_text: I have to hand it to the NFL. They could market ice to an Alaskan. Little things like the release of the schedule, scouting combine, and now the final cut downs of rosters are turned into huge media events. Fans are so thirsty for football that they eat it all up. In point of fact, the final 53 is never really the final 53. Even in the last few days, we have seen some changes to the list as teams jockey to fill in holes that they saw in training camp. Those of us that comment on these things for a living get paid (as little as it might be) to read something into what is likely a whole lot of nothing. However, there were some things that raised eyebrows when the Texans initially released their roster. Obviously, the biggest stories are those that got cut that we thought would make it. One of those interesting stories was how Zay Jones and Sterling Shepard were signed to beef up the wide receiver room and them were unceremoniously cut. That’s usually how these things go as Nick Caserio and DeMeco Ryans hoped they would provide some quality depth, but apparently there wasn’t enough left in the tank to warrant keeping them around. Even the way these things are reported and covered is misleading. Over 1200 players got their walking papers and that often gets couched as players seeing their dreams die before their very eyes. This is overly dramatic. Certainly, most of those players will never see an NFL field, but a good percentage of them will land somewhere eventually. The most significant here locally is Jawhar Jordan. Three years in a row he has failed to make the final roster. Three years in a row he has been added to the practice squad. It is likely that he will see NFL action this year at some point for the third year in a row. Others will be cut here and catch on somewhere else when injuries or lack of performance calls for it. No one’s story is completely written on September 1st unless they choose for that to be the definite ending. The one big takeaway from the Texans roster was the inclusion of twelve offensive linemen. That is two or three more than just about every other team in the NFL. The whys and what fors are particularly telling here. Some of it is a temporary accounting trick as players like Braden Smith come back from injury. They don’t want to put him on IR. You only have so many spots designated for return and even that includes a mandatory four week layoff. Even all of that doesn’t fully explain what we are seeing. Clearly, the line is in a state of flux. The line that finished 2025 was not the same as the one that started. That happens naturally through attrition, but even with the Texans there is a point where things seem purposefully unsettled. It points to the fact that they probably really don’t know who their top five guys are. That is particularly telling as we enter week one. I praised Caserio in my last piece and so this serves as a bit of meat on that sandwich I mentioned earlier. Caserio is adept at a number of things. He and Ryans have built the first or second best defense in the NFL. A lot of that depends on how good the Rams will be with Aaron Donald back in the fold. I guarantee if you track every general manager that has ever lived, you will find holes in their game. Some are good at finding free agents while struggling in the draft. Others scout college talent really well, but struggle with contracts. Then, you have position groups that seem to be a hole year after year. That is the offensive line for Caserio. When we focus on that position group in particular we can’t help but feel underwhelmed. It looks like Wyatt Teller might be another miss as Keelan Rutledge is set to take over at left guard with Evan Brown winning the center job. The Caserio way seems to be to throw as much spaghetti at the wall and hope that some of it sticks. Some of it did last season. Ed Ingram was a success. Trent Brown ended up being a success for the most part. Others have failed miserably. Obviously, no real downs have been played, so it is way too early to call anyone a success or a bust for this season. We just know that the way things have been set up, there is likely to be some mixing and matching early on to find the combination that works. That also means that the first month of the season could be a slog again on the offensive side of the ball. Hope springs eternal and all of that, but the numbers clearly indicate that they really don’t know what they have yet. We can hope that the group is collectively better than it has been the last few seasons, but even that is relative. The line that took the field in November and December of last season was far better than the one that took the field in September. That might not be such a bad thing if you can bank enough early wins to secure a playoff birth.You want your best at the end of the season and it looks like that is the plan yet again, Gird your loins for some shaky football early on, but hopefully the defense will good enough to get through that first month.

full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - AUGUST 27: Davon Booth #29 of the Cleveland Browns carries the ball to score an eight-yard touchdown during the fourth quarter of a preseason game against the New England Patriots at Huntington Bank Field on August 27, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Tuesday, the Indianapolis Colts announced that the team has made practice squad moves, signing former Cleveland Browns running back Davon Booth and releasing Ulysses Bentley IV in a corresponding roster move. The team also signed offensive guard Reid Holskey to its practice squad with its remaining vacant spot, bringing its taxi-man team to the maximum of 17 players (also re-signing offensive tackle Luke Tenuta last night after he cleared league waivers). Regarding Booth, the 5,‘9”, 192 pound running back was signed as an undrafted rookie free agent out of Mississippi State by the Cleveland Browns earlier this offseason, but was waived as part of their final cuts. During 3 preseason games with the Browns, Booth had the following lines: Week 1 at Chicago: 4 carries for 53 total rushing yards (including a long run of 28 rushing yards) Week 2 vs. Buffalo: 3 carries for 16 total rushing yards; 2 receptions for -7 total receiving yards Week 3 vs. New England: 10 carries for 40 total rushing yards and a rushing touchdown; 1 reception for 4 total receiving yards Davon Booth breaks the tackle and spins into the end zone for a TD! NEvsCLE on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/PkN3q5OWFQ — NFL (@NFL) August 28, 2026 As a senior running back, he had 136 carries for 553 total rushing yards (4.1 ypc. avg.) and 7 rushing touchdowns, as well as 15 receptions for 165 total receiving yards and 2 touchdown receptions in 12 games for Mississippi State during the 2025 season. Here’s his NFL.com draft profile: Overview Compact runner lacking ideal size and athleticism for the position. Booth processes run-lane development with adequate quickness and is a solid decision-maker when it’s time to find his lane. He has straight-line speed to threaten the corner but lacks wiggle or power to create for himself. Booth carries some third-down value, but it might not be enough for him to lock down a roster spot in the pros. Due to his lack of relative size and explosion, he has a RAS of 3.68 out of a maximum of 10.0 . Given that Bentley IV had been with the Colts through two training camps and preseasons, it was a little surprising to see the Colts replace him on their practice squad—as he stood out in camp as a pass catcher. Bentley IV appeared in 1 game for the Colts last season. That being said, perhaps they felt as though Booth offered more developmental upside as a running back. Regarding Holskey ( via Colts.com ): Holskey , 6-6, 306 pounds, participated in the Denver Broncos’ 2026 offseason program and training camp. He also spent time with the New York Giants during the 2026 offseason program. In 2025, Holskey spent time on the practice squads of the Giants and Houston Texans. He participated in the Baltimore Ravens’ 2025 offseason program and training camp after originally being signed by the team as an undrafted free agent on May 5, 2025. Collegiately, Holskey started 53-of-55 career games in five seasons (2020-24) at Miami (OH). He earned First Team All-MAC honors (2024) and Second Team All-MAC recognition (2023). At any rate, the Colts currently have a new running back and interior offensive lineman on their practice squad headed into the 2026 regular season opener.

title: Keenan Allen expected to play Week 1 after OVWI arrest
summary: Keenan Allen is expected to be in the lineup for the Indianapolis Colts in Week 1 against the Baltimore Ravens. Colts general manager Chris Ballard told reporters Tuesday that Allen will play in the regular-season opener after the veteran wide receiver was arrested over the weekend for operating a vehicle while intoxicated. Ballard declined to […]
full_text: Keenan Allen is expected to be in the lineup for the Indianapolis Colts in Week 1 against the Baltimore Ravens. Colts general manager Chris Ballard told reporters Tuesday that Allen will play in the regular-season opener after the veteran wide receiver was arrested over the weekend for operating a vehicle while intoxicated. Ballard declined to get into the specifics of the incident, but said Allen will “work through the process of the legal system” and added that any team discipline would be handled internally. Allen could also still face potential discipline from the NFL under the league’s Personal Conduct Policy. “I’m not going to comment on what happened,” Ballard said. “What I’m gonna tell you is good people make mistakes. He’s a tremendous human being, give him some grace and he’ll work through the process of the legal system.” From a football standpoint, Allen’s availability is significant for a Colts offense that is already trying to build chemistry around Daniel Jones. Indianapolis added Allen to give the passing game a proven veteran presence, and with Michael Pittman Jr. no longer on the roster, his role becomes even more important. Alec Pierce, Josh Downs and Tyler Warren are all expected to be major pieces of the offense, but Allen gives the Colts a reliable route runner who can win underneath and work the middle of the field. The Colts play the Baltimore Ravens in Week 1 and they are not the kind of opponent where the Colts can afford to be short-handed or disorganized offensively. Jones needs as many trusted options as possible, especially in his first regular-season game leading the offense. Allen’s ability to separate quickly and create easy completions should help, particularly if the Colts are trying to avoid putting too much pressure on Jones early. At the same time, the situation is not something the team can just brush aside. Ballard’s public comments were supportive, but the legal process and potential league review are still ahead. For now, the immediate takeaway is clear: Allen remains on the roster, remains in the Colts’ plans, and is expected to play against the Ravens. That gives Indianapolis one fewer offensive concern before the opener, even if the larger situation is not fully resolved.

title: Did the Colts make the right move at kicker?
summary: It was one of the more intriguing but not always talked about battles in camp. It went back and forth and dipped into last season’s production to make the call. One showed a lot of promise, the other perfection. That was last year, and this is now. The race was neck and neck, but only […]
full_text: It was one of the more intriguing but not always talked about battles in camp. It went back and forth and dipped into last season’s production to make the call. One showed a lot of promise, the other perfection. That was last year, and this is now. The race was neck and neck, but only one kicker could make the 53-man roster. The Indianapolis Colts put any remaining speculation to bed as they made their choice at kicker by choosing Spencer Shrader over Blake Grupe. Why did they choose Shrader over Grupe? That’s one question. The other? Was it the right decision? Time will tell for the second question with hindsight being 20/20. For the why, while we don’t have all the details, the proof was in the pudding. When the lights turned on, one man showed up while the other went quiet. Grupe was a star in practice, but practice kicks don’t win games. He struggled close and at distance. Even one that went in needed the crossbar’s help. Meanwhile, Shrader demonstrated the ice water in his veins. He added the one piece that was missing from his game; the long ball. His leg didn’t have the necessary strength in 2025. He could convert, but the Colts had to get him closer than they would like. Having a kicker who can trot out and make 60+ yard field goals at a consistent rate is huge. It could be the difference between the playoffs and sitting at home. That’s the confidence the Colts needed. They found it in Shrader. Either man probably would have done well. Blake Grupe’s yips might not have translated over to the regular season. Then again, they might have. Shrader was the kicker before his injury. He cleaned up the deficiencies in his game and demonstrated his ability on the field. That seems like more than enough reason to feel the Colts got it right.

Practice squad formation rules Teams can begin forming their practice squads after the waiver period expires at 1 p.m. ET on Monday, August 31. The NFL will send a subsequent Personnel Notice confirming the results of the waiver process, and teams can begin signing practice squad players after receiving that notice. A player claimed off waivers cannot go directly to a practice squad. A successful waiver claim means that player goes onto the claiming team’s 53-man roster. The player must first clear waivers before becoming eligible to sign with a practice squad. A standard practice squad consists of 16 players. Teams can have a 17th player if that player qualifies for and is designated under the NFL’s International Player Pathway Program (Jacksonville may keep OL Kilian Zierer in this spot). Players who are not subject to waivers can immediately sign with another team or join a practice squad. Players with four or more accrued seasons are unrestricted free agents when released and are not subject to waivers. Players with three or fewer accrued seasons are subject to the waiver process. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Jaguars fans and fans across the country. Jaguars fans — should the team get a Parker Washington contract extension done before the regular season begins? Washington doesn’t have a ton of bargaining power now, considering his draft pedigree (sixth round) and career production (under 1,500 yards). That could soon change, though. The fourth-year pro is about to play his first full season as a starting receiver; a strong start could alter his asking price. The Jaguars should be eager to lock up Washington before he officially breaks out, but as of this writing, the 2026 NFL regular season is only eight days away. “That’s not my focus,” Washington said of contract negotiations in early August. “It’s there, and it’s a conversation, but my focus is just coming out here, and I need to make plays for Trevor [Lawrence]. So that’s my mindset, and that’s how I’m going to attack it. I’m not going to step on my agent’s toes. They can have those conversations. I’m just going to come out here and do my job.” The Jaguars won’t want to break the bank, partly because they already extended WR Jakobi Meyers and probably want to keep OT Anton Harrison around long-term. summary: The latest There’s a new third-string quarterback for the Kansas City Chiefs this season after multiple years. Rookie Garrett Nussmeier overtook Chris Oladokun on the depth chart, even earning a spot on the 53-man roster because he performed well enough to keep. After Oladokun went unsigned through the initial wave of practice-squad headlines, the veteran […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - AUGUST 28: Justin Fields #6, Garrett Nussmeier #14 and Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs talk before an NFL preseason game between the Seattle Seahawks and Kansas City Chiefs on Aug 28, 2026 at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The latest There’s a new third-string quarterback for the Kansas City Chiefs this season after multiple years. Rookie Garrett Nussmeier overtook Chris Oladokun on the depth chart, even earning a spot on the 53-man roster because he performed well enough to keep. After Oladokun went unsigned through the initial wave of practice-squad headlines, the veteran also lost his jersey number to his competitor. Kansas City Chiefs Make Telling Change After Chris Oladokun Is Removed From Active Roster | Yahoo! Sports Kansas City waived Oladokun with an injury designation Sunday, opening a spot in a quarterback room that includes Patrick Mahomes, Justin Fields and rookie Garrett Nussmeier. The Chiefs then made another change involving the quarterback: They reassigned his jersey number. Nussmeier, who wore No. 14 throughout training camp and the preseason, has now been given Oladokun’s No. 19. 2026 NFL roster cuts: Biggest moves, more for all 32 teams | ESPN Kansas City Chiefs Biggest move: Although the Chiefs didn’t have any major surprises, the biggest trend with their roster is just how many young players are featured throughout. Because the Chiefs are relying on a large rookie class, the defense has just two veterans who are older than 30: pass rusher Chris Jones (32) and linebacker Drue Tranquill (31). The same is true for the offense, with just Patrick Mahomes (30) and Travis Kelce (36). Much of the season will be about how much the rookies and fellow young players improve. — Nate Taylor Ben VanSumeren might be a bigger part of the Kansas City Chiefs’ plans than a practice squad signing would typically suggest | A to Z Sports The Chiefs want to run the ball more, and VanSumeren could be a part of that plan It’s no secret that the Chiefs want to run the ball more effectively and efficiently during the 2026 NFL season. Training camp showed this with an increased emphasis on the under-center run game with Kenneth Walker and Emmett Johnson now in the fold. The addition of VanSumeren, with only three running backs on the 53-man roster, is an eyebrow-raiser. He can block from any alignment, not just as a true fullback, but as an H-Back on the wing. Kansas City Chiefs and Hunt Family Foundation Release 2025-2026 Kingdom Impact Report | The Mothership The report features many details and highlights, including: The annual Chiefs Charity Game, the Chiefs annual preseason philanthropic initiative benefiting Kansas City-based charities and nonprofit organizations. The Hunt Family Foundation 50/50 Raffle, the Chiefs gameday fundraising initiative allowing fans the opportunity to purchase raffle tickets with half of the proceeds donated to local charities. The Hunt Family Foundation Spring Grant Cycle, which aids local organizations across the Kansas City region creating a more sustainable environment to live in for children and families. Red Friday tradition, which has benefited Ronald McDonald House Kansas City since 2014. Why Chiefs looked around country — and other sports — to get ideas for new stadium | The Kansas City Star The Tennessee Titans’ new stadium is scheduled to open next season. The Jacksonville Jaguars, Cleveland Browns, Washington Commanders, Denver Broncos and Chicago Bears also are in line for new stadiums — or, in the case of the Jaguars, a major renovation. “With all of these things, you learn from them,” Donovan said. “Some of them are really inspirational. We are in discussions with the Bears, the Broncos, the Commanders and the Browns. “We’ve spent three days at various points over the past two years in Nashville, just looking. I’ve seen that building in various stages and sort of learned what they went through, and tried to learn from mistakes and the things they discovered and incorporated.” Around the NFL Colts GM on NFL players going back to college: ‘That’s the stupidest (thing) I’ve ever heard’ | The Athletic Longtime Clemson coach Dabo Swinney, who faces LSU on Saturday, called this an “embarrassing” moment for college football. “Rarely am I at a loss for words … it’s kind of embarrassing, honestly,” Swinney said Tuesday. “It’s just embarrassing that that’s where we are. I don’t blame the kids, trying to take advantage of the system. But it’s embarrassing for college football. … “It’s a joke. We’ve got zero rules. And when you enforce rules, somebody just goes and finds a judge to say you can’t enforce those rules. Never did I feel like I’d be playing in an era like that, but that’s where we are right now.” Linebacker Kyle Van Noy, 35, signs with Vikings, reports say | ESPN Van Noy, 35, played the last three seasons with the Baltimore Ravens. He followed up a career year in 2024 with one of his most disappointing seasons last year, struggling to generate consistent pressure. He finished last campaign with just two sacks, ending a run of six straight seasons with at least five. But with the Vikings, he should provide some needed depth and experience at the edge rusher position, where Andrew Van Ginkel and Dallas Turner give Minnesota a dynamic set of starters but the rest of the depth chart is largely unproven. Steelers CB Joey Porter Jr. leaves door open to sit out season opener without new deal | NFL.com With a strong training camp and preseason, Daniels leapfrogged Jake Browning and Connor Bazelak for the No. 2 QB gig behind Baker Mayfield. “I’m proud of Jalon,” Mayfield said from his charitable event at Topgolf on Sunday, via the Tampa Bay Times. “I think he’s shown tremendous steps from the first time I met him in the offseason until now. He played his tail off. Worked hard. Worked on the things the coaches wanted to get done out of him and for him to progress with.” In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride The 5 biggest takeaways from the Chiefs’ 53-man roster reveal Kansas City currently has 12 rookies on the roster: Yes, over one-fifth of the Chiefs are first-year players, which alludes to the first bullet point of this list. This team isn’t just going young; it’s relying on many first-year players to fill out the team’s depth. It speaks to the exciting, long-term prospects of the roster — but also the fragility of the team in 2026. title: Chiefs announce signings to form initial 16-man practice squad
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs have signed 16 players to the practice squad ahead of the 2026 season. The team officially announced the initial practice squad in two waves: 12 players on Monday, then four more on Tuesday. Here are the 16 practice-squad players, subject to change after Tuesday’s waiver claims process, with a quick note […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - AUGUST 22: Andrew Armstrong #85 of the Kansas City Chiefs makes a catch against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the first half of a preseason game at Raymond James Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs have signed 16 players to the practice squad ahead of the 2026 season. The team officially announced the initial practice squad in two waves: 12 players on Monday , then four more on Tuesday . Here are the 16 practice-squad players, subject to change after Tuesday’s waiver claims process, with a quick note on each: Running backs (3) Jaydn Ott The undrafted rookie from Oklahoma only played nine snaps on offense in the preseason, all of them coming in the opening exhibition. He caught two passes for 40 yards. Kansas City may have been stashing Ott in preseason Weeks 2 and 3. Nate Carter The second-year back from Michigan State gained 60 yards over nine rushing attempts for the Atlanta Falcons last season. Editor’s note: According to the NFL Transactions Report, Carter has an exception as a member of the practice squad, meaning the team can si gn a 17th player — like recently waived defensive tackle Marcus Harris, who cleared Tuesday’s waiver wire. Editor’s note to the editor’s note: I was wrong. Per staff writer Jared Sapp, Exception appears to be the category for players with accrued service time but not veteran status. So a player will have to be released from the practice squad for Harris to be signed. Ben VanSumeren The return of the fullback features VanSumeren, a fourth-year player who began his career as a linebacker for the Philadelphia Eagles . Wide receivers (2) Andrew Armstrong Arguably the closest to the active roster of the practice-squad members, Armstrong’s family ties to Kansas City likely made it feel guaranteed that he would pick the Chiefs over the other 31 practice squads to sign with. Omari Evans The undrafted rookie from the University of Washington stood out during training camp by playing with the speed he showed at his Pro Day when he ran the 40-yard dash in 4.28 seconds. Offensive linemen (2) Pete Nygra The undrafted rookie from Louisville played 182 snaps in the preseason, according to Pro Football Focus. He lined up at left guard for 36 snaps, center for 85 snaps and right guard for 61 snaps. Ethan Driskell This preseason, the third-year player from Marshall lined up at right tackle 44 times and left tackle 54 times. He allowed three pressures over 57 pass-blocking snaps. Defensive linemen (3) Cole Brevard The undrafted rookie from the University of Texas was the heaviest player on the Chiefs’ offseason roster and will wait in the reserves while Khyiris Tonga and rookie Bryson Eason take up the spots for nose tackle on the active roster. Emmanuel Ogbah The oldest player on the practice squad didn’t show enough in the preseason to earn a roster spot — or have the team worried he’ll be signed elsewhere — but that doesn’t mean he won’t be ready to contribute later in the season if needed. Tyreke Smith The second-year player from Ohio State looked the part of a bottom-of-the-rotation edge defender in camp, and could be back in that mix for the fifth spot next preseason. Linebackers (2) Cole Christiansen Cam Jones Two Chiefs veterans who can be called up at a moment’s notice to fill in on special teams. Defensive backs (4) Tanner McAlister The fifth-year safety from Ohio State has appeared in six games over the 2023 and 2024 NFL seasons. D’Arco Perkins-McAlister There was a lot to like about this undrafted rookie, listed at 6 feet tall and 200 pounds with 32-inch arms, from the University of Louisiana-Monroe during the preseason. As an outside cornerback, he played physically at the catch point and will be one to remember next preseason. DeShon Singleton The undrafted rookie from Nebraska battled with rookie Xavier Nwankpa for arguably the final spot on the 53-man roster. Both are similarly bigger-bodied safeties who look comfortable playing over the top; Nwankpa’s special-teams experience may have been the difference. Kader Kohou Kohou is an easy call-up should any of the Chiefs’ slot defenders — L’Jarius Sneed, Christian Roland-Wallace, rookie Jadon Canady — get injured, especially now that Kevin Knowles, who initially made the 53-man roster, was claimed by the Tampa Bay Buccaneer s after being waived on Monday.

title: The 5 biggest takeaways from the Chiefs’ 53-man roster reveal
summary: The dust is still settling on the chaos of NFL cutdown day, when the Kansas City Chiefs and 31 other NFL teams must cut down 90-man rosters to 53 players to begin the season. The Chiefs’ initial 53-man roster was announced on Sunday evening and has been adjusted a couple of times since. The practice […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 15: Cornerback Jadon Canady #22 of the Kansas City Chiefs and running back Emmett Johnson #10 of the Kansas City Chiefs run onto the field prior to an NFL preseason game against the Los Angeles Rams at Arrowhead Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images The dust is still settling on the chaos of NFL cutdown day, when the Kansas City Chiefs and 31 other NFL teams must cut down 90-man rosters to 53 players to begin the season. The Chiefs’ initial 53-man roster was announced on Sunday evening and has been adjusted a couple of times since. The practice squad is still being finalized , with the season’s opening game now under two weeks away. We’ve had time to digest the moves Kansas City made, so let’s sort out the top takeaways: 1. The Chiefs have one of the NFL’s youngest rosters NFL Oldest & Youngest Teams Post 53-Man Roster Deadline Oldest Team – @AtlantaFalcons Youngest Team – @MiamiDolphins Oldest Player – Aaron Rodgers Youngest Player – Keldric Faulk Full Story & Analysis In Comments 🔽 pic.twitter.com/DsuURSm4NQ — Bill Speros (@billsperos) August 31, 2026 According to Bill Speros of Bookies.com , the Chiefs’ initial 53-man roster was the third-youngest in the NFL. That was the case before the team waived two second-year players in favor of two rookies. Arrowhead Pride user Dandridge pointed this out in The Feed on Sunday evening : The biggest standout to me is Andy going against form and relying so heavily on youthful, inexperienced, potential for depth instead of proven, low-ceiling veterans. On the flip side, AFC West foes like the Denver Broncos and Los Angeles Chargers rank among the top 7 oldest rosters. The Chiefs will be looking to reclaim the throne in the division with the youngest roster of the bunch. 2. The Chiefs’ backfield could be a one-two punch One of the most surprising cuts of the weekend was the Chiefs’ decision to waive veteran running back Emari Demercado, who was claimed by the Dallas Cowboys on the waiver wire. This is notable because of Demercado’s experience compared to the backups behind lead running back Kenneth Walker. Earlier in the offseason, Demercado told local media that pass blocking was his niche in the NFL, and Kansas City — with a heightened sense of protecting quarterback Patrick Mahomes — was willing to let that go. It speaks to the trust in rookie running back Emmett Johnson and second-year back Brashard Smith, especially Johnson. To my eye, Smith has improved on the fundamentals of the position, but he still lacks the strength to run between the tackles and pick up pass rushers one-on-one consistently throughout a game. On the other hand, Johnson is a natural running back in all facets and has proven it in the preseason. There’s a chance Walker and Johnson are splitting the majority of the work, whether it’s a run or pass play, and Smith plays less often as a change-of-pace back in the third-wheel position. 3. The ‘Esa Pole’ project has concluded From The Feed, by Big RiverDude: Disappointed in Pole — more disappointed in his performance this preseason than in his not making the team. Was expecting him to take a significant step forward this year, but just didn’t seem to happen. When the Chiefs traded for Baltimore Ravens rookie left tackle Diego Pounds last week, alarm bells went off in Chiefs Kingdom about that position. Local media quieted the concerns about left tackle Josh Simmons’ (Back) situation being related to the move. It turns out that second-year left tackle Esa Pole had just overstayed his welcome. On Sunday, he was cut for the second straight preseason; he elected to join the Washington Commanders ’ practice squad rather than returning to Kansas City. Some players are gamers, showing up when the lights are on but not meeting that performance level in practice. Pole filled in admirably last season on the blind side, but it’s clear the team was not impressed with how he built on that this offseason. 4. The wide receiver room feels deeper One of the most polarizing moves of the weekend was the Chiefs’ roster maneuvering at the bottom of the receiver depth chart. With six players in the group, starting kick and punt returner Nikko Remigio beat out second-year wideout Andrew Armstrong for the last spot. Armstrong cleared waivers and returned to Kansas City’s practice squad on Monday. So it’s a happy ending (for now) for both sides of the discussion surrounding the roster battle. User Mikek1989 put it best in The Feed : The fact the majority of people are going to complain about our WR6-7 battle speaks about where this team is. KC is freakin BACK BABY!! To my eye, Armstrong put together a strong enough camp to warrant a roster spot, but that’s why I’m just a blogger. General manager Brett Veach knew he would retain Armstrong, giving the team a quality depth option should the Chiefs need to call up the 6-foot-4 receiver who built chemistry with Mahomes during training camp due to injuries at the position. It’s also worth noting that both wide receivers Jalen Royals and rookie Cyrus Allen have shown enough to feel confident in as backups to the projected starting three. If either or both had not impressed, Armstrong might have been a stronger consideration to keep. 5. The Chiefs have a big rookie class From The Feed, by Old Perfesser: This may be the best draft class I’ve seen for the Chiefs–ever. Kansas City currently has 12 rookies on the roster: CB Mansoor Delane DT Peter Woods DE R Mason Thomas CB Jadon Canady RB Emmett Johnson WR Cyrus Allen QB Garrett Nussmeier OL Kahlil Benson OL Diego Pounds DT Bryson Eason DE Jack Pyburn S Xavier Nwankpa Yes, over one-fifth of the Chiefs are first-year players, which alludes to the first bullet point of this list. This team isn’t just going young; it’s relying on many first-year players to fill out the team’s depth. It speaks to the exciting, long-term prospects of the roster — but also the fragility of the team in 2026. Kansas City doesn’t have the reliable veterans on the fringes of the team to fall back on for the “next-man-up mentality.” It remains to be seen whether that is a positive or negative change to a long-time trend for the Chiefs under head coach Andy Reid and defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo.

full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - FEBRUARY 06: Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs and AFC records a video message on a sideline during the 2022 NFL Pro Bowl against the NFC at Allegiant Stadium on February 06, 2022 in Las Vegas, Nevada. title: Chargers duo named one of the top PFF pass rush duos in history
summary: The late 2010s were a fun time to watch the Chargers pass rush. Every time Joey Bosa and Melvin Ingram were healthy and on the field together, it was a good time. So good, in fact, that the duo was just named as one of Pro Football Focus’ top pass-rushing duo of their platform’s history. […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - DECEMBER 01: Phillip Lindsay #30 of the Denver Broncos is tackled by Joey Bosa #97 and Melvin Ingram III #54 of the Los Angeles Chargers in the third quarter at Empower Field at Mile High on December 01, 2019 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Matthew Stockman/Getty Images) | Getty Images The late 2010s were a fun time to watch the Chargers pass rush. Every time Joey Bosa and Melvin Ingram were healthy and on the field together, it was a good time. So good, in fact, that the duo was just named as one of Pro Football Focus’ top pass-rushing duo of their platform’s history. Now, even as someone who could admit he may be remembering those years as better as they were, I would not have been shocked to see them not make it. However, apparently my mind isn’t all that scrambled. “ Prior to numerous injuries, Bosa was regularly one of the most dominant edge defenders in the NFL, which only makes it fitting for him and Ingram to make this list,“ says PFF analyst Bradley Locker. ‘‘In 2017, each was in the top seven in PFF pass-rush grade and the top eight for pass-rush win rate for any eligible defensive lineman. By pass-rush grade alone, the Chargers featured two of the four best edge rushers in the league that season. ” “ Bosa netted 75 pressures and 13 sacks, while Ingram posted 76 pressures and 11 sacks himself. While their collective work didn’t help Los Angeles reach the playoffs that year, it lives on as one of the premier teammate pass-rushing seasons in recent memory. ” In five years as teammates, Bosa and Ingram combined to record 61.5 sacks, buoyed mainly by the aforementioned 23 total sacks between the two in 2017. Two other times, the duo combined for 18+ sacks with 18.5 during both the 2016 and 2019 campaigns. That 61.5 sacks total between them during a five-year stretch may seem low to you, and it is, due to a goose egg Ingram laid in 2020 and the numerous injuries him and Bosa had that cost the pair 32 total games. But hey, we’ll always have that 2017 season, right?

title: Why Quentin Johnston is ‘excited’ about Chargers offense
summary: Los Angeles Chargers wide receiver Quentin Johnston is going into his fourth NFL season, where the hype may be higher than it has ever been before. Johnston and the Chargers have been building momentum all offseason long as they learn from new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, who served as head coach of the Miami Dolphins […]
full_text: May 12, 2023; Costa Mesa, CA, USA; Los Angeles Chargers receiver Quentin Johnston (1) during rookie minicamp at Hoag Performance Center. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con Los Angeles Chargers wide receiver Quentin Johnston is going into his fourth NFL season, where the hype may be higher than it has ever been before. Johnston and the Chargers have been building momentum all offseason long as they learn from new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, who served as head coach of the Miami Dolphins for the last four seasons. Quarterback Justin Herbert is responding well to McDaniel’s system, which should allow Johnston and the other wide receivers to flourish. “I’m glad I got a quarterback that can get the ball out there like that. I always still go back at film and get amazed at some of the passes and how far he throws the ball. Fun to be a part of,” Johnston said via the team’s website . “We got a supreme quarterback, supreme offensive coordinator and we got all the pieces that fit in and mesh well. I’m excited for us.” During the team’s final preseason game against the Los Angeles Rams, Herbert found Johnston for a 65-yard touchdown. That served as a preview for what could be coming with the Chargers offense this season. After scoring just three points in their wild card round game against the New England Patriots back in January, the Chargers knew they needed to make some changes when it came to the offense. By inserting McDaniel into the coaching staff, the Chargers were able to bring a new perspective that could result in more firepower for the unit. It might take some time throughout the first part of the season, but if the Chargers’ offense can click quickly, they should have a chance to do better than they did last season. BFTB community, how do you feel about the offense going into the season? Let us know in the comments section below.
