The Rams defeated the Cardinals 45-17. (Photo by Chris Coduto/Getty Images) | Getty Images Owner of the Los Angeles Rams, Stan Kroenke, is now the owner of MLB’s Los Angeles Angels, and the announcement of the purchase was made just about one week before the Rams kickoff their 2026 season against the San Francisco 49ers in Australia. A season where the Rams are heavily expected to make a run at the Super Bowl. How busy must you be to be Kroenke? As his NFL team was focused on trading for Myles Garrett and then figuring out how to fit Aaron Donald back into the equation, Kroenke was figuring out how to buy the Angels and make baseball fans around the country happier. The expectation is that Kroenke and the Angels will find success, as so many other of his teams (like the Rams) have. We’ll see. It’s major sports news, and it in about one week when the NFL kicks off, that will be major sports news too. Never a dull moment in L.A. or the world of sports. LA Rams owner Kroenke reaches agreement to buy Angels (mlb.com) “It ends Moreno’s 23-year tenure as owner since he bought the club in 2003, but he will remain a minority owner with an undisclosed share. The Angels had early success under his ownership, winning six division titles (2004-05, ’07-09 and ’14) but have struggled over the last decade. They haven’t had a winning record since 2015 and currently have a 53-85 record that’s tied for the worst mark in the AL. “The Angels are a storied franchise anchored in a great market,” Kroenke said in a statement released by both the Angels and Kroenke Sports & Entertainment. “We look forward to an exciting future with the Angels organization.” Mike Trout isn’t ditching Eagles fandom despite Rams owner buying Angels (sports.yah00) “ Los Angeles Rams owner Stan Kroenke has agreed to buy the Angels , with the monumental purchase going through Kroenke Sports & Entertainment for a valuation of $4 billion. Assuming Trout stays with the ballclub through the remainder of his contract — expires after the 2030 season — he will probably get to know the new man in charge pretty well. The three-time American League MVP has no intention of abandoning the Eagles, though. “Mike Trout said he’s too diehard of an Eagles fan to change allegiances and become a Rams fan with Stan Kroenke buying the team,” MLB.com’s Rhett Bollinger posted on X. “But said that he would go support the Rams at a home game as long as they weren’t playing the Eagles.” Why Your Team Sucks 2026: Los Angeles Rams (defector) “The Rams were SO CLOSE to winning the NFC West, getting a first-round bye and home-field advantage throughout the playoffs, and being served up a birthday cake of a Patriots team in the Super Bowl—only for the division-rival Seahawks to snatch all of that away from them and win the championship. Those seven weeks are collectively the most delighted I have ever been as a Seahawks fan. A Super Bowl win may be the mountaintop, but I am a hater first and foremost, and the combined late-season failures of the Rams and 49ers will keep my wicked black heart pumping poison long after my brain dies. Friends, I’m about to tell you all about how the Rams faceplanted, and I am GIDDY. I get to live it all again.“ The LA Rams are either winning the Super Bowl or facing a massive disappointment with almost no margin for error (atozsports) “As Ben Fox pointed out on X, every team over the past 30 years that entered Week 1 with +500 or better odds to win the Super Bowl outright has failed to hoist the Lombardi Trophy. That has happened 20 times. Those short favorites have gone 0-for-20 winning the ring. The list reads like a graveyard of dominant rosters. It includes the 2024, 2021, and 2020 Chiefs, the 2019 and 2017 Patriots, the 2015 and 2014 Seahawks, the 2011, 2009, 2008, and 2007 Patriots, a three-way tie in 2005 between Indianapolis, New England, and Philadelphia, the 2004 Eagles, the 2001 and 2002 St. Louis Rams, the 2000 St. Louis Rams, the 1999 Vikings, the 1998 and 1997 Packers, and the 1996 49ers.“ Rams rumors: Aaron Donald’s mysterious Rams Week 1 status less likely (sports.yahoo) “ESPN’s Dan Graziano reported Tuesday that a later debut currently appears more likely. “I would say, based on everything I’ve been told, a Week 2 or 3 debut looks more likely than Week 1,” Graziano said on “NFL Live.” “But again, it’s still on the table.” And keeping it on the table may have some value.“ Puka Nacua’s ex-girlfriend makes new abuse claim as Rams await suspension verdict: ‘What broke me’ (nypost) “Puka Nacua’s off-the-field worries could be getting worse. But now Nacua’s ex-girlfriend Hallie Aiono has made some concerning claims about elements of her relationship with him during a TikTok video that was published on Sunday night.“ Running Back Market Rebounds, Todd Gurley Has Thoughts (sports.yahoo) “” I’m definitely happy for them boys and what they’re doing ,” Gurley said on the “4th and South” podcast. “But I’m still a little bit pissed off at the same time because you got somebody that’s half the player making double the amount. title: 3 Rams who could crack ESPN’s 2027 top 100 rankings
summary: The Los Angeles Rams saw four players — Myles Garrett, Puka Nacua, Matthew Stafford and Trent McDuffie — make ESPN’s predictions for the top 100 players in 2026. With the Rams stockpiled with talent at nearly every position, who else could join them in next year’s rankings? Stafford, Nacua and Garrett were included in the […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - JANUARY 25: Kamren Kinchens #26 of the Los Angeles Rams lines up during an NFC Championship NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on January 25, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams saw four players — Myles Garrett , Puka Nacua , Matthew Stafford and Trent McDuffie — make ESPN’s predictions for the top 100 players in 2026 . With the Rams stockpiled with talent at nearly every position, who else could join them in next year’s rankings? Stafford, Nacua and Garrett were included in the top 10 of the rankings, with the reigning Defensive Player of the Year at No. 1. LA might’ve had five players featured, but the unretired Aaron Donald was ineligible. Either way, the Rams are more than their biggest names. Since Los Angeles will be prominently featured in primetime this season, several players who don’t get as much recognition can make a greater name for themselves. Here are three players with the most realistic chances of making ESPN’s 2027 rankings with a strong campaign this year. Kamren Kinchens Earlier this offseason, PFF tabbed Kinchens as one of 10 players who could earn All-Pro honors for the first time in 2026. All-Pro recognition is entirely possible for the third-year defender, who has played in all 39 games of his Rams career since being selected in the 2024 NFL draft. He is due for a breakout season after finishing fourth on the team in total tackles with 84. According to Pro Football Reference , his yards after catch (YAC) allowed dropped from 150 in 2024 to 82 last season, while his missed tackle percentage fell from 9.5% to 6.7%. His tackling notably improved from Year 1 to Year 2, even though his interception total was cut in half from four to two. Despite that, Kinchens can still get a key pick when the opportunity arises. 2 INTs for Kamren Kinchens! 3 INTs for the Rams! SEAvsLAR on FOX/FOX One https://t.co/HkKw7uXVnt pic.twitter.com/aHfIhhew5A — NFL (@NFL) November 16, 2025 With the Rams set to have a more potent pass rush in ‘26, expect quarterbacks to rush the ball out of their hands, which bodes well for Kinchens’ chances of increasing his interception total. Byron Young Young is perhaps the most underappreciated player on the team. He was the only defender to amass double-digit sacks last season and has always been a strong pass rusher. Through his first three seasons, he has 27.5 sacks in 51 games played, averaging around nine sacks per season. The Tennessee product is more than just a sack master. Even when he doesn’t get to opposing quarterbacks, they still feel his presence. Young led the team with 29 QB hits, which were two more than Jared Verse. He also led the team with 12 tackles for loss. Want more evidence of his dominance? During his rookie season in 2023 , when he last shared the field with AD, he finished with 19 QB hits, only four behind the future Hall of Famer. Hopefully, Donald’s return won’t limit Young’s time on the field because he’s been one of the most consistent members of the defense since joining the Rams. Young doesn’t have many accolades to his name yet, but that might change if he remains his typical productive self. Kobie Turner Another underappreciated member of the defense, though not to the extent of Young. Turner has also been one of the team’s most consistent defensive players. He has 24 sacks through his first three seasons and has generally been close to the top of many team statistical categories. Last season, he finished third on LA in sacks (7.0), TFLs (9) and QB hits (14). Like Young, he is another defender who manages to make quarterbacks squirm, even if he doesn’t always get there. The Conductor has been an excellent pass rusher and playmaker during his brief Rams tenure. He could post even greater stats with Garrett and Donald expected to garner much of the attention, allowing him to slip through the cracks.

title: Aaron Donald returns to Rams (salary cap)
summary: Aaron Donald has returned to the Los Angeles Rams … balance sheet. The un-retired defensive tackle is now an official member of the 2026 active player salary cap and Overthecap.com has the numbers to explain how much Donald is going to cost the Rams this season. Donald’s addition, with no corresponding moves yet, leaves L.A. […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 03: Defensive tackle Aaron Donald #99 (L) and quarterback Matthew Stafford #9 of the Los Angeles Rams wait to take the field before playing against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium on October 03, 2022 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Aaron Donald has returned to the Los Angeles Rams … balance sheet. The un-retired defensive tackle is now an official member of the 2026 active player salary cap and Overthecap.com has the numbers to explain how much Donald is going to cost the Rams this season. Donald’s addition, with no corresponding moves yet, leaves L.A. ranked 30th in available salary cap, potentially necessitating more cap moves in case the Rams feel the need to add even more players this season. It would actually be more surprising if the Rams stopped making additions than if they made another blockbuster move. Remember adding Odell Beckham, Jr. and Von Miller in the middle of the 2021 season ? Donald has a $10 million cap hit Before his return, there was the matter of the $30 million Donald had left on the contract when he retired, which the Rams have been able to skirt by structuring the deal like this : $10 million base salary for 2026 (all counts against the cap) $10 million roster bonuses for 15 games $10 million in incentives It adds up to $30 million and Albert Breer of SI believes that barring unforeseen setbacks, it should be easy for Donald to get at least $25 million of that. Roster bonuses should count in the current year’s salary cap, so if Donald earns $10 million, the Rams will need to find that money. Incentives depend if they’re classified as “likely to be earned” or “not likely to be earned” and Breer is suggesting that they’re likely to be earned. Those also count on the current year’s salary cap. Therefore, if Donald makes another $20 million in 2026, the Rams need to find $20 million. The Rams have $5.8 million in salary cap space According to OTC, L.A. is down to only $5.8 million in cap space . The easiest way to create space would be restructuring contracts of players with multiple years left, or extending players who are in a contract year. There are quite a few of those. If the OTC calculator is correct, the Rams could save over $11 million by restructuring Matthew Stafford’s contract. Stafford is taking his career year to year at this point, so it is somewhat of a small risk. The best impending free agent to extend would ironically be A.J. Jackson, who carries an $18 million base salary in the final year of his contract. Ironic because Jackson could still be suspended this year. But $18 million is a lot of money to move around, if the Rams need to do that. Other free agents, like Puka Nacua, don’t make that much. Nacua only has a $5.7 million base salary, so an extension wouldn’t help . For now, the Rams are only paying Donald $10 million. That’s certain to change. Vote in this week’s Feed Post React Poll: Who benefits the most from AD return? 2-game exemption Donald was granted a 2-game commissioner’s exemption, meaning he won’t have to be added to the roster until Week 3. That’s also why his $10 million per-game roster bonus is only 15 games. But soon Aaron Donald will be on the Rams roster, and on the field, perhaps as soon as Week 1. That’s exciting for the defense, but still costly to the salary cap. We don’t know how much it will cost by the end, but we do know that right now he’s kind of a discount.

title: Matthew Stafford ranked No. 4 on NFL Top 100 players of 2026
summary: Matthew Stafford has officially found his place on the NFL Top 100 Players of 2026, with the Los Angeles Rams quarterback coming in at No. 4 overall. While Stafford’s exact ranking is the headline, his placement is also notable when compared to where he appeared on last year’s list. Stafford was ranked No. 59 overall […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - JANUARY 10: Matthew Stafford #9 of the Los Angeles Rams celebrates after a touchdown during the first quarter of an NFL wild card playoff game against the Carolina Panthers at Bank of America Stadium on January 10, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Matthew Stafford has officially found his place on the NFL Top 100 Players of 2026, with the Los Angeles Rams quarterback coming in at No. 4 overall. Leading the way🫡 pic.twitter.com/WoI3zcz8dd — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) September 1, 2026 While Stafford’s exact ranking is the headline, his placement is also notable when compared to where he appeared on last year’s list. Stafford was ranked No. 59 overall in the 2025 edition of the NFL Top 100, making his 2026 ranking a significant reflection of the quarterback’s resurgence. The veteran quarterback turned back the clock during the 2025 season, reminding the NFL why he has been considered one of the league’s most talented passers throughout his career. Stafford’s ability to consistently make difficult throws, operate Sean McVay’s offense and deliver in high-pressure situations helped establish him as one of the most important pieces of the Rams’ offense. His climb up the NFL Top 100 also comes during a period in which Los Angeles has accumulated an impressive collection of highly regarded players. Puka Nacua has already been announced at No. 7 overall , giving the Rams one of the highest-ranked offensive players on the entire list. Nacua’s placement represents a massive jump from his No. 41 ranking in 2025 and further demonstrates how quickly he has established himself as one of the NFL’s elite receivers. Nacua’s rise also provides some context for Stafford’s ranking. The quarterback has played a major role in helping Nacua become one of the league’s most productive offensive weapons, and the connection between the two has become a central part of Los Angeles’ offensive identity. The Rams also have another player among the top five, with Myles Garrett receiving an elite placement following his arrival in Los Angeles. Garrett’s presence alongside Stafford and Nacua gives the Rams three players ranked among the upper echelon of the NFL Top 100 . For Stafford, however, this ranking is about more than simply adding another accolade to his résumé. It represents the recognition that his level of play remains among the best in the NFL despite being one of the league’s most experienced quarterbacks. At this stage of his career, Stafford has already accomplished nearly everything a quarterback can accomplish. Yet his latest NFL Top 100 ranking serves as another reminder that the veteran isn’t simply hanging around the league — he remains one of its most respected and impactful players.

title: Rams were surprised by Aaron Donald’s return
summary: The Los Angeles Rams and their staff made moves for Trent McDuffie, Myles Garrett and more because it was what they thought were the best moves for the team. They apparently did not make these moves thinking Aaron Donald would come out of retirement to join a “super team”. That was an added bonus and […]
full_text: DETROIT, MI - JANUARY 14: Los Angeles Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald (99) walks off of the field at the conclusion of an NFL NFC Wild Card playoff football game between the Los Angeles Rams and the Detroit Lions on January 14, 2024 at Ford Field in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Scott W. Grau/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams and their staff made moves for Trent McDuffie, Myles Garrett and more because it was what they thought were the best moves for the team. They apparently did not make these moves thinking Aaron Donald would come out of retirement to join a “super team” . That was an added bonus and a welcomed surprise . Now, for the past few months and weeks, yes, it was known that AD may be making a comeback, but when the Rams made their initial offseason moves back in the Winter/Spring, Donald was not part of the plan. Donald was happily retired. Once the door opened even a little for AD to make a return, conversations were had, plans were made and actions was taken by L.A. and Donald. Maybe it’s all a lie, and Donald has been orchestrating L.A.‘s offseason this whole time, crafting the team he wanted to play with whether they win it all or not. However, according to the Rams, this all just happened. Funny how life works out sometimes. Trent McDuffie never imagined playing with Myles Garrett, Aaron Donald: ‘Would’ve said you’re lying’ (nfl.com) “A stunning trio of moves that McDuffie would never have predicted. “I probably would’ve said you’re lying, for real,” McDuffie told Andrew Siciliano during an interview that will air during Tuesday’s “The NFL Report”, which streams at 7 p.m. ET on NFL Channel . “There’s no way you can get me. There’s no way you can get Myles. There’s no way you can get A.D. But, hey, hat off to (general manager) Les [Snead]. Hat off to (head coach) Sean [McVay]. Those guys are masterminds and they did it.” Aaron Donald’s absence from Monday’s practice “part of the plan all along” (sports.yah00) “I wouldn’t rule anything out yet,” McVay said, via the team’s website. “Sometimes when you put unnecessary parameters or guidelines on something, you can skew things. But what I think what’s really good for us is if he’s able to go, great, if not, that’s kind of how we’ve been operating as is, and guys have done an excellent job of being able to do some really cool stuff in the meantime. So, if he’s not ready, and that’s not what’s best for him and for the team, (we) absolutely wouldn’t have him play in Australia.” Donald’s participation as well as that of defensive end Myles Garrett will continue to be closely monitored as the football world waits to find out when we’ll see the duo on the field at the same time.“ Rams sign 17 players to initial 2026 practice squad (therams.com) “WOODLAND HILLS, Calif. — The Rams have signed 17 players to their initial practice squad on Monday for the 2026 season following the announcement of their initial 53-man roster on Sunday, utilizing the 17th spot for an international player. Here is Los Angeles’ initial practice squad:” Aaron Donald’s Los Angeles Rams return creates the NFL’s most fascinating experiment, potentially ever (atozsports) “The conversation around Donald’s return inevitably gravitates toward percentages. If he is only 60% of what he once was, how useful is that version of the player? The answer depends entirely on what baseline you are measuring against. Here is where the Rams’ roster construction changes the equation. For the first time in Aaron Donald’s football career, dating back to his days at Pittsburgh and through his entire tenure with the Rams, he will not be the primary target of opposing offensive lines.“ Rams linebackers have an opportunity to prove themselves with all eyes watching (ramblinfan) “That gives LA’s linebackers an opportunity, though. Led by Nate Landman and Omar Speights, the group has an open invitation to take their game to another level, proving to the NFL world that they are far from a weak link. Both Landman and Speights became full-time starters last season, and they are reprising those roles in 2026. Landman proved to be a high-value free-agent signing a year ago, having a career campaign with 132 tackles, eight tackles for loss, 2.5 sacks, and one interception. Speights, a 2024 undrafted signee, added 85 tackles.“ Rams believe in Aaron Donald because they’ve seen this story before (ramblinfan) “Forget what you think you know about the former All-Pro defensive tackle. He doesn’t need to reinstate his prime. Donald merely has to be in the right position to make plays to help the Rams win games. Rams know what Aaron Donald is capable of, and so does he He overcame size concerns to dominate. Draft analysts were brutally harsh in writing up Donald’s profile . Noting his size and weight (just under 6-foot-1 and 285 pounds), they waved off general managers with catch phrases like ‘undersized’ and ‘overpowered’. And yet, Rams GM Les Snead took him with the 13th pick in 2014.“ Fans had jokes about the Rams naming way too many captains (larrybrownsports) “Fans couldn’t help but laugh at the Rams handing out captaincy like cars on that one episode of Oprah. One fan hilariously compared it to a bride being indecisive about which of her friends to name as bridesmaids.” Super Bowl Odds for Every NFL Team in 2026 Season (Rams Enter as Favorites, 14 Teams 20/1 or Better) (si.com) “Last year’s champions – the Seattle Seahawks – are fourth in the odds to win the Super Bowl (+1100), a sign that oddsmakers expect a big season once again from Sam Darnold and Co. Seattle doesn’t have the best odds to win the Super Bowl in its own division, though, as the Los Angeles Rams (+550) enter the season as the favorite to win Super Bowl LXI. The Rams made the NFC title game in the 2025 season before they lost to the Seahawks, and they added two defensive superstars in Trent McDuffie and Myles Garrett (the reigning Defensive Player of the Year) to their roster in the offseason. “ Sean McVay, Kobie Turner, Kyren Williams & more Rams players and coaches join fans at this year’s Kickoff for Charity (therams.com) “Watch a recap of the Los Angeles Rams’ annual Kickoff for Charity event presented by UNIFY Financial Credit Union. Fans watched an exclusive interview between Rams legend Andrew Whitworth and head coach Sean McVay, then met wide receiver Davante Adams, quarterback Matthew Stafford, defensive end Kobie Turner, running back Kyren Williams & more Rams players.” 2026 NFL Preseason Week 3 rookie grades: Ravens punter thriving; did Texans find undrafted gem? (nfl.com) “NFL rookies had some time to get acclimated to their new cities and teammates. Now, we all get to see how these newcomers handle the best competition they’ve ever faced. Below, I’ve graded the performance of one rookie from each of the past week’s 16 preseason contests . Some of these players are well-known to football fans, while others are trying to make names for themselves on the professional gridiron. These evaluations are not predictions of how players will fare in this upcoming season, nor are they long-term career projections. Each mark simply takes stock of how the rookie played in Week 3 of the 2026 preseason.“ Comment of the Day: “Joe Milton was cut by the Cowboys. One of our posters said over and over that we should’ve drafted him because “arm talent is important”. Well, it is, but it’s also important to be a good QB, and Milton ain’t. A good arm is only half the battle….maybe even less. Accuracy, being pocket aware, not locking on to your #1 target, not always throwing rockets….all of these are equally important.“ -JeffinBranson Feedpost of the Day:

title: Raiders GM preaches development of young roster
summary: Las Vegas Raiders’ general manager John Spytek and assistant GM Brian Stark addressed the media Tuesday afternoon to speak about the newly set 53-man roster for the 2026 season, which starts in 12 days. They set a clear theme — they know they have a young roster that will need time to develop, but they’re […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - AUGUST 27: Mike Washington Jr. #30 of the Las Vegas Raiders runs against the San Francisco 49ers during the first quarter of a preseason game at Allegiant Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images Las Vegas Raiders’ general manager John Spytek and assistant GM Brian Stark addressed the media Tuesday afternoon to speak about the newly set 53-man roster for the 2026 season, which starts in 12 days. They set a clear theme — they know they have a young roster that will need time to develop, but they’re excited about it. “We got a long way to go, a lot of work to do with a young roster,” Spytek said. He noted that the roster “requires development and development requires time.” Of course, the player at the center of the Raiders’ youth movement, is rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 overall pick in the draft. The Raiders haven’t yet announced that veteran addition Kirk Cousins will start Week 1 at home against Miami, but that is the reported expectation. Of Mendoza, Spytek said “his time is coming, but he has to earn it every day.” Spytek gave an encouraging thought on starting running back Ashton Jeanty’s return from an ankle injury he suffered nine days ago, saying he’s “in a good spot.” Jeanty was on a side field, working with a trainer during Tuesday’s practice. “I expect him to be back as quick as he can,” Spytek said. “Maybe quicker than some would expect, but we’ll see.’ Spytek said head coach Klint Kubiak “stood on the table” to draft running back Mike Washington in the fourth round out of Arkansas. Spytek said the player is a perfect scheme fit for Kubiak’s offense. He was impressive in the preseason and should play a lot in the regular season. Spytek said the organization is excited about the “track” Washington is on. Asked about which player impressed them the most this summer, Spytek said late addition, pass-rusher Patrick Johnson. Stark tabbed second-year defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway. The Raiders like the experience of cornerback Darrell Luter, who was claimed off waivers from the San Francisco 49ers on Monday. Luter, who can play special teams, has played in 27 games and has three starts. He’s 26.

title: Rob Leonard settling into new role as Las Vegas Raiders’ defensive coordinator
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders are about to begin the 2026 regular season with almost a brand-new coaching staff. Pete Carroll is out and Klint Kubiak is in as head coach, and the majority of the rest of the staff is entering its first year in Las Vegas. However, Kubiak did keep one familiar face: Rob […]
full_text: HENDERSON, NEVADA - AUGUST 06: Defensive coordinator Rob Leonard of the Las Vegas Raiders walks on a field during the team's training camp at the Las Vegas Raiders Headquarters/Intermountain Health Performance Center on August 06, 2026 in Henderson, Nevada. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders are about to begin the 2026 regular season with almost a brand-new coaching staff. Pete Carroll is out and Klint Kubiak is in as head coach, and the majority of the rest of the staff is entering its first year in Las Vegas. However, Kubiak did keep one familiar face: Rob Leonard. Leonard is no stranger to the Raiders and the organization’s regime changes, serving as the team’s defensive line coach from 2023 to 2025. Kubiak will be the fourth head coach he’s worked under in as many years with the club, but even the organization’s longest-tenured current coach will be stepping into a new role this season. In his 14 years as an NFL coach, Leonard has never held the ‘defensive coordinator’ title until this year. So, the preseason was the first time he’s called plays in a game, which the 38-year-old said has “been fun.” “You learn something every game,” Leonard explained. “Very focused. I mean, you’re just so process-oriented within the middle of the game. As soon as the series is done, what problems do we need to fix? Coaches up. Let’s get on the same page here of, ‘Okay, what did we run on first and 10 that last series? What do we want to do the next series?’ “Very similar to how we would do it as a position coach, but now being the guy that is making sure you get the right information from upstairs to get the right information to the position coaches. We talk about it a lot as a staff of them understanding the cadence of how the game is going to flow together. So, we’re in this together.” Reinforcing the togetherness, Leonard continued to say that he has been leaning on his staff to help with situational play calls, referring to defensive line coach Travis Smith as the “head coach” of the early-down run game as an example. That did come with some growing pains, though. The Raiders surrendered 27 points and 368 yards to the Arizona Cardinals in their first preseason game, Leonard’s first time making calls into the headset. However, the defense settled in during its second go-around, yielding just 13 points and 219 yards to the Houston Texans’ offense. For bookkeeping purposes, the Texans’ defense had a pick-six to bring the team’s total to 20 points. What accounts for the difference between the two outings? Familiarity. “A little bit,” Leonard replied when asked if the process slowed down from week one to week two. “I just thought we put our guys in a little bit better position to do what we do. We were very vanilla early, but the guys played faster because we ran a lot of calls that our guys are familiar with, without speaking too much on that.” The defensive coordinator’s comments touch on another aspect of the preseason. Most coaches keep their scheme pretty simple in the three games that don’t count toward the team’s record, not wanting to reveal too much before the results really start to matter. After the Cardinals game, Kubiak even said that the defensive scheme was pretty simple, primarily sticking to man coverage so the coaching staff could see which cornerbacks can cover. However, it was a different story against the Texans, as the clip below highlights how Leonard dove a little deeper into the playbook. Someone's gotta tell Rob Leonard this is the preseason lol -Shift into a double-mug look -Both LBs drop, boundary CB blitzes w/ no stacked S -Show 2-high pre-snap, rotate boundary S down to bluff 1-high -Field S rotates to deep half in boundary -SS drops to play Cover 2 pic.twitter.com/ilC1i1wMkS — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) August 22, 2026 But again, how the team performs in August doesn’t mean much in the big picture, as the following four months (plus a few weeks) are what really matter. Instead, getting his defense prepped for the regular season and growing with his players has been the first-time play-caller’s primary focus over the summer. “I’m really just thinking about improving with the guys,” Leonard explained. “You’re really over the scheme [in the preseason]. And you can get into your own head, what to show, what not to show. I wanted our play style to improve from game one to game two, and I think we did that. “I just focus on what I’m asking these guys to do. Klint talks all the time about our operation, substitutions, getting in and out of the huddle, a sense of urgency to get lined up, safety rotation, like that’s really been the focus over all of those things, of improving with that.” That’s a fair statement and what any coach should be paying extra attention to during training camp, especially with a young team like the Raiders. But the training wheels are coming off soon, as Leonard will face his first major test in his new role on Sept. 13, when the Miami Dolphins come into town and the final score matters.

title: What does Keyron Crawford injury mean?
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders suffered a big blow when they were forced to put rookie, third-round pick, defensive end Keyron Crawford on season-ending injured reserve with a broken ankle. Crawford was injured in the final preseason game, last Thursday. The Auburn product had a sack shortly before being injured and was hurt on a play […]
full_text: HENDERSON, NEVADA - MAY 02: Keyron Crawford #42 of the Las Vegas Raiders attends a news conference after the team's rookie minicamp at the Las Vegas Raiders Headquarters/Intermountain Health Performance Center on May 02, 2026 in Henderson, Nevada. (Photo by David Becker/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders suffered a big blow when they were forced to put rookie, third-round pick, defensive end Keyron Crawford on season-ending injured reserve with a broken ankle. Crawford was injured in the final preseason game, last Thursday. The Auburn product had a sack shortly before being injured and was hurt on a play while he was in pursuit. After a slow start to training camp and the preseason, Crawford was showing a good pass-rush burst. He is a naturally talented player. The expectation was that he was a bit green and may take some time to develop. Thus, this injury is tough because it pushes back his on-field development. Crawford can still work on the mental part of the game during his rehabilitation, but he is missing valuable time in his playing development. Usually, ankle injuries don’t linger beyond a season, so he said be ready to resume his career next year. But t’s definitely a tough blow to start the career of Crawford, who turns 23 in October. The hope was he would be a valuable backup and get some playing time as a pass-rusher. Now, his role will be taken by veteran addition Patrick Johnson, who had a strong preseason. The six-year veteran has played in 70 games with two sacks. He has one career sack.

Poupart suggests Miami should look at former Dallas Cowboys quarterback Joe Milton, who was waived by the team on Monday. Prior to the waiver claim deadline, Poupart explained his suggestion, writing: And it brings us to quarterback Joe Milton III, who the Dolphins absolutely, positively need to bring into the fold — or at least attempt to. Milton now is available via waivers after the Dallas Cowboys made the surprising decision Monday to waived him after picking up running back Emari Demercado from the Arizona Cardinals. By all accounts, the Cowboys made this move with the thought of bringing Milton back to the practice squad because they figure other NFL teams settled their quarterback situation over the weekend… The Dolphins are not in a win-now mode; they’re in a mode of establish a foundation and an identity and, perhaps more importantly, finding talented young players to become major contributors down the road. That’s Milton’s profile. While Poupart’s basis was Miami needing to file a waiver claim for Milton, signing him as a free agent is still valid. Saving two million by cutting Dotson ? Yea we are going to need that money thru out the year ! Poaching costs money ! You have to be able to pay someone you stole off another teams practice squad. Naw one of them is getting cut when the waivers go thru ! But our backups do not scare anyone. First string stays healthy we might actually win 4 games. I would have liked to see them cut Ollie or Jaylen at RB and keep Jarquez. Glad to see Heck and all of the QBs go. Altmeyer would not be a bad get. bringbackthewhalers , like most of us, is concerned about the depth, especially at OL. We should give Evan Neal a look as an IOL. Sounds like he’s had a rough start in NY, but wonder if he could be a gem with some new coaching. Don’t have a lot of faith in our back-up OL and Achane has some really good games in our 6 OL sets last year. Gllmiaspr is confused by the team cutting Ewers. The most puzzling cut was Ewers. I did not watch the practices and am just going by the first pre-season game. In that game he did not play well but the back up offensive lineman were horrible. In my view Ewers last year showed he could become a started and definitely was at the level of a competent backup. MiamiItaliano was surprised that they cut Major Burns. Major Burns was most surprising to be cut. I thought they would keep 4 safeties on the roster. But it looks like Kyle Louis will go back and forth between linebacker and strong safety. Relieved to see Cam Miller gone. He should be done in the league. If they don’t resign Gronowski to the PS, they should sign Altmeyer. Phoenix6 was relieved to see a couple of QBs let go. However, I believe his contract dollars & the emergence of LBer Jacob “the ‘stache” Rodriguez ,made him expendable. Additionally, were any of these unexpected departures particularly disappointing? The emergence od Rodriguez makes it easy to see Dotson go. On the flip side, which players were you relieved to see go? Ewers & C. Miller. Which players recently released by other teams should the Dolphins consider targeting via a waiver claim? This I do not know. But I’m feeling the RB is not done getting remodeled. Joining Miami on Tuesday are linebacker Liam Anderson, defensive end Clelin Ferrell, […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - DECEMBER 09: Mazi Smith #58 of the Dallas Cowboys looks on from the sideline during the national anthem prior to an NFL football game against the Cincinnati Bengals at AT&T Stadium on December 9, 2024 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins continue to build out their 2026 practice squad, adding another eight players Tuesday to the players they signed on Monday. The Dolphins announced the additions on Tuesday afternoon, rounding out the practice squad, at least until the next roster move. Joining Miami on Tuesday are linebacker Liam Anderson, defensive end Clelin Ferrell, defensive end Amari Gainer, defensive tackle Jordan Miller, wide receiver Will Sheppard, cornerback Jaylin Simpson, defensive tackle Mazi Smith, and tight end Tre Watson. The Dolphins released quarterback Mark Gronowski from the practice squad to make roster space. Anderson joins Miami after being waived by the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday. He started his NFL career as an undrafted free agent out of Holy Cross, signing with the Indianapolis Colts in 2023. He spent most of his rookie season on the Colts’ practice squad before making a late season appearance. He returned to Indianapolis for the 2024 season, again spending much of the season on the practice squad, before an injury during the 2025 training camp ended his Cincinnati tenure with an injury settlement. He joined the Colts during the 2025 season. Anderson has appeared in four career games with all of his snaps on special teams. Ferrell returns to the Dolphins after being released on Monday as part of Miami’s roster moves after being awarded seven waiver claims. He joined Miami as a free agent during training camp this year. A 2019 first-round draft pick of the Oakland (now Las Vegas) Raiders, Ferrell has also played for the San Francisco 49ers, Washington Commanders, and Los Angeles Chargers in his career. In 98 career games, he has recorded 184 tackles, 12 passes defensed, four forced fumbles, two fumble recoveries, and 21 sacks. Gainer was released by the New England Patriots in their roster cuts on Sunday. He originally entered the league in 2024 as an undrafted free agent, signing with the Las Vegas Raiders. He was released at the end of the 2025 training camp, then joined the Patriots near the end of the season. He played all 17 games for the Raiders in 2024, primarily on special teams, with five defensive tackles. Miller signed with the Denver Broncos in 2024 as an undrafted free agent out of SMU and Miami. He spent both his rookie season and last year on the practice squad. Sheppard went undrafted in 2025, signing with the Green Bay Packers out of Colorado and Vanderbilt. He spent the majority of the year on the practice squad, with a brief stint on the active roster. He was waived by the Packers on Sunday in their roster cuts. Simpson spent 2025 with the Green Bay Packers, appearing in one game. He was originally a fifth-round selection by the Indianapolis Colts in 2024, spending the season on their practice squad. He has eight career tackles. Smith was a first-round pick (27th overall) by the Dallas Cowboys in 2023 out of Michigan. He was traded to the New York Jets during the 2025 season. In his career, he has played in 42 games, starting 20 of them, with 57 tackles and two sacks. Watson spent the 2025 season on the Kansas City Chiefs practice squad after going undrafted out of Texas A&M and Fresno State. He was cut by the Chiefs as part of their roster moves on Sunday.

summary: As previously reported on the DN and elsewhere, the Minnesota Vikings hosted free agent outside linebacker Kyle Van Noy for a visit on Tuesday. That visit apparently went well as Tom Pelissero is reporting that Van Noy is signing with the Vikings. Apparently Van Noy will start on the practice squad, which is likely a […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - OCTOBER 12: Kyle van Noy #53 of the Baltimore Ravens reacts prior to an NFL football game against the Los Angeles Rams at M&T Bank Stadium on October 12, 2025 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images As previously reported on the DN and elsewhere, the Minnesota Vikings hosted free agent outside linebacker Kyle Van Noy for a visit on Tuesday. That visit apparently went well as Tom Pelissero is reporting that Van Noy is signing with the Vikings. Veteran OLB Kyle Van Noy is signing with the Vikings, sources tell @ringer @netflixsports . Van Noy and DC Brian Flores won two Super Bowls together with the Patriots. Now they’re teaming up in Minnesota, where Van Noy will start on the practice squad to ramp up. pic.twitter.com/VPyL4aosTD — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) September 2, 2026 Apparently Van Noy will start on the practice squad, which is likely a temporary move as the Vikings finagle their roster in advance of the regular season. Van Noy has played under Brian Flores in New England and Miami, but things didn’t end well in Miami after he was cut one year into a four-year, $51 million contract. But apparently Van Noy and Flores were able to mend fences and will work together again in Minnesota. Van Noy also played with Andrew Van Ginkel in Miami. Van Noy is 35 but has fared well into his 30s, chalking up 14 sacks among 56 quarterback pressures as recently as 2024. He’s also a solid run defender and when dropping in coverage. Wow. Terms of the deal are not yet available.

title: 2026 NFC North Season Forecast: Detroit Lions
summary: Next up in this year’s series forecasting the Minnesota Vikings’ NFC North rival seasons is the Detroit Lions. Once again, we’ll look at coaching and roster changes this offseason, how last season unfolded and any luck and injury factors that affected their results, along with a comparison of how this year’s strength of schedule compares […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - DECEMBER 04: (L-R) Jared Goff #16 looks on alongside head coach Dan Campbell of the Detroit Lions against the Dallas Cowboys during the fourth quarter at Ford Field on December 04, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Next up in this year’s series forecasting the Minnesota Vikings’ NFC North rival seasons is the Detroit Lions. Once again, we’ll look at coaching and roster changes this offseason, how last season unfolded and any luck and injury factors that affected their results, along with a comparison of how this year’s strength of schedule compares to last season, and a prediction for the Lions win total this season. You can find the Chicago Bears forecast here . Detroit Lions The Detroit Lions finished a disappointing last in the NFC North last season, tied with the Vikings with a 9-8 record but the Vikings having swept them in the season series. The Packers swept them too but the Lions swept the Bears, finishing 2-4 in the division. It was a disappointing finish for the Lions because despite losing offensive coordinator Ben Johnson, the Lions still maintained a top five offense. Having said that, the Lions scored 83 fewer points than 2024. The Lions replaced Ben Johnson with John Morton, who was relieved of play-calling duties mid-way through the season and was let go at the end of the season. At the same time, the Lions defense went from 7th in points allowed in 2024 to 22nd last season. Overall, the Lions went from leading the league in point differential at +222 in 2024 to +68 in 2025- which was still best in the division. All of the latter came in blowouts of the Bears, Browns, and Commanders. But the Lions struggled more against quality opponents. Still, they were 8-5 with four games to play but lost two close games to the Rams and Steelers before falling 23-10 to the Max Brosmer-led Vikings which ended their playoff hopes. A big reason for the Lions disappointing season was due to injuries. They were once again hit hard- especially defensively- with injuries. We’ll get into that more later but there was a six-game stretch late in the season where they were giving up an average of 30 points per game. The offense wasn’t as productive in part because of the change in coordinators, but primarily because the offensive line was not the dominant one of 2024. Kevin Zietler and Frank Ragnow- both top performers in 2024- were replaced with 2024 weak-link Graham Glascow at center and rookie Tate Ratledge at right guard. Christian Mahagony took over at left guard and disappointed. And left tackle Taylor Decker played injured most of the season. All that led to more pressure on Jared Goff, who has the largest performance differential between having a clean pocket and when pressured. Bottom line, each unit for the Lions regressed from 2024 whether due to injury, roster or coaching downgrades. Offseason Changes The Lions replaced John Morton this offseason with Drew Petzing, who was the offensive coordinator for the Cardinals the last three seasons. He has more of a short passing, under center, play-action, balanced pass/run game approach, although last season the Cardinals led the league in pass percentage- likely a product of game situation and injuries to running backs. He spent several seasons with the Vikings before following Kevin Stefanski to Cleveland. Apparently head coach Dan Campbell wanted someone outside the organization to help bring a new perspective to the offense. Petzing had a near top-12 offense in Arizona in 2024 when his key players- including Kyler Murray- were healthy. He seems a pretty good fit for the Lions personnel offensively and what they like to do. Other than Petzing, the Lions have continuity in head coach Dan Campbell (who called plays the second half of last season) and defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard who is entering his second season as defensive coordinator. In terms of the Lions’ offensive roster, they are continuing to try to rebuild their offensive line. They let Taylor Decker and Graham Glasgow go this offseason and are moving All-Pro tackle Penei Sewell from right to left tackle. They acquired center Cade Mays in free agency but he is expected to miss the first half of the season with a wrist injury. Juice Scruggs, who they acquired as part of a trade, will play center until Mays is ready. Both are significant downgrades from Frank Ragnow, who played center in 2024, and are more in-line with Graham Glasgow last season, Mays grading a bit better in pass protection. Tate Ratledge will return at right guard while Christian Mahagony, who struggled last season, will likely be the starter at left guard. The Lions also drafted Blake Miller with their first-round pick, and he is likely to start at right tackle. Overall, this isn’t likely to be the dominant line the Lions had in 2024, and it may not be much improved from last season. The Lions are also promoting wide receiver Isaac TeSlaa after moving on from Kalif Raymond. TeSlaa has shown flashes but not a clear upgrade at this point. They also traded David Montgomery, who they seemed to be phasing out last season in favor of Jahmyr Gibbs, who will be their bell cow back this season. Gibbs is the better back but the extra workload could wear on him as a smaller back for a bell cow role. Defensively, the Lions have also made some changes over the offseason. They moved on from the oft-injured Marcus Davenport, who has made roughly $20 million over the past three seasons playing less than 500 total snaps. They replaced him with former Viking D.J. Wonnum, who turns 29 this year. Wonnum was always a decent backup but never a starting-caliber edge rusher. The Lions are hoping that defensive tackle Alim McNeill, who is their third-largest cap hit this year at $29 million, will return to his form of 2-3 years ago before his injuries. He tore his ACL in 2024 which kept him out some games in 2025 but he also had an abdomen issue as well. Last season was his worst of his pro career according to PFF grading at 52.2 overall. Otherwise, the Lions will continue with Aiden Hutchinson but not much else up front. At linebacker, the Lions return All-Pro Jack Campbell but moved on from Alex Anzalone in favor promoting Derrick Barnes. They also acquired Devin White who could see some action. The Lions defensive secondary is in flux. Starting safeties Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph start on the PUP list while former first-round pick Terrion Arnold, who was a starting cornerback, was released after an off-field issue this offseason. Arnold struggled as a starter and will be replaced by Rock Ya-Sin. DJ Reed returns as the other outside corner. He’s been a good corner over his career, but he turns 30 later this year and his best days are probably behind him. The Lions also moved on from Amik Robertson at slot corner and replaced him with Roger McCreary. He is a decent slot corner but probably not an upgrade. The issue with the Lions now is after a few good drafts those core players are now getting paid. Jared Goff, Amon-Ra St Brown, Alim McNeill, and Penei Sewell are nearly $127 million cap hits collectively, and will be $152 million next year. Aiden Hutchinson, Jahmyr Gibbs, Jack Campbell, Kerby Joseph, and Jameson Williams have massively backend weighted contracts as well. And it looks like they will be letting TE Sam LaPorta and S Brian Branch go at the end of this season because they can’t afford to extend them. In some ways it’s a good problem to have but when you are providing market-setting contracts to a handful of players, it leaves the roster top-heavy and difficult to fill out with quality players. Jared Goff turns 32 next month and averages a $65 million annual cap hit over the 2027-28 seasons. How well he’ll play as he gets further into his 30s remains a question, but how good the offensive line will be will likely be a major factor. Goff has the largest dropoff in performance under pressure of any starting…

title: Report: Vikings to Host Kyle Van Noy on Free Agent Visit
summary: The Minnesota Vikings are likely in the market for a veteran edge defender, and there could be one on the way according to a recent report. Kyle Van Noy, who has played under Brian Flores at two different stops in his NFL career, is reportedly on his way to visit with the Vikings at some […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - DECEMBER 21: Kyle Van Noy #53 of the Baltimore Ravens runs around the edge during an NFL football game against the New England Patriots at M&T Bank Stadium on December 21, 2025 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings are likely in the market for a veteran edge defender, and there could be one on the way according to a recent report. Free agent Kyle Van Noy is very much on the #Vikings radar. A visit is expected to take place. Personally, seeing how entertaining he is on this app, 🙏🏼 to happening! pic.twitter.com/aa2eRyUJLI — Darren Wolfson (@DWolfsonKSTP) September 1, 2026 Kyle Van Noy, who has played under Brian Flores at two different stops in his NFL career, is reportedly on his way to visit with the Vikings at some point in the next day or two, according to Darren Wolfson of KSTP in Minneapolis. Van Noy has been in the league for a long time now, having been selected by the Detroit Lions in the second round of the 2014 NFL Draft out of BYU. He spent the first two and a half years of his career in Detroit before being traded to the New England Patriots midway through the 2016 season, where Flores was the team’s linebackers coach. He played for the Patriots through the 2019 season and then spent the 2020 season with the Miami Dolphins, where Flores had taken over as the head coach. Despite signing a four-year contract with the Dolphins before the 2020 season, he was released after just one year and returned to New England for the 2021 season. He was then released by the Patriots despite a productive 2021 season and spent the 2022 season with the Los Angeles Chargers before landing with the Baltimore Ravens, where he’s spent the past three seasons. In 2024, Van Noy recorded a career-high with 12.5 sacks, but saw that number drop to just two last season. The 35-year-old has tallied 57 sacks in his 12-year NFL career thus far. At this point, Van Noy obviously wouldn’t be expected to start but would provide some quality depth behind Dallas Turner and Andrew Van Ginkel. He probably wouldn’t cost a ton of money, either, although the Vikings have enough cap space to make a reasonable deal possible. What do you think of the possibility of adding Kyle Van Noy to the Minnesota defense, folks?

title: Vikings 53-Man Roster: McCarthy Stays, Banks Is the Future, and the Practice Squad Revealed
summary: J.J. McCarthy stays on the Vikings 53 — and the injury story still doesn’t add up. The Minnesota Vikings set their 53-man roster with J.J. McCarthy still on it, then spent Monday shuffling the edges. On The Real Forno Show, Tyler Forness and Dave Stefano unpacked the leak that McCarthy’s ankle is suddenly “week to […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - AUGUST 22: J.J. McCarthy #9 of the Minnesota Vikings warms up before an NFL football game against the Baltimore Ravens at U.S. Bank Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Kara Durrette/Getty Images) | Getty Images J.J. McCarthy stays on the Vikings 53 — and the injury story still doesn’t add up. The Minnesota Vikings set their 53-man roster with J.J. McCarthy still on it, then spent Monday shuffling the edges. On The Real Forno Show, Tyler Forness and Dave Stefano unpacked the leak that McCarthy’s ankle is suddenly “week to week,” Ben Goessling’s report that McCarthy himself chose not to play Friday, the Max Brosmer and Dillon Bell cuts, waiver claims of Trevor Keegan and Nick Samac, and a practice squad still taking shape. Forness opened with the elephant in the room: he expected Minnesota to move on from McCarthy before the deadline. Then Adam Schefter said on Pat McAfee that the ankle is a multi-week injury — 10 days after the sprain, after McCarthy practiced fully Monday and Tuesday. “I don’t buy it for a second,” Forness said. “If it really was a multi-week injury… now we’re calling it a week-to-week injury after he goes out and practices in full?” Stefano called a grade-one deltoid sprain “100% playable” and asked why sitting Friday or leaking “week to week” would help trade stock. Forness noted other backups (Quinn Ewers, Kyle McCord) already moved for sixth-rounders, and that waiting only shrinks the market. Goessling reported the sit-out was McCarthy’s call, not the organization’s. “It was him not being comfortable playing in the game,” Forness quoted. “The whole thing just smells rotten.” Monday’s moves were clearer. Minnesota claimed interior linemen Keegan and Samac after trading Walter Rouse, then waived Brosmer and Bell to make room. Forness said if McCarthy can’t go Week 1, Kevin O’Connell will want a third active-roster quarterback because an emergency QB must be on the 53, not the practice squad. They also ran the rest of the roster: four tight ends with T.J. Hockenson in a contract year; Tyler Batty’s torn ACL thinning the edge; Caleb Banks as a long-term “unicorn” pick, not a Year 1 finished product. “You drafted him for ’27, ’29, and ’30,” Forness said. “Trading him now would be incredibly shortsighted.” Key points from the episode: J.J. McCarthy saga : McCarthy practiced fully Monday and Tuesday before sitting out Wednesday. He chose not to play Friday’s preseason finale despite the plan being for him to start the first half. Trade talks reportedly occurred but no deal materialized. Tyler expects a new quarterback added if McCarthy can’t play Week 1. Offensive line : The Vikings claimed Trevor Keegan (fourth-ranked PFF guard) and Nick Samac (top PFF preseason center), both with center versatility. Walter Rouse was traded for a sixth-round pick. Max Brosmer and Dillon Bell were waived. Tight end : Four TEs made the roster—T.J. Hockenson, Josh Oliver, Ben Yurosek, and Gavin Bartholomew. Tyler noted Hockenson is in the final year of his deal. Caleb Banks : Tyler defended the developmental pick: “You’re drafting for ’27, ’29, and ’30. This guy could, if he reaches his potential, be a Chris Jones type wrecking All-Pro.” Edge depth : Tyler Batty tore his ACL and is out for the year. The edge group includes Dallas Turner, Andrew Van Ginkel, Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins, Bo Richter, and Chaz Chambliss. Linebacker : Ivan Pace Jr. showed improvement in coverage. Blake Cashman, Eric Wilson, and Jake Golday round out the group. Special teams : Brett Thorson beat out Johnny Hekker for the punter job, with Tyler citing the international pathway player designation and comparable performance. Practice squad : Da’Veawn Armstead, Kahlef Hailassie, Bangally Kamara, Jahvaree Ritzie, and Cam’Ron Stewart highlight a group Tyler called “pretty solid.” GM Nolan Teasley’s Seattle connections brought in Marshall Lang, Michael Briscoe, and Trayvon Rudolph. Listen: Or on your favorite podcast aggregator. Watch: Whether you’re tracking the McCarthy saga or excited about Elijah Williams potentially starting Week 1, this episode delivers the full roster breakdown Vikings fans need. Catch The Real Forno Show with Tyler Forness and Dave Stefano—your home for unfiltered Minnesota Vikings analysis on Vikings 1st & SKOL. Fan with Us!!! Tyler Forness @TheRealForno of Vikings 1st & SKOL @Vikings1stSKOL and A to Z Sports @AtoZSportsNFL , with Dave Stefano @Luft_Krigare producing this Vikings 1st & SKOL production, the @RealFornoShow found at the @BleavNetwork . What do you think? Which roster decision surprised you the most—and do you think McCarthy is still on this team come Week 1?

title: Are the Minnesota Vikings Super Bowl contenders?
summary: The Minnesota Vikings may not be the betting favorites like some of the teams with more recent playoff success, but they have become one of the more popular dark horse picks among national TV and radio personalities entering the season. One of the advantages of not living in the local market is getting to hear […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - AUGUST 28: Head Coach Kevin O'Connell of the Minnesota Vikings motions on the field before a preseason game against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on August 28, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings may not be the betting favorites like some of the teams with more recent playoff success, but they have become one of the more popular dark horse picks among national TV and radio personalities entering the season. One of the advantages of not living in the local market is getting to hear outside perspectives on the Vikings. I’ve been struggling to get into this season. Maybe it’s life, maybe it’s the lingering disappointment from last season, but for whatever reason, I couldn’t get excited about this season. However, that started to change recently. Every time I turn on an NFL show or listen to a football podcast, someone seems to be talking about the Vikings as a dark horse contender. Why are the Vikings Generating Buzz? The most obvious answer is talent. For a team that recently moved on from its general manager, the roster is surprisingly stacked. The offensive line is stout, the wide receiver group is elite, and the Vikings have two very capable running backs. The biggest question is whether Kyler Murray can take full advantage of those weapons while still providing a threat with his mobility. Brian Flores’ defense is consistently among the league’s most respected units, and he has a track record of maximizing the talent available to him. The team has done well to shed aging talent and continue to develop young players. Dallas Turner is a name on everyone’s tongue as a breakout player. The coaching staff and the addition of Kyler Murray are two more reasons for the optimism surrounding the team. Kevin O’Connell has a knack for developing quarterbacks and winning games even when his teams aren’t receiving elite quarterback play. He has helped multiple quarterbacks step into the system and find immediate success. The timing for Kyler Murray couldn’t be any better for a career revival, and it was only two seasons ago when the team rode Darnold to 14 wins in his first year in purple. Murray has always had the talent, and this might be the team he needs to get the most out of it. The Perfect “Dark Horse” Profile The team has a likable coach with a history of getting veteran quarterbacks comfortable in his system quickly. The roster is very deep and doesn’t depend on one star, but it does have a star in Justin Jefferson. The Vikings are the perfect dark horse pick because they’re talented enough that no one will be surprised if they’re playing meaningful games in January. Kyler Murray for MVP? Vikings QB among top nine dark horse candidates in 2026, @TheDan_Parr writes https://t.co/A3SIZ5AOt1 pic.twitter.com/nbgZdNNnrt — Around The NFL (@AroundTheNFL) June 10, 2026 Final Thoughts The national media is mostly lazy. There isn’t an effort to go in depth on 32 teams. That means national narratives aren’t always the best measuring stick. I don’t know if I’m fully ready to call them Super Bowl contenders, but I do believe they’ll be in the hunt for the division title and a playoff spot late in the season. And once you get in, it’s anyone’s game.

title: Kyle Williams ready to prove he’s more than just a deep threat
summary: Kyle Williams has a special trick as a wide receiver That was on display during the preseason, as the second-year wide receiver caught three touchdowns all on the same route: a go ball. But Williams knows his game has more than just that one trick. “I’ve been hearing that my whole life man, so I […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 22: Kyle Williams #18 of the New England Patriots celebrates after scoring a touchdown against the Philadelphia Eagles during an NFL preseason football game at Gillette Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Kyle Williams has a special trick as a wide receiver That was on display during the preseason, as the second-year wide receiver caught three touchdowns all on the same route: a go ball. But Williams knows his game has more than just that one trick. “I’ve been hearing that my whole life man, so I wouldn’t really say it’s a chip on my shoulder,” Williams said. “I know what I can do. I know I’m more than just a vertical guy. Whatever my role is that’s my role and I’m gonna accept it.” Williams’ elite release package and vertical speed make him a big-time threat along the outside. That was his role for much of last season, as one-third of his routes were go balls — one of the highest rates in football. Among the few players with a higher rate was recently traded wide receiver Kayshon Boutte. The 2025 third-round pick’s ability to win deep will continue to be an asset for the Patriots’ offense — especially with Boutte’s departure. While the team spent the offseason upgrading the wide receiver depth chart, A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs are not specifically burners at the position. Quarterback Drake Maye is also one of the best deep-ball throwers in the NFL. Entering his second season, however, Williams is adding to his game. This offseason, the 23-year old spent time running more intermediate routes and moving around the formation after spending virtually all of last season outside and on the ball. “In college, I really wasn’t exposed to too many intermediate routes. So now I’m getting that opportunity to do it,” Williams said this summer. “So Year 1 to Year 2 it’s definitely been night and day. Now it’s just that ball finding me across the middle and everything so I can really showcase what I’ve been working on.” Mastering those route concepts in Josh McDaniels’ offense is no easy task for a wide receiver. Williams noted that the on-the-fly decision-making process was the biggest challenge, but was pleased looking back on his training camp with how his mindset developed throughout the process. “It’s time on task, right?,” wide receiver coach Todd Downing said. “And there are some things that collegiately, maybe Kyle was able to do, because he was just more physically talented than some of the defenses that he was going against. And you get it this league, and I’ve always said that the closer you are to the football, the faster things happen. “I think Kyle is starting to get more and more comfortable with that speed and that urgency that it takes to make the right decisions in there. So, I’m excited where he’s at and I love the approach that he’s taken — a do anything he’s asked approach, and he’s done well with his [opportunities].” As the Patriots are just a week away from their regular season opener against the Seattle Seahawks, Williams is ready to keep growing and find his footing in a talented wide receiver room. “I feel like I bring a lot, just as much as the other guys do,” Williams said. “So, I mean, I don’t really want to single myself out, but as a whole room, I feel like we nasty. I feel like we got a nasty group.”

title: Mike Vrabel gives intel into Patriots’ waiver wire pickups
summary: The New England Patriots’ roster construction process did not end with the 53-man deadline on Sunday. In the two days since, the reigning AFC champions continued making moves to modify the roster with the season opener in Seattle on the horizon. Two of those moves involved recently-released players getting picked up on the waiver wire. […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - DECEMBER 28: Darius Muasau #53 of the New York Giants warms up prior to the game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium on December 28, 2025 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots’ roster construction process did not end with the 53-man deadline on Sunday. In the two days since, the reigning AFC champions continued making moves to modify the roster with the season opener in Seattle on the horizon. Two of those moves involved recently-released players getting picked up on the waiver wire . Despite ranking 31st in the priorities order, the Patriots were able to pick up both tight end Cameron Latu and linebacker Darius Muasau after they were cut from the Eagles and Giants, respectively. For head coach Mike Vrabel, those moves came down to one thing: experience. “Just guys that have really played NFL games, meaningful football games,” Vrabel explained talking to the media at Gillette Stadium on Tuesday. Latu started his career as a third-round draft pick by the 49ers in 2023, and has taken the field in 15 games since. then — all as a member of the Eagles last season. Remaining with Philadelphia this summer, Vrabel and the Patriots were able to get an up-close look at him during the two teams’ joint practices and preseason game earlier this month. As Vrabel pointed out, however, this was not the first touching point. In fact, he worked closely with his new head coach before he moved to New England in January 2025. “I was with Cam during my time in Cleveland, and really enjoyed getting to know him, being able to work with him and try to help him,” he said about the 26-year-old. “We had some conversations about him last year, and he went on to do some really good things to help Philadelphia. Then we just thought it would be a good opportunity to add somebody that has excelled at special teams and also looking to earn a role at tight end.” Muasau spent both of his NFL seasons with the Giants. Playing 27 combined games along the way as an off-ball linebacker and special teamer, he briefly crossed paths with multiple members of New England’s coaching staff: during his 2024 rookie season, the sixth-round draft choice worked under a staff featuring current Patriots assistants Zak Kuhr and Shane Bowen. “Darius has shown the ability to play both spots inside,” said Vrabel. “Zak had some comfort and some familiarity with him in New York.”

title: Former Patriots find new homes after NFL roster cuts
summary: In order to get under the NFL’s 53-man roster limit on Sunday, the New England Patriots made a combined 37 roster cuts over the weekend. And while some of those players have found their way back via the team’s practice squad, a significant portion remains unsigned or has officially moved on. As of Wednesday morning, […]
full_text: Dec 15, 2024; Glendale, Arizona, USA; New England Patriots cornerback Marcellas Dial Jr. (27) against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con In order to get under the NFL’s 53-man roster limit on Sunday, the New England Patriots made a combined 37 roster cuts over the weekend . And while some of those players have found their way back via the team’s practice squad, a significant portion remains unsigned or has officially moved on. As of Wednesday morning, that second group consists of five players highlighted by 2024 sixth-round draft pick Marcellas Dial Jr. The cornerback, who found himself on the roster bubble throughout the summer, was claimed off waivers by the Miami Dolphins. Dial Jr., 25, entered the Patriots as the 180th overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft. He appeared in all 17 of the Patriots’ games as a rookie, mostly on special teams, but had to miss his entire sophomore campaign after suffering a torn ACL in training camp. He returned this year and saw action as a nickel back and four-unit kicking game contributor, but ultimately lost a roster spot to rookie cornerbacks Karon Prunty and Channing Canada. This, in turn, meant that the Patriots’ eight-player 2024 draft class was now down to only quarterback Drake Maye. Dial Jr., on the other hand, will try to revive his career with the Patriots’ division rivals. Also joining him in Miami are outside linebackers Bradyn Swinson and Amari Gainer, who were both signed to the team’s practice squad. Tight end Jack Westover, meanwhile, joined the Washington Commanders’ developmental roster. Offensive lineman James Hudson, on the other hand, has also found an opportunity on a 53-man roster. The veteran was signed by the Tennessee Titans after making his way to free agency.
