title: Patriots 2026 scouting report for DT Cory Durden
summary: The New England Patriots made major investments in their defensive tackle group last year, but one of the most impactful actually happened after roster cuts: signing Cory Durden, who eventually ended the 2025 season as one of the team’s most-used players along the interior defensive line. Heading into his second year in Foxborough, little is […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - JANUARY 11: Cory Durden #94 of the New England Patriots reacts after a play against the Los Angeles Chargers during the second quarter of the AFC Wild Card Playoff game at Gillette Stadium on January 11, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Adam Glanzman/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots made major investments in their defensive tackle group last year, but one of the most impactful actually happened after roster cuts: signing Cory Durden, who eventually ended the 2025 season as one of the team’s most-used players along the interior defensive line. Heading into his second year in Foxborough, little is expected to change for the 27-year-old. Hard facts Name: Cory Durden Position: Defensive tackle/Interior defensive line Jersey number: 94 Opening day age: 27 (1/26/1999) Measurements : 6’4”, 305 lbs, 10 1/8” hand size, 33 1/2” arm length, 82 1/8” wingspan, 5.17s 40-yard dash, 7.56s 3-cone drill, 4.80s short shuttle, 31” vertical jump, 9’2” broad jump, 16 bench press reps, 5.79 Relative Athletic Score Experience NFL: Detroit Lions (2023), Los Angeles Rams (2023-24), New York Giants (2024), New England Patriots (2025-) | College: Florida State (2017-20), N.C. State (2021-22) A three-star recruit coming out of Newberry, FL, Durden received more than a dozen scholarship offers. Among the schools offering him were prestigious institutions such as Alabama, Georgia and Miami. However, Florida State had shown interest in him since his sophomore season at high school and he eventually opted to join the Seminoles. In four seasons in Tallahassee, he played 32 games with 16 starts and a combined 7.5 sacks. In December 2020, however, he opted to enter the transfer portal. Durden moved to N.C. State just two days later, and finished his college career with the Wolfpack. In two seasons, he added 25 games and 21 starts to his career totals and was named All-ACC twice (first team 2021, third team 2022). Durden entered the NFL as a rookie free agent with the Lions, but was cut before his rookie season began. He joined the Rams’ practice squad shortly thereafter and remained in Los Angeles until December 2024, when the Giants poached him. Durden left New York the subsequent August and later arrived in New England. Entering the 2026 season, his fourth in the NFL, he has played a combined 29 regular season and playoff games with six starts. He also has 47 tackles to his name. Scouting report Strengths: At 6-foot- with 33 1/2-inch arms, Durden offers solid length to hold his own along the interior defensive line. He is the most robustly-built player his position has to offer, but he uses his 305 pounds well to drop a firm anchor and stand up blockers at the point of attack. In general, he provides good core strength and a firm base while also displaying some burst out of his stance. This combined with powerful hands and an ability to employ counters, allows him to be disruptive both as a pass rusher and a run defender. Weaknesses: Durden is good when penetrating up the field, but his later quickness leaves some to be desired and puts him in challenging positions against zone-based blocking schemes. He also plays with an inconsistent pad level, which is exacerbated by a tendency to lean into his opposition and in turn creates too many off-balance plays that neutralize him. He also has been inconsistent as a finisher, posting solid pressure numbers but not actually hitting or sacking the quarterback at an accompanying rate. His tackling also has been on and off. 2025 review Stats : 21 games (6 starts) | 512 defensive snaps (39.9%), 126 special teams snaps (23.0%) | 34 tackles, 5 missed tackles (12.8%), 5 TFLs | 30 QB pressures (3 hits, 27 hurries) | 2 penalties (incl. 0 declined/offsetting) Season recap: Even though 2024 was the best season of his career up until that point, Durden entered his first training camp in New York on the roster bubble. He never managed to escape it, and ultimately saw the bubble burst ahead of the cutdown deadline: he was cut by the Giants as part of their final moves toward the 53-player limit. Passing through the waiver wire unclaimed, though, he was in a position to return via the practice squad. That did not happen. Instead, Durden took his talents to New England. He spent one week on the Patriots’ practice squad to open his stint, and then got himself promoted to the 53-man roster. Durden never looked back, and ended up producing the most productive campaign of his career. Appearing in all 21 of the Patriots’ regular season and playoff games, including six as a starter, Durden finished as the club’s No. 3 defensive tackle in terms of playing time. He did benefit from injuries higher up on the depth chart, especially the one suffered by Milton Williams, but nonetheless looked solid in his 512 total snaps on the defensive side of the ball — all while working mostly as an early-down run defender asked to also rush the passer on occasion. In the first area, he registered 32 tackles including five for a loss of yardage. While he did show some inconsistency protecting his gaps and finishing tackles, his pass defense was quite effective. In fact, his 30 quarterback pressures ranked fifth on the team. Of those 30, 13 came in the playoffs: while he registered no disruptions in the Super Bowl and was generally quiet on the game’s biggest stage, he was a handful for the Chargers’ and Texans’ offensive lines in their respective postseason matchups with the Patriots. All in all, Durden’s first year as a Patriot did leave some to be desired particularly against the run. His pass rush, on the other hand, was quite solid and a reason why he remained on the 53-man roster all year and into 2026. 2026 preview Position: Nose tackle/1-technique defensive tackle | Ability: Fringe starter/Role player | Contract: Signed through 2026 (2027 ERFA) What will be his role? Durden was a part-time starter for the Patriots in 2025, but effectively spent the year as the fourth option behind Milton Williams, Christian Barmore and Khyiris Tonga. With the latter now gone, however, the team might be looking at him to take a step up. Don’t expect him to be used the same fashion as Tonga, simply because he is a different body type, but he should end up taking over some of his early-down responsibilities at the heart of New England’s defensive line. What is his growth potential? Durden saw irregular in-game opportunities in his first two seasons in the NFL, but he showed some promise in his third with the Patriots — despite joining the team without the benefit of training camp. Now with a full year in New England under his belt, he should naturally take a step forward even if he might never become an impact player like some of the other DTs the team currently has under contract. Does he have positional versatility? Durden can line up in multiple spots up front, but on the whole is not a particularly noteworthy player from a versatility perspective. That said, he did show that he can wear a diverse set of hats on special teams: in 2025, he lined up on both the punt block team, the field goal/extra point block team, and on the field goal kicking squad. What is his salary cap situation? When the Patriots signed Durden from their practice squad to the 53-man roster last September, they did so via a two-year contract. As part of that pact, he counts $1.145 million against their books right now. That sum consists entirely of a non-guaranteed base salary. How safe is his roster spot? Durden was part of the Patriots’ initial 53-man roster, and in no real danger to leave it anytime soon. The bigger question is just how heavily-involved he will be in a group also featuring the aforementioned Milton Williams and Christian Barmore. Summary: Whether or not Durden will be a capable replacement for Khyiris Tonga will be seen; the Patriots seem to believe he can provide some similar value. However, his run defense needs to be better for him to…

title: What Erick Hunter, Ben Brown signings mean for the Patriots
summary: With just over a week to go until their season opener in Miami, the New England Patriots continue fine-tuning their 53-man roster. On Tuesday, the team of head coach Mike Vrabel added two players the mix: offensive lineman ben Brown was re-signed one day after his release, while rookie linebacker Erick Hunter was welcomed as […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OH - AUGUST 13: Detroit Lions linebacker Erick Hunter (48) walks off the field at halftime during the preseason game between the Detroit Lions and the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Cincinnati, OH. (Photo by Ian Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images With just over a week to go until their season opener in Miami, the New England Patriots continue fine-tuning their 53-man roster. On Tuesday, the team of head coach Mike Vrabel added two players the mix : offensive lineman ben Brown was re-signed one day after his release, while rookie linebacker Erick Hunter was welcomed as the latest new face to arrive. Let’s analyze what all of this means for the team. More speed at the second level Hunter was not selected in the 2026 NFL Draft, but it was not for a lack of athletic skill. The former Morgan State product, who finished second in school history with 298 combined tackles, performed well during pre-draft testing: he registered a fairly solid Relative Athletic Score of 8.64. What stands out about Hunter’s testing is his explosiveness. While his three-cone drill does not look the part, his burst and long speed are impressive; he ranks in the 98th percentile among linebackers over the last 40 years in both the 40-yard dash and the broad jump. A look at new Patriots linebacker Erick Hunter through @mathbomb.bsky.social's Relative Athletic Score. — Bernd Buchmasser (@berndbuchmasser.bsky.social) 2026-09-01T23:46:35.291Z Obviously, testing speed and game speed are two different things; the latter is closely tied to a player’s read-and-react skills, something Robert Spillane — who ran a 4.77-second 40-yard dash — excels in. That said, Hunter’s athletic foundation is strong and certainly of an NFL-caliber level. Depth questions remain The Patriots’ linebacker group is set at the top, with Robert Spillane and Christian Elliss a potent and proven starter pairing at the position. Further down the depth chart, however, there are questions — questions that remain even with Hunter in the mix. The 23-year-old, after all, is a relatively unproven commodity and one of two rookies now backing up Spillane and Elliss: 53-man roster (5): Robert Spillane (14), Christian Elliss (53), Namdi Obiazor (48), Darius Muasau (54), Erick Hunter (49) Practice squad (2): K.J. Britt (35), Riley Wilson (51) Injured reserve (1): Khalil Jacobs (59 | short-term) As long as Spillane and Elliss are both available, the Patriots should be in decent shape at linebacker. They also have some experience on the practice squad in the form of K.J. Britt. Darius Muasau, even more so than the rookies Hunter and Obiazor, might be the wild card. He has played a decent number of snaps over his first two seasons in the NFL, and also has some experience with the Patriots’ defensive staff from his time working under Shane Bowen with the Giants. Special teams impact Hunter’s role on the defensive side of the ball has yet to be determined, but it seems like a safe bet that he will be actively used in the kicking game fairly early. His athletic profile looks the part, and he saw his fair share of reps while spending the summer with the Lions: he played on five special teams units — kickoff return, kickoff coverage, punt return, punt coverage, field goal/extra point block — and registered three tackles. How the Patriots will employ him in the game’s third face is to be determined. His presence might allow the aforementioned Darius Muasau or Namdi Obiazor to place more of their focus on the LB3 role, however. Back to normal up front Ben Brown’s release on Monday might have come as a surprise, but not the follow-up report that he was expected back. It took only 24 hours for him to return, which means that the top five along the Patriots’ interior offensive line now look as most last-minute roster projections had it: 53-man roster (6): Alijah Vera-Tucker (75 | LG), Jared Wilson (55 | C), Mike Onwenu (71 | RG), Greg Van Roten (70), Ben Brown (77), Walter Rouse (72) Practice squad (2): Jake Kubas (63), Jacob Rizy (64) Based on their personal histories, Brown might primarily serve as the backup center behind Jared Wilson with Greg Van Roten the next man up at guard. Recent trade pickup Walter Rouse projects as an extra layer of developmental depth capable of lining up both on the inside and at tackle. Full roster, for now The Patriots adding Hunter and Brown to their roster moves the body count from 51 to 53 again, meaning that no open spots remains. Whether that means there will be no additional moves in the coming days will be seen. What the moves also mean is an increase in financial commitment. According to salary cap expert Miguel Benzan, New England lost roughly $3.6 million on Tuesday to bring the club’s cap space to $16.59 million .

summary: Votes were rounded up at Gillette Stadium on the first day of September. An official announcement followed. Quarterback Drake Maye, tight end Hunter Henry, offensive tackle Morgan Moses, linebacker Robert Spillane, cornerback Marcus Jones and safety Kevin Byard III have been named New England Patriots captains for the 2026 season. Maye, 24, officially stands as […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - DECEMBER 2: Morgan Moses #76 of the New England Patriots looks to block against the New York Giants during the game at Gillette Stadium on December 2, 2025 in Foxborough, Massachusetts.(Photo By Winslow Townson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Votes were rounded up at Gillette Stadium on the first day of September. An official announcement followed. Quarterback Drake Maye, tight end Hunter Henry, offensive tackle Morgan Moses, linebacker Robert Spillane, cornerback Marcus Jones and safety Kevin Byard III have been named New England Patriots captains for the 2026 season. The 2026 Patriots Captains 🫡 pic.twitter.com/s2AMrgsbx7 — New England Patriots (@Patriots) September 1, 2026 Maye, 24, officially stands as a back-to-back captain in Foxborough. The North Carolina product, taken No. 3 overall in the 2024 NFL draft, completed an NFL-leading 72 percent of his passes for 4,394 yards with 31 touchdowns and eight interceptions last regular season. He added 450 yards and four visits to the end zone as a rusher for the eventual AFC champions. Henry, 30, initially served as a Patriots captain in 2023, was elevated again amid 2024, and got the call out of the gate in 2025. He now gets his fourth nod on the heels of a contract extension in training camp. Arriving as a free agent from the Los Angeles Chargers in 2021, the former No. 35 overall pick and John Mackey Award winner out of Arkansas has appeared in 81 games while making 67 starts for the franchise. His tenure at tight end spans 259 catches for 2,973 yards and 26 touchdowns. Moses, 35, appeared in the running to become a team captain dating back to his introductory press conference in March 2025. The veteran right tackle is one now. Moses started all 17 games during his first year with the Patriots and stayed in 1,033 offensive snaps. Originally entering the NFL with Washington in the third round of the 2024 draft, the Virginia alum has also made stops with the New York Jets and Baltimore Ravens. He has appeared in 183 career games and started 175. Spillane, 30, gets his second nod in his second season with the Patriots. The 2025 signing made 13 starts at linebacker last campaign. Wearing the green dot off the ball, he totaled 97 tackles, one sack, one forced fumble and two interceptions in the process. Previously a captain for the Las Vegas Raiders, Spillane has also been a member of the Tennessee Titans and Pittsburgh Steelers. The Western Michigan product entered the NFL as an undrafted tryout in 2018 and stands 99 games into his career. Jones, 27, checks in as a two-time Patriots captain. The lone selection left from the organization’s 2022 draft class, the former No. 85 overall pick by way of Troy and Houston has appeared in 48 games. Making 22 starts in the secondary, Jones’ career includes 167 tackles, two sacks and six interceptions. It also includes two touchdowns on defense, one touchdown on offense and three touchdowns on punt returns. He earned first-team All-Pro honors as a rookie and second-team All-Pro honors last season. Byard, 33, reunited with a familiar staff in March after leading the NFL with seven interceptions as a Chicago Bear in 2025. A three-time Pro Bowler and first-team All-Pro, the veteran safety has appeared in 164 games and made 155 starts since entering the league out of Middle Tennessee State in the third round of the 2016 draft. A team captain throughout his journey, which began with the Tennessee Titans, Byard has amassed 972 tackles, 36 interceptions, six sacks, four forced fumbles, six fumble recoveries and two touchdown returns. Ahead of Mike Vrabel’s inaugural season as Patriots head coach, outside linebacker Harold Landry III and special teams ace Brenden Schooler also found themselves among New England’s six team captains . Both will miss the start of 2026 while on the club’s physically unable to perform and non-football injury list , respectively.
author: Oliver Thomas

title: Patriots practice report: TreVeyon Henderson remains sidelined
summary: Following their preseason finale on Thursday, the New England Patriots received a needed weekend off as the front office dwindled the roster down to 53 players. That group was back at Gillette Stadium on Tuesday for their first regular season practice in preparation for the Seattle Seahawks. As they did, they remained without running back […]
full_text: Jul 28, 2026; Foxborough, MA, USA; New England Patriots running back Treveyon Henderson (32) walks to practice for training camp at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Following their preseason finale on Thursday, the New England Patriots received a needed weekend off as the front office dwindled the roster down to 53 players. That group was back at Gillette Stadium on Tuesday for their first regular season practice in preparation for the Seattle Seahawks. As they did, they remained without running back TreVeyon Henderson after the second-year back suffered an ankle injury early last week. Henderson was present in the locker room in good spirits and walking normally, but has not yet fully been cleared to return to work. The only other non-participant on the roster was tight end Cameron Latu, who was claimed off of waivers on Monday. Latu was in the locker room ahead of practice after just arriving to the team. Fellow waiver claim, Darius Muasau, was on the practice field. “Just guys that have really played NFL games, meaningful football games,” Mike Vrabel said. “Darius has shown the ability to play both spots inside. Zak [Kuhr] had some comfort and some familiarity with him in New York. I was with Cam during my time in Cleveland and really enjoyed kind of getting to know him and being able to work with him and try to help him. “We had some conversations about him last year and he went on to do some really good things to help Philadelphia and then, you know, we just thought it’d be a good opportunity to add somebody that has excelled at special teams and also looking to earn a role at tight end.” The Patriots will continue to tinker with their 53-man roster and practice squad as Mike Vrabel stated they have brought in up to 10 new faces since the preseason finale. Several of those are expected to be announced later Tuesday afternoon. They will then be back on the practice fields on Thursday and this weekend before departing for Seattle on Monday.

title: State of the NFC South: Preseason recap
summary: The preseason is (finally) over, and the start of the season is nearly here. With that being the case, let’s look at a quick NFC South preseason recap! Tampa Bay Buccaneers The Buccaneers had an overall productive preseason experience. QB Jalon Daniels looked like a long term option post Baker Mayfield, Reuben Bain Jr. had […]
full_text: The preseason is (finally) over, and the start of the season is nearly here. With that being the case, let’s look at a quick NFC South preseason recap! Tampa Bay Buccaneers The Buccaneers had an overall productive preseason experience. QB Jalon Daniels looked like a long term option post Baker Mayfield, Reuben Bain Jr. had great plays that made the Bucs feel confident about that draft pick, and the team was able to sign star DT Vita Vea to a contract extension. Also, Bain Jr.’s teammate Kieonte Scott had some really good plays as well, which may be the most important rookie performance of all. Tampa Bay’s pass defense is arguably their biggest weakness, so if Scott can be a quality CB, the defense could be much better. Getting production from the rookies was very important, especially with the injuries and turnover this team has had. Losing Mike Evans in the offseason was big, and in the draft, the Bucs drafted his “replacement”, Ted Hurst. Hurst didn’t have any massive performances, but Bucs media is high on the rookie. Carolina Panthers Entering the preseason, Carolina was faced with some massive injuries to their team. Nic Scourton, who was a standout rookie last year, tore his ACL, and rookie WR Chris Brazzell III also suffered a season-ending knee injury. Brazzell is a WR with all the potential in the world due to his athleticism and size, but is still in the developmental phase of his NFL career. A season-ending injury could really hurt that development, and the Panthers will miss his potential production this season. The good news for Carolina is that the two WRs from the preseason, John Metchie III and Jimmy Horn Jr., both had standout performances, leading to their making the roster. Both players are still considered depth options, but Metchie III did play with QB Bryce Young in college. Atlanta Falcons As of writing this, the Falcons have not named their starting QB for Week 1. Michael Penix Jr. is ramping up from his season-ending injury last season, but he may not be 100% healthy, and risking that makes little sense. Then, Tua Tagovailoa did not have a good end to the preseason, struggling against his former team, the Miami Dolphins. In the end, Jack Strand was the standout QB, and he made the roster, along with Penix, Tua, and Cooper Rush. Interestingly enough, the Falcons also only brought two RBs onto their 53-man roster. Having Bijan Robinson probably takes pressure off the need for depth at that position, but HC Kevin Stefanski knows RB injuries from his time in Cleveland. New Orleans Saints Last we have the Saints, and they had a very up-and-down preseason. The first game was a close loss, the second a horrible defeat, and the third a really good win. At times, the position battles looked lost and uninspiring, but game three against the Dallas Cowboys made everyone feel a bit better going into the season. Spencer Rattler ended up winning the backup QB job, Daniel Carlson won the kicker competition, and although Kevin Austin Jr. initially got the last WR spot, he ended up getting released soon after. The main question that still lingers from preseason is the WR room and TE room, because the Saints need to add at least one player in each of those groups. Going into the season with only 4 WRs with the injury luck the Saints have had, and 3 TEs eventhough the team wants to use more TEs this season, makes little sense.

summary: The New Orleans Saints have placed rookie safety Lorenzo Styles Jr. on the Injured Reserve list as he recovers from a calf injury. Styles was a fifth-round selection in this year’s NFL Draft and expected to serve in a large capacity for special teams work. With Styles’ placement on IR, he will miss at least […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - AUGUST 22: New Orleans Saints safety Lorenzo Styles Jr. (36) during the NFL preseason game between New Orleans Saints and the Los Angeles Rams on August 22, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, CA. (Photo by Jevone Moore/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New Orleans Saints have placed rookie safety Lorenzo Styles Jr. on the Injured Reserve list as he recovers from a calf injury. Styles was a fifth-round selection in this year’s NFL Draft and expected to serve in a large capacity for special teams work. With Styles’ placement on IR, he will miss at least the first four games of the season meaning that the earliest he could return would be for New Orleans’ home game versus the Minnesota Vikings. Although Lorenzo was expected to play as a primary gunner role for the Saints, this injury adds another hit to an already thin defensive backfield. In three preseason games, Styles contributed six total tackles, four solo and two assisted, as well as one pass deflection. He was one of six safeties/defensive backs that New Orleans opted to keep on the initial 53-man roster following the final cutdown. In a potentially related move, the New Orleans Saints claimed former Las Vegas Raiders’ DB Decamerion Richardson off of waivers on Tuesday.

title: Saints add WR Cedric Tillman, TE Stone Smartt to practice squad
summary: The New Orleans Saints are adding more experience to their practice squad, as they officially signed wide receiver Cedric Tillman and tight end Stone Smartt on Tuesday. Tillman gives the Saints an intriguing depth option at wide receiver. The six-foot-three receiver was originally selected by the Cleveland Browns in the third round of the 2023 […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - MAY 27: Cedric Tillman #19 of the Cleveland Browns catches a pass during the Cleveland Browns OTA Offseason Workouts at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on May 27, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images The New Orleans Saints are adding more experience to their practice squad, as they officially signed wide receiver Cedric Tillman and tight end Stone Smartt on Tuesday. Tillman gives the Saints an intriguing depth option at wide receiver. The six-foot-three receiver was originally selected by the Cleveland Browns in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft out of Tennessee. He spent three seasons in Cleveland, appearing in 38 games with 19 starts and recording 71 receptions for 833 yards and five touchdowns. Last season, Tillman caught 21 passes for 270 yards and two touchdowns in 13 games. His size and experience could make him an interesting developmental piece for New Orleans, particularly with the release of Kevin Austin Jr. earlier this week. Smartt provides additional depth at tight end. The six-foot-four, 226-pounder spent the first three seasons of his career with the Los Angeles Chargers before joining the New York Jets last season. He’s hauled in 38 receptions for 432 yards and one touchdown across 53 career games. Adding Smartt gives New Orleans another experienced option who can continue developing on the practice squad while remaining available if the team needs additional insurance during the season. The Saints are still constructing their roster ahead of the season opener against the Detroit Lions, so expect to see more moves soon.

title: Saints vs. Cowboys: Game MVP
summary: The Saints were able to finish the preseason with a check in the win column, giving a young locker room its first victory this year. While the game started off strong, with the Saints holding a big lead for the majority of the game, it did get close at the end, and the Saints needed […]
full_text: The Saints were able to finish the preseason with a check in the win column, giving a young locker room its first victory this year. While the game started off strong, with the Saints holding a big lead for the majority of the game, it did get close at the end, and the Saints needed a late field goal from Daniel Carlson to hold on for the win. There were several players who played really well throughout the game. Spencer Rattler had his best game of the preseason. Rattler finished 8-of-10 for 70 yards with zero turnovers. He was pressured four times and sacked once. Rattler also ran the ball twice for nine yards and a touchdown. Zach Wilson also played pretty well. Wilson finished 9-of-12 for 93 yards with zero turnovers. Wilson was also pressured seven times and sacked once. On the defensive side of the ball, safeties Terrell Burgess and Jordan Howden finished as the two highest-graded defenders on PFF. Isaiah Stalbird finished the game leading the team in tackles on defense with eight total tackles. There were several players who truly showed up and played well, but the overall game MVP was Ronnie Bell. Bell finished as the highest-graded player on PFF for the Saints with a 91.7 overall offensive grade. Bell was targeted seven times and had six receptions for 65 yards, with a long of 23 yards and an average of 10.8 yards per reception. Bell definitely made a statement with this game, but unfortunately, it was not enough to earn a spot on the Saints’ roster. Hopefully, scouts will see this tape and he will be able to get another opportunity in league.
author: Anthony Parker

title: Saints’ penalty problem could become costly in 2026
summary: The New Orleans Saints ended the preseason on a high note, defeating the Dallas Cowboys 27-24. After two ugly performances to begin the preseason, the victory provided plenty of reasons for optimism heading into the regular season. However, there is one issue from the preseason that shouldn’t simply be forgotten because of a better showing […]
full_text: The New Orleans Saints ended the preseason on a high note, defeating the Dallas Cowboys 27-24. After two ugly performances to begin the preseason, the victory provided plenty of reasons for optimism heading into the regular season. However, there is one issue from the preseason that shouldn’t simply be forgotten because of a better showing in the finale. Penalties. Through three preseason games, the Saints had 24 accepted penalties for 201 yards. That’s an average of eight penalties and 67 yards per game. The problem was especially noticeable in the first two games. New Orleans committed eight accepted penalties for 66 yards in its preseason-opening loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. Things got considerably worse the following week against the Los Angeles Rams, when the Saints were hit with 12 accepted penalties for 96 yards in a 34-0 blowout loss. That’s a lot of self-inflicted damage, especially for a team trying to establish consistency heading into the regular season. The good news is the Saints cleaned things up against Dallas. They had just four accepted penalties for 39 yards, a significant improvement from the previous two games. That’s enough to make this feel more like a warning sign than a full-blown concern. Preseason games also come with plenty of variables. Young players are getting significant reps, different combinations are playing together and mistakes are more common. It’s reasonable to expect some of those issues to disappear once the regular-season starters are on the field together. But the Saints can’t afford for the penalty problems to follow them into the regular season. Penalties that stall drives, erase positive plays or give opponents extra opportunities can quickly determine the outcome of the game. New Orleans showed against Dallas that it can play a cleaner game. Now they need to make that the standard. So, is it an overreaction to be concerned? Probably, for now. But after 24 accepted penalties in three preseason games, it’s certainly something worth monitoring once the games start counting.

title: NY Giants’ QB Jaxson Dart says team’s defense is ‘best reps I could possibly get’
summary: New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart had the perfect answer on Tuesday when asked about the fact that the Sept. 13 season-opener against the Dallas Cowboys will be his first game action in almost a month. How could the second-year quarterback be sharp? “Every day I’m going against (defensive coordinator) Dennard’s (Wilson) defense, the great […]
full_text: Jaxson Dart talking with Matt Nagy. | Getty Images New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart had the perfect answer on Tuesday when asked about the fact that the Sept. 13 season-opener against the Dallas Cowboys will be his first game action in almost a month. How could the second-year quarterback be sharp? “Every day I’m going against (defensive coordinator) Dennard’s (Wilson) defense, the great players that we have, the scheme that’s in place, and those are some of the best reps that I’m going to get going into Week 1,” Dart said. “So, I’ve been very grateful for those because I would say early on in camp there was a lot of things that maybe caught me by surprise, and against a defense that I haven’t really had a ton of experience playing against. But I think it’s just made myself and this team a lot better, and I don’t take those reps for granted. “So, I feel like those are the best reps I could possibly get each and every day.” Dart played 14 snaps in the Sept. 15 preseason opener against the Minnesota Vikings, and did not appear in the final two preseason games. Head coach John Harbaugh acknowledged the concern about Dart’s lack of playing time in preseason. “We have to make sure the practices are the kind of practices that put pressure on him as much as possible,” Harbaugh said. “So, as game-like as we possibly can make them, so he’s ready to go.” Dart seems to think that is exactly what it happening. Here are more takeaways from Dart’s Tuesday media availability: On Odell Beckham making the team … “I would say it’s pretty nostalgic. Just, as a kid, that’s like an icon, in a way where you feel like he changed the game a little bit. You’re in your backyard as a young kid, talking about, ‘Odell,’ when you catch it one hand, or just things like that. So, that part, it’s a really cool experience. From a player standpoint, really just proud of him. He came in here, he earned it. He got better each and every week, and he’s playing his best ball since he got here right now, from just alignment, assignment, playing fast, getting open, making plays. So, really proud of him, and just the dedication that he’s put in to get into this point. And he’s a great teammate as well. So, there’s a lot that we, as younger guys, can learn from him. And he’s still a great player.” On when he knew Beckham could still play … “I think I started to realize that, probably like when you said, just the extra work that we put in in the offseason where – you hear stories like this and you don’t really know how dedicated somebody’s going to be when they walk into a situation like this because he’s damn near had it all, right? He’s experienced and had so much success. But I knew he was serious when he’s flying out across the country to come throw with me, to get those extra reps in. And when you just have that one-on-one time, you see his talent and the things that make him a special player. So, I think just from those experiences and him growing each and every week, you realize that he’s still got it.” On what he likes about the team’s new offense … “There’s just a lot of answers. There’s a lot of plays that you can get to. There’s a lot of options that you can get to, and it lets us just go out there and play football. It lets the creators that we have make plays, get open in space, and us just being on the same page and getting a ton of reps has really helped. And I definitely feel like we’ve taken a lot of really big strides.” On his progress from the spring … “I feel so much better. I feel in command. I feel confident. In this offense, there’s a lot that’s put on the quarterback’s plate, but it’s exactly how I want it. It’s exactly how I viewed this coming together. And we still have a lot of room to improve and grow as a unit, but I’m definitely feeling way better each and every day, continuing to learn, continuing to grow as a player, and just the comfort in the offense, seeing the defense and putting ourselves in great situations. On potentially having Malik Nabers in the lineup Week 1 … “He’s just a game-changing player. So, whenever he’s out there on the field, whenever his time is ready for us as a team, I think it’s going to change a lot, and I can’t wait for that time to come. But at the same time, I think that we’ve done a really good job of putting ourselves in position to be ready and be prepared for any situation that may come our way. “So, guys have stepped up and done a really good job, and like I said, whenever his time is to come back, we’re all going to be really excited, and he’s a game-changing player.”
author: Ed Valentine

full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know for your Wednesday morning. 2026 NFL Rank: Predicting top 100 players for this season | ESPN.com 82. Andrew Thomas. Thomas is entering a season healthy for the first time in years. And when he’s healthy, he’s one of the league’s best left tackles. His 92.3% pass block win rate is the fifth best among all left tackles over the past three seasons. There is no reason to think that will dip with Thomas healthy and in his prime. Signature stat: Last season, Thomas was one of three offensive tackles to rank in the top 15 of pass block win rate and run block win rate. The other two were the Rams’ Warren McClendon Jr. and the Vikings’ Brian O’Neill. 81. Brian Burns. Burns is coming off a career-best 16.5 sacks and looks even better this summer. “He does so many things well, he’s going to excel,” said new coach John Harbaugh about Burns’ prospects in new coordinator Dennard Wilson’s defense. Burns also shouldn’t be getting a ton of double-teams with the continued development of Abdul Carter. He was doubled at a rate of just over 13% last season. Signature stat: Burns had the second-most sacks in the NFL last season, which marked the most by a Giants player in a single season since Jason Pierre-Paul’s 16.5 in 2011. OBJ in 13 again Odell Beckham works on Tuesday in his familiar No. 13 jersey. pic.twitter.com/2QxGiZIxMA — Big Blue View (@bigblueview) September 1, 2026 Giants Roster Breakdown: A look at John Harbaugh’s group heading into 2026 NFL season | SNY.tv Carter had a tremendous first week in West Virginia. Then the pads came on and Thomas did what he does to most people on Sundays and erased him. There were entire practices where you’d forget Carter was out there. That sounds alarming, until Carter started tormenting the interior of the Giants line once Wilson began moving him around as the team plans to on game days. Burns is still Burns — a stud. Thibodeaux is one of the better third rushers in the NFL. This group isn’t just the strength of the Giants, but one of the best in the NFL. The key, though, is in the Giants providing them obvious situations to rush the quarterback. New York Giants’ Dennard Wilson needs his blitz to bite in The Big Apple | USAToday.com New York Giants defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson will have his work cut out for him in 2026. Working alongside veteran head coach John Harbaugh, Wilson will look to improve the team’s defensive foundation and restore the physical tenacity that built the franchise’s reputation. Last season, the Giants finished No. 26 in points allowed per game, tied for No. 15 in total team sacks, and were mid-tier versus the pass, ranking No. 16 in opponent pass yards per game. Wilson’s defensive strategy will base out of 3-4 and nickel personnel groups in 2026. Versus the Washington Commanders and Dallas Cowboys, who are both NFC East rivals, Wilson will have his pass defense greatly tested. Generic man coverages and soft-zone won’t be enough to inhibit these particular teams because their high-powered offensive attacks are heavily talent-based. Therefore, Wilson will want to implement blitz packages and shell concepts to create negative plays and potentially force turnovers. The Giants had just nine interceptions last season, and Wilson’s stint with the Tennessee Titans only produced six interceptions in 2024. 26 people who will define the NFL in 2026 | SB Nation Jaxson Dart, QB — New York Giants. The Giants enter this season with unbelievable hype behind them. For the first time in a decade it feels like they’re ready to compete, but that requires Jaxson Dart to step his game up in 2026. Dart garnered unbelievable hype during his rookie campaign, but it was a profoundly up-and-down year by the numbers. It was decent for a rookie, but there will need to be some major progression in year two in order to have faith in Dart as the signal caller long term. It’s not just about how he plays on the field, but how well he can adapt to a more demanding, exacting football coach in John Harbaugh. If this fits together then the Giants can be contenders in the NFC East — if it doesn’t, well, it will be another long season for the G-Men. NFC East Preview: Is This the Cowboys’ Year? | The Ringer If you are a Giants fan and want to believe that this team can be frisky and compete for a wild-card spot this season, go for it. There’s a scenario in which Harbaugh shows he’s still got it, Dart is an exciting playmaker (and stays healthy), and Carter emerges as a Defensive Player of the Year candidate. But I can’t get there. Harbaugh did not look like a great coach with the Ravens last year. I need to see a lot more from Dart before believing that he can be a real difference maker. This roster still has a lot of holes and lacks depth. And I’m not sure that the offensive coaching staff will be able to do more with less. This feels more like a transition year in which Harbaugh figures out which guys he wants to build with going forward. Projected record: 6-11 National insider picks Giants to win NFC East View this post on Instagram Grading every NFL team’s 2026 preseason | CBSSports.com New York Giants Grade: B. The wide receiver room garnered a lot of attention this preseason, largely due to Odell Beckham Jr. and Malik Nabers. Beckham made the team after a solid showing in the preseason, setting the stage for a feel-good story as he writes his final chapter. That said, Nabers is the bigger story. The star receiver has made tremendous strides in his recovery from an ACL tear he suffered last season, and could be available as soon as Week 1. That’s a major development for an offense looking to take a step forward in Year 2 of Jaxson Dart. Of course, Dart staying out of the blue medical tent will be a key focus, and he did find his way in there during the preseason. The backfield, while deep, does have some questions. Cam Skattebo caught the ire of John Harbaugh, who called him “infectious” and not in a glowing manner. Meanwhile, Najee Harris was added to the room after Tyrone Tracy Jr. struggled mightily out of the gate. title: NY Giants, Malik Nabers seem uncertain about his availability for Week 1
summary: EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — Malik Nabers did not follow what has become his usual practice routine on Tuesday. Nabers was not on the field at the beginning of practice for stretching warmups and individual drills. Instead, he remained inside with training staff. Reporters passed Nabers, in full uniform and headed to the field, while leaving […]
full_text: Malik Nabers | Getty Images EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — Malik Nabers did not follow what has become his usual practice routine on Tuesday. Nabers was not on the field at the beginning of practice for stretching warmups and individual drills. Instead, he remained inside with training staff. Reporters passed Nabers, in full uniform and headed to the field, while leaving at the conclusion of the media viewing period. That was roughly 20 minutes into practice. With hopes having risen that the star wide receiver, recovering from a torn ACL, could play in the Sept. 13 season-opener against the Dallas Cowboys, should the change in routine raise alarm bells regarding Nabers’ Week 1 availability? Head coach John Harbaugh downplayed the significance of the change in routine, calling it “just part of the process” as Nabers recovers from the pair of surgeries he had to repair his knee. “It’s just day-to-day. That’s up to the trainers,” Harbaugh said. “They let us know what he’s ready for at a certain time, so it’s part of the process.” Harbaugh said Nabers took “most of the team reps” after coming out to the practice field. Nabers seemed a bit cryptic when asked on Monday how he was physically. “I’m going to keep the checkpoints in-house,” Nabers said. “It’s not really anything too big, but like I said, I’m going to keep it more in-house and just to myself. “I feel real good, to be honest. But like I said, you’re going to feel good, but there’s still some things that you still have to check off the box for you to participate. So, I’m still going through that, still listening to the trainers, still listening to doctors and sharing everything with them.” John Harbaugh references The Odd Couple when talking about the Giants planning around Malik Nabers' injury and potential availability: "We've got to plan for every outcome." pic.twitter.com/IdJKz5a5EU — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) September 1, 2026 Time is, of course, growing short. Week 1 is less than two weeks away. “We’ve got to plan for every outcome,” Harbaugh said. “So we have to plan that he’ll be there fully. We’ll have to plan that he’s not there at all, and we’ll have to plan that he’s there for some partial amount, and every kind of amount in between.” Harbaugh admitted the uncertainty “makes it tough” to prepare. “You never know if a player’s going to be available or not, because anything can happen,” Harbaugh said. “Things can happen first play of the game, last play of the game, whatever. “Someone’s got to be ready to come in and step in, so you don’t overthink that. You just prepare for it, and you have guys ready to play.” Could Nabers play in a limited capacity? “How much he can play and in what capacity? That’s exactly what we’re looking at,” Harbaugh said. “Is he going to be where he needs to be to help us win? And then he has to be confident. Of course, he’s got to be confident. “Because for him to play at the level he’s going to need to play for us to win and protect himself, he’s going to have to feel good about it. He’s got to feel like he’s there. He’s got to know he’s there. To me, that’s just going to be an ongoing conversation right throughout. “When you come back from an injury, whether it’s long-term or even short-term, where do we stand with the doctors, the trainers, the player? How does he look on tape? What do the numbers say? How fast is he running?” Nabers himself doesn’t seem certain how this will play out. “That would be a decision that would be made when that time comes,” he said. “Like I said, the outside view, I might look like I’m one hundred percent. I make everything look well. I mean, sometimes I run routes and I go look on the internet and I’m like, ‘Dang, I was moving kind of crazy.’ “But when you’re in your body and you’re in it, you still have some things that you still got to work on as a football player that you got to be like, I don’t feel right doing this cut, I don’t feel right, I haven’t been hit, I haven’t seen this. So, it’s certain things that you just got to, as a forward player, you got to mentally prepare that before you go into a game and then everybody’s just seeing you. So, if you make a mistake, it’s all broadcast, so nobody really knows. So, it’s like, I want to be able to come out there and make no mistakes and just be able to fly around and do what I do. So, I’m getting there for sure. I’m getting there.” Will he get there fast enough for opening night? Stay tuned.

title: NY Giants add 4 more players to complete their practice squad
summary: EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — The New York Giants filled out their practice squad on Tuesday by signing four players. The Giants added wide receiver/kick returner Charlie Jones , cornerback Elijah Jones, and offensive linemen Kingsley Eguakun and Darian Kinnard. Charles Jones, 27, was a fourth-round pick by the Cincinnati Bengals in 2023. He caught eight […]
full_text: Charlie Jones with the Bengals during the preseason. | Getty Images EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — The New York Giants filled out their practice squad on Tuesday by signing four players. The Giants added wide receiver/kick returner Charlie Jones , cornerback Elijah Jones , and offensive linemen Kingsley Eguakun and Darian Kinnard . Charles Jones, 27, was a fourth-round pick by the Cincinnati Bengals in 2023. He caught eight passes in 33 games while also returning punts and kickoffs. Jones has averaged 9.2 yards on 50 career punt returns, and 27.3 yards on 47 kickoff returns. The Giants also have wide receiver/kick returner Braxton Berrios on their practice squad. John Harbaugh said Monday that Berrios would be the team’s primary return man in the season-opener against the Dallas Cowboys. Jones, though, clearly offers the Giants depth in the return game. Elijah Jones was a third-round pick by the Arizona Cardinals in 2024. He spent his rookie season on injured reserve. He played in 10 games last season, with 37 defensive snaps and 68 on special teams. He had three tackles and two pass breakups. Elijah Jones is a 6-foot-1, 185-pound 26-year-old. Eguakun is a 6-foot-3, 305-pound center. A former undrafted free agent, he spent 2024 on the Detroit Lions’ practice squad. He was waived by the Lions at the end of last season, and picked up by the Cleveland Browns. Cleveland waived him this week when rosters were cut to the 53-man regular-season limit. Eguakun, 25, will add center depth to the practice squad. Kinnard, 26, was waived by the Green Bay Packers in roster cutdowns. Kinnard was a fifth-round pick by the Kansas City Chiefs in the 2022 NFL Draft. Kinnard has played in 20 NFL games. Seventeen of those, including four starts, came last season with the Packers. The 6-5, 322-pound Kinnard is primarily a right tackle. title: Are the Giants getting better at drafting?
summary: There are multiple reasons why an NFL team fairly consistently finishes a season well below .500 as the New York Giants mostly have since 2017, but first and foremost, it’s because they don’t have enough good players. The NFL Draft is the primary mechanism by which teams build their roster. The Giants’ fall from grace, […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FL - AUGUST 22: New York Giants linebacker Arvell Reese (52) defends near the line of scrimmage during the preseason NFL game between the New York Giants and the Miami Dolphins on Saturday, August 22, 2026 at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami, FL (Photo by Peter Joneleit/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images There are multiple reasons why an NFL team fairly consistently finishes a season well below .500 as the New York Giants mostly have since 2017, but first and foremost, it’s because they don’t have enough good players. The NFL Draft is the primary mechanism by which teams build their roster. The Giants’ fall from grace, so to speak, after their 2016 playoff appearance can be traced to some extent to draft successes vs. failures. Let’s try to get a handle on that. I used Pro Football Reference’s weighted Approximate Value (wAV) statistics for each Giants draft since 2016 to get an idea of how productive their drafts have been in their last nine drafts spanning three general managers. Like any quantitative metric, wAV has its strengths and weaknesses, but it tries to capture the combination of good play and availability, emphasizing a player’s best years more than his worst. Since it is cumulative, wAV increases with a player’s time in the league. Here are the summed wAVs for each of the Giants’ last nine draft classes: In general wAV should increase with time since the draft took place, i.e., the 2017 number is the accumulation of nine years of play while that for 2025 is for that season only. Furthermore, it reflects a player’s entire career, not just the time he spent as a Giant. Nonetheless it is some kind of indicator of draft success. The deviation from the trend line in any year is what tells the story. The Giants’ downfall began in 2017, when the Giants used their first round pick on Evan Engram rather than players such as T.J. Watt and Ryan Ramczyk who were still on the board. Dalvin Tomlinson in Round 3 and Wayne Gallman in Round 4 were productive pros, but the Giants got no elite players from that draft. That is reflected by the class wAV, which is about 40 below the trend lime. 2018 was much better with the pick of Saquon Barkley, even though in retrospect the Giants really should have take Josh Allen – the excess value from that draft roughly cancelled the deficit from 2017. 2019 was arguably the best draft of the Dave Gettleman era despite Daniel Jones only getting the Giants to the playoffs once and the trade-up for Deandre Baker being a disaster. In addition to Jones, who has thrived as a Colt, the Giants got Dexter Lawrence, Julian Love and Darius Slayton from that draft. 2020 was also a little better than average because of the Andrew Thomas and Xavier McKinney picks, but little benefit came from the Giants’ other 8 picks that year. Still, the Giants were building something promising. That’s three consecutive good drafts, which should have put the Giants on the verge of playoff contention. Then came 2021 and the ill-fated trade-down by Gettleman. It’s not worth re-hashing the details. Suffice to say, though, as pointed out by BBV member Madhops in The Feed, that with Azeez Ojulari and Gary Brightwell being cut this weekend, at the moment there is not a single member of the Giants’ 2021 draft class active in the NFL – only five years after the draft took place. What an indictment of Gettleman’s strategy that year. In fairness, I was as surprised as anyone that the Cowboys would hand DeVonta Smith to a division rival. However, Gettleman’s failure to “settle” for Rashawn Slater or Micah Parsons, even though he got a great haul of picks, can be seen as what has kept the franchise down most of the time since then. (Fun fact: After Gettleman selected Kadarius Toney at No. 20, Najee Harris went at No. 24 and Greg Newsome at No. 26.) You can see from the figure that the Giants’ 2021 draft class wAV is about 60 points below the trend line that reflects what a “typical” wAV for that draft class should be by now. That’s roughly equivalent to the wAVs of Parsons (67, highest in that class), Penei Sewell (64), and Ja’Marr Chase (58). Basically 2021 wiped out the effect of the excess draft value Gettleman had accumulated in 2019 and 2020 and it showed in the team’s performance. Part of that was Daniel Jones’ neck injury, but the lack of talent elsewhere was revealed when he went down. Giants fans tend to be critical of the picks of new general manager Joe Schoen in 2022, but you can see from the figure that they account for about 40 points of excess wAV over that expected. Schoen got no blue chip players from that draft, but Kayvon Thibodeaux and Wan’Dale Robinson were both productive players their first four years. Furthermore, the extra picks inherited from Gettleman plus Schoen’s two trade-downs for extra picks (11 total) yielded a few other players who started and played well or at least adequately (Cor’Dale Flott, Dane Belton, Daniel Bellinger; even Evan Neal started for parts of three seasons). The result is that the total wAV from that draft is now about 40 points higher than expected. You can get a better sense of average player quality by plotting wAV per pick per year instead: Looked at in this way, we can say that 2022 was actually an average draft year. Most of these 11 draftees are now gone, but Robinson and Flott signed lucrative contracts with Tennessee, along with Bellinger, while Belton moved from one MetLife team to the other. Only Thibodeaux and Micah McFadden (a good value in the 5th round even though he’s a backup now) remain Giants, but as a group those 11 players are much better than the 2021 group that Gettleman chose. 2023 was a different story. You can see from both diagrams above that Schoen’s second class is below average, both in total wAV and wAV per pick per year. Jalin Hyatt was brought back on the practice squad, but unless the coaching staff performs a miracle, this draft will hinge on whether Deonte Banks can become the performer his first round status suggested he should become, and whether WYSIWYG now from John Michael Schmitz., i.e., an adequate center but nothing more. JMS has a wAV of 14, which is at or slightly below average for a starter the way PFR calculates things. The rest of the class is now gone from the Giants after only three years, which itself is quite a statement about the quality of that draft. The 2024 draft class is still TBD, because its second year was a big disappointment compared to its first. You can say that Malik Nabers was a no-brainer at No. 6 after Caleb Williams, Jayden Daniels and Drake Maye came off the board, but give Schoen credit for not being seduced by the chance to solve the Giants’ quarterback problem with J.J. McCarthy, Michael Penix, or Bo Nix (the last of whom has admittedly had a very good start to his NFL career) and for choosing Nabers over Rome Odunze. The rest of this draft is a Rorschach test. You can look at Tyler Nubin, Dru Phillips, Theo Johnson, and Tyrone Tracy Jr. and see four promising players who might be big contributors to this year’s Giants. You can also look at them and see a safety who can’t play the run and has not intercepted a pass in two NFL seasons after being a ballhawk in college; a cornerback who is a demon close to the line of scrimmage but is very vulnerable in pass coverage downfield; an athletic tight end who is a threat to take it all the way after catching a pass but who is also a threat to drop the pass; and a running back who has posted 1,000+ yards of offense in each of his first two seasons but who has a disturbing tendency to cough the ball up. Darius Muasau was cut on Sunday but he is a reasonable player for a Round 6 pick who was claimed by the Patriots. By the end of this season we may either consider this Schoen’s first great draft, or another disappointment to go with 2022 and 2023. At the moment, though, it has the highest wAV per pick per year by far because every single one of the…

title: Odell Beckham Jr. will wear number 13
summary: It’s safe to get your classic Odell Beckham Jr. jerseys out of the closet. The New York Giants have announced that the veteran receiver is once again wearing number 13. Beckham said on Monday that there would be “conversations” with WR Jalin Hyatt, who has worn number 13 since 2023. “I think we all know […]
full_text: New York Giants receiver Odell Beckham Jr. catches a pass﻿ | Getty Images It’s safe to get your classic Odell Beckham Jr. jerseys out of the closet. The New York Giants have announced that the veteran receiver is once again wearing number 13. Beckham said on Monday that there would be “conversations” with WR Jalin Hyatt, who has worn number 13 since 2023. “I think we all know what that means to me, and there definitely will be some conversations,” Beckham said. “I’ll just say we’ll see what happens, but like I said, it would be an honor and a privilege to put that back on.” It seems those conversations were fruitful. OBJ back in 13 pic.twitter.com/CqVBiaI09n — New York Giants (@Giants) September 1, 2026 Beckham wore number 3 throughout camp and preseason, the number he wore as a collegiate receiver at LSU. However, it’s just fitting that he would want the number in which he rewrote the record books for the Giants. Beckham wasn’t the only receiver to get a new number, with rookie Malachi Fields swapping in his “0” jersey for “88”. Fields never wore 88 in college, playing as number 86 and 8 at Virginia and 0 at Notre Dame. However, it’s also fitting that Fields swapped to 88, considering he has been compared to Hakeem Nicks since being drafted. The number has largely laid fallow since Nicks’ 2011 season, with the exception of Evan Engram’s stint from 2017 to 2021. Nick’s run until his injury in 2012 still leaves big shoes for the rookie to fill, but his preseason was certainly promising.

title: Malik Nabers – ‘I’m getting there’ after dark days in the offseason
summary: There has been a lot to watch over the course of the 2026 off-season for the New York Giants. But other than the pursuit and hiring of John Harbaugh, there really hasn’t been a bigger story than WR Malik Nabers’ recovery from the torn ACL that ended his 2025 season. Fans didn’t know what to […]
full_text: Malik Nabers | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect There has been a lot to watch over the course of the 2026 off-season for the New York Giants. But other than the pursuit and hiring of John Harbaugh, there really hasn’t been a bigger story than WR Malik Nabers’ recovery from the torn ACL that ended his 2025 season. Fans didn’t know what to expect from his recovery, and whether he would be able to participate in training camp. Then it was revealed that he had a second surgery to clean up scar tissue, fans doubted whether Nabers would even be able to start the 2026 season. So did Nabers. “I thought I would probably never run a route again, just how the stuff was going,” Nabers said after practice on Monday. “But I’ve made it here, I’ve been through the hard stuff. So, I feel like there’s nothing in my life that I can’t overcome. And the step that I’m going to take forward is going to be better than before. And will it take me some time? Who knows. But I know for sure if I’m out there, I’m going to run some routes for sure.” Nabers has had the unwavering support of the Giants’ organization, who have been both patient and methodical in how they’ve managed his rehab. He’s also had the support of the locker room, including a fellow LSU alum who’s walked a similar path. Odell Beckham Jr. knows what it’s like to be a star receiver working to overcome a bad knee injury. Nabers has said that the veteran has been a constant presence, supporting him, sharing wisdom, and providing encouragement. “He’s come up many times and just asking me about the rehab process,” Nabers said of Beckham. “Trying to give me tips and things to do that helped him during his rehab, and asking me to continue, to ask what I’m doing, telling me I can do more. ‘You can do more.’ He wanted to see me back out there.” Perhaps not solely due to Beckham’s encouragement, but reporters have consistently remarked that Nabers has practiced more intensely than expected. And while Nabers’ reps in practice were managed, he responded well to the work and steadily ramped up over the course of training camp. “I feel real good, to be honest,” he said, contrasting with the dark thoughts he grappled with earlier in the off-season. “But like I said, you’re going to feel good, but there’s still some things that you still have to check off the box for you to participate,” he added. “So, I’m still going through that, still listening to the trainers, still listening to doctors and sharing everything with them.” It was something of a surprise that Nabers avoided the PUP list entirely, and was ready to start training camp. It wasn’t, however, a surprise that Nabers never took part in preseason games. That, he insists, was never a target for him or the Giants. Instead, the focus has been on being healthy for the regular season. Like John Harbaugh and Joe Schoen, Nabers wouldn’t commit to being ready Week 1 to play against the against the Dallas Cowboys. “My mind is focused on playing the regular season, playing whenever that is and playing what team it is,” he said. The plan is currently to make sure that Nabers is ready to be a star receiver when he retakes the field. “I’m going to be making sure that I’m ready to go out there and I’m healthy enough to play all four quarters,” he added. “So, that’s the main focus is just trying to be out there as much as I can.” Right now, Nabers seems to be in the process of relearning how to trust his body. “I might look like I’m one hundred percent. I make everything look well. I mean, sometimes I run routes and I go look on the internet and I’m like, ‘Dang, I was moving kind of crazy’,” he said. “But when you’re in your body and you’re in it, you still have some things that you still got to work on as a football player that you got to be like, I don’t feel right doing this cut, I don’t feel right, I haven’t been hit, I haven’t seen this.” He added that he wants to be able to play without mistakes or hesitations when he gets back on the field. “So, it’s like, I want to be able to come out there and make no mistakes and just be able to fly around and do what I do. So, I’m getting there for sure. I’m getting there.” Reporters did note that Nabers had shed the red non-contact jersey during practice on Monday. “I’ve heard a lot of people say it takes a little while for you to feel better,” Nabers said. “But I’ve put in countless hours of work, I’ve put in many nights. I’ve sat in rooms, cried. I did everything to get to this moment right here. So, I feel like when I get out there, I feel like I’ll be better than what I was before. I’ve put in work, I’ve went through everything that I could just to get to this moment.”

title: Prognosticating the 2026 Jets
summary: Right now, depending on where you look in Vegas, the Jets’ O/U sits at 5.5 wins. With the odds leaning toward the over, the Jets’ projected win total by Vegas is likely modeled somewhere in the ~5.7 to 5.8 range. As everyone is aware, that isn’t great! But as always, although there’s a lot of […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 09: (NEW YORK DAILIES OUT) Breece Hall #20 and Armand Membou #70 of the New York Jets in action against the Cleveland Browns at MetLife Stadium on November 09, 2025 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The Jets defeated the Browns 27-20. (Photo by Jim McIsaac/Getty Images) | Getty Images Right now, depending on where you look in Vegas, the Jets’ O/U sits at 5.5 wins. With the odds leaning toward the over, the Jets’ projected win total by Vegas is likely modeled somewhere in the ~5.7 to 5.8 range. As everyone is aware, that isn’t great! But as always, although there’s a lot of predictive value in using Vegas projections, the market is frequently wrong. Just take a look at last year. The Seahawks exceeded their preseason win total by 6 games, the Jaguars by nearly 6 as well, and the Broncos by 5. Meanwhile, teams like the Chiefs, Cardinals, and Commanders all disappointed by at least 5 wins from their preseason expectations. After doing some thinking, I’ve made some cases for the Jets on either side of the spectrum. How can they vastly overperform their ~6 win expectation this year, and how can they vastly underperform it? Although injuries might be the main component that drives teams to startling differences from preseason projections, I won’t even attempt to prognosticate them here. These “stories” won’t have injuries factored in. These scenarios also have varying degrees of likelihood. I don’t want to write about something that I think has less than a 1% chance of happening, but I’ll also warn you that I’m not going to act like either scenario is incredibly likely. Let’s take a look at what could happen this year that would allow the Jets to meaningfully differ from their preseason projection. We’ll follow up with the negative version in our next article, but for now let’s take a look at the positive case: The Positive Spin How can the Jets meaningfully overachieve this season in a somewhat plausible way? In my opinion, it’s going to start in the trenches. The Jets enter the season with major question marks at head coach, offensive coordinator, and quarterback. That’s not an ideal trio to have questions about entering the season, and it’s obviously a major reason why the Jets’ projection is sitting where it is. So how can the Jets overcome those question marks? Competent offensive line play. I don’t have a full-scale research study to back this up, but I do know off the top of my head that historically, offensive lines are a huge barometer for raising an offense’s floor. I took a quick look at last year’s numbers and examined how every team that ranked in the top 10 in offensive line play by PFF finished as an offense. As you might expect, the results were strong. Out of the top 10 offensive lines last year, every single one had a league-average or better offense except for the Giants, who ranked 22nd by DVOA. If you expand the analysis even further, even having a league-average offensive line pretty much guaranteed that your offense wouldn’t be a complete dumpster fire. Every offense with a PFF offensive line ranking of 16th or better finished 23rd or higher in offensive DVOA. None were amongst the leagues worst. The evidence is clear; a good offensive line can give an otherwise questionable offense a much higher floor. For the Jets, there’s a legitimate story to sell yourself on this offensive line. There’s been a lot of high-quality investment in the unit over the past few seasons and, on paper, there theoretically should be a lot of potential. Armand Membou just turned 22, and between his rookie season and his collegiate pedigree, he has as good a chance as anyone on this roster to break out into a legitimate top-tier tackle sooner rather than later. Olu Fashanu is only 23 and now has two straight years where he’s graded at least average. He’s another guy where it wouldn’t be shocking to see him take another leap. Then you have the 25-year-old Joe Tippmann, who theoretically should be entering his prime and has already proven to be a capable, average guard at this level. With Dylan Parham, who should also be entering his prime, and Josh Myers at the other two positions, you have two guys who, while not world beaters, shouldn’t be bad enough to sink the rest of the offensive line. The floor is less stable than some of the other offensive lines in the league, but there is a realistic story where this line looks like a borderline top-10 unit as early as this year. Brandon Thorn of Bleacher Report had the Jets at 15th going into the offseason, while a super bullish analysis from Joseph Bryan, formerly of Pro Football Focus, had the Jets at 6th. 🧱Predicted 2026 NFL Offensive Line Rankings🧱 The Offensive Line can be CRITICAL for fantasy success Using PFF Pass Block & Run Block grades, age, draft capital, and some light time series I predicted 2026 Pass Block & Run Block rankings for every team! pic.twitter.com/iw2K2PiNXl — Joseph Bryan (@KoalatyStats) August 19, 2026 Bottom line, if this unit does hit its potential this year, it should be a top-half-of-the-league unit. The offensive line also matters a bit more because of the uncertainty at quarterback. We don’t need to rehash it, but Geno Smith was awful behind an awful offensive line last year despite three seasons prior of league-average to better play in Seattle. Since becoming a full-time starter in 2022, Geno has consistently been one of the better operators from clean pockets, regularly ranking highly in accuracy percentage in clean situations. A potential bounce-back year could realistically happen if this offensive line holds up, especially with a healthy Garrett Wilson and young-upside pass catchers like Adonai Mitchell, Omar Cooper, Mason Taylor, and Kenyon Sadiq, who should all get plenty of opportunities this year. And none of this even mentions a defense that will likely begin Week 1 with 8-9 new starters. Never say never, but it would be almost impossible for this defense to play as poorly as it did last year. Minkah Fitzpatrick, Demario Davis, and David Onyemata are veterans, and it remains to be seen how much each has left in the tank. But all three were effective players last year and should theoretically be major floor raisers for the unit. From a turnover perspective, we already discussed how it would be borderline unheard of for the Jets not to get strong improvement on that front. It legitimately cannot get worse from an interception perspective. And recent history shows that the Jets should significantly outperform last year in terms of forcing turnovers. Then there’s David Bailey, the prize acquisition of this offseason. By all accounts through camp and the preseason, Bailey appears to be a guy who is ready to make a major impact immediately. If the No. 2 pick can be a legitimate NFL-caliber edge rusher in Year 1, which according to all reports should be the expectation, the Jets should be pairing a capable offensive line with a top-half defensive line, especially with the depth they possess at defensive tackle. So what does all of this lead us to? In this scenario, the Jets would almost assuredly overachieve their 6-win projection and become a scrappy Wild Card contender. The offense, led by a good offensive line and a collection of young pass catchers, would project to be at least an average unit. Meanwhile, a defense with improved talent and some regression to the mean from a turnover perspective would also be wildly improved. It would be a pleasant surprise for Jets fans: a bunch of young players taking steps forward, a competent offensive line giving the offense a chance, and a defense that led by their front 7 experiences major improvement on the turnover front. That’s a pretty easy recipe for going from 5-6 wins to 8-10 wins. That’s likely how the Jets overachieve their preseason projection. I’m not saying this scenario is the most likely one, but I also don’t think there’s no chance it happens.
