title: Which position group is the deepest for the 49ers?
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year, we ask questions of the most plugged-in 49ers fans and fans across the country. The San Francisco 49ers released their initial 53-man roster and continue to maneuver to complete the final 53 before they clash with the Los Angeles Rams […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - JANUARY 20: Fred Warner #54 of the San Francisco 49ers celebrates with Dre Greenlaw #57 of the San Francisco 49ers during an NFL divisional round playoff football game between the San Francisco 49ers and the Green Bay Packers at Levi's Stadium on January 20, 2024 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year, we ask questions of the most plugged-in 49ers fans and fans across the country. The San Francisco 49ers released their initial 53-man roster and continue to maneuver to complete the final 53 before they clash with the Los Angeles Rams in Australia next week. The concerns about certain position groups have either been answered or ignored, depending on who you ask. After a full training camp and preseason, four position groups are a strength for the 49ers, two on each side of the ball. Here are the deepest position groups for the 49ers: Offense Wide Receiver Yes, Ricky Pearsall will miss the 2026 season, and Mike Evans has dealt with various injuries before taking a single snap, but the receiver group actually feels safe with proven commodities. De’Zhaun Stribling’s preseason and usage are such a boost, as is Deebo Samuel’s return with the veteran presence of Demarcus Robinson. The top three receiver options should be Evans, Stribling, and Samuel, in that order. Jordan Watkins and Jacob Cowing fill out the back end of the group, and there is Christian Kirk, who is eligible to return after four weeks. It would have been even better if Pearsall was available, but still this group feels far more solid than expected before training camp began. Running Back Christian McCaffrey returns to what can only be assumed as his normal role as the workhorse, but the emergence of both Kaelon Black and Jordan James gives the 49ers confidence in case of an injury to McCaffrey. Even if the 49ers and Kyle Shanahan want to use Black or James as a change of pace, the rookie and second-year running back have looked great in preseason, and who finishes as the RB2 will depend on pass protection. Now, the 49ers are only carrying four running backs, including Kyle Juszczyk, but Samuel is the fifth running back and gives the team a ton of flexibility in personnel and play calling. The confidence comes from the fact that any of the options behind McCaffrey are capable and bring different things to the offense. Defense Cornerback The 49ers’ top three options in a perfect world would be Deommodore Lenoir, Renardo Green, and Upton Stout. Green is dealing with an injury, and the hope is he will be ready for Week 1, but if he isn’t, veteran Jack Jones has shown plenty in the preseason as a ball hawk. Generally, when a starting cornerback went down, the options weren’t exactly appealing, but even if Jones takes risks as a cornerback, he provides a safety net. Having three starters and a reliable veteran is a strength for Raheem Morris and the 49ers defense. Linebackers Fred Warner and Dre Greenlaw lead the room, but the question marks behind the two starters feel answered. Jaden Dugger, Garret Wallow, and Luke Gifford are perfect depth pieces. Nick Martin begins the season on IR, and Tatum Bethune has experience from last season. By no means am I implying that if Warner or Greenlaw miss significant time, the 49ers will be fine, but if one is down with a replacement from depth, the team is in a better spot now than expected heading into training camp. title: Former 49ers corner was the most claimed player on waiver wire by far on Monday
summary: The San Francisco 49ers lost only two of their players to the waiver wire on Monday as they cut down from 53 players and settled on their practice squad. One of them, undrafted rookie Bryson Eason, was a player who could’ve made the practice squad, but the Kansas City Chiefs scooped him up after seeing […]
full_text: Aug 23, 2024; Paradise, Nevada, USA; San Francisco 49ers cornerback Darrell Luter Jr. (28) against the Las Vegas Raiders in the first half at Allegiant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con The San Francisco 49ers lost only two of their players to the waiver wire on Monday as they cut down from 53 players and settled on their practice squad. One of them, undrafted rookie Bryson Eason, was a player who could’ve made the practice squad, but the Kansas City Chiefs scooped him up after seeing his preseason tape. The other? Cornerback Darrell Luter Jr., who was claimed by the Las Vegas Raiders with the top spot on the waiver wire. Luter was a fifth-round pick by the 49ers in the 2023 NFL Draft, and he made the 49ers 53-man roster in each of the first three years of his NFL career. While injuries were prevalent earlier in his career, Luter played in all 17 games last year, starting three, while playing a key role on special teams. The 49ers ended up keeping six cornerbacks, but Luter wasn’t one of them. Instead, they had Deommodore Lenoir, Renardo Green, Upton Stout, Jack Jones, Ephysians Prysock, and Nate Hobbs make the 53-man roster. Green, Prysock, and Hobbs are all dealing with injuries, and Hobbs was reverted to Injured Reserve with a designation to return after making the initial 53. Perhaps the 49ers were hoping to bring back Luter on the practice squad, but he was actually the most-claimed player on the waiver wire on Monday, and it wasn’t close. While the Raiders, who had top priority, submitted only one waiver claim overall, the Tennessee Titans, Miami Dolphins, Dallas Cowboys, and Indianapolis Colts all attempted to claim Luter as well. No other player who was waived had more than two claims on them by a team, according to ESPN’s Field Yates. Luter ended up with a clear chance to play early on the Raiders, while the 49ers signed back Jakob Robinson to the practice squad as the lone additional cornerback. With their current injury situation, the 49ers may need to add another body ahead of Week 1 for practice situations, but their 2023 fifth-round pick is no longer on the roster following another busy cutdown day.

full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - JULY 27: Mike Evans #5 of the San Francisco 49ers works out during training camp practice at SAP Performance Facility on July 27, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images San Francisco 49ers general manager John Lynch provided a few injury updates on KNBR Tuesday morning. Lynch confirmed that Nick Bosa worked on the side of practice on Monday and that’ll be the plan for Tuesday as well: “On Wednesday, he wants to get out on the field. We’ve been working in conjunction with Nick on the best plan, he’s been doing great work to the side, Nick has always had a great sense…I’ve always believed this. Really good players are always in tune with their body. Nick is certainly that. He’s come back from ACLs before. It’s disappointing, because he came back in camp, and was all ready. And then when he tried to get out there on the field, it got stirred up a little. He got some tendinitis, that often happens in an ACL recovery. So that was unfortunate. He pulled back and got everything to where it was feeling better. And then Nick has gotten behind this plan of really building him up and putting him back on the field. Is it ideal? No. But I will tell you, so long as he responds well, he’s been tracking very well. Now, always ramping it up to actual football is a difference. So that’s the next step, and we’re very hopeful.” Lynch made it sound like the 49ers are being overly cautious with their star player in hopes of avoiding any kind of setback ahead of Week 1. Bosa won’t be in the kind of football shape he wants to be by the time the regular season gets underway, but the trade-off was not dealing with any tendinitis. George Kittle begins his ramp-up Lynch said George Kittle returning is “a combination of a lot of things” when asked if he could play in Week 1: “He’s done a ton of volume to the side, and he’s looked incredible doing it. Yesterday was the first time that he got involved in team reps. We plan to continue that moving forward, continue to see how he responds. George is pushing. He’s got tremendous energy each and every day. I think that helps coming back from something like this. The way he’s approached this rehab has been tremendous. We’ll see where it goes, but it certainly has us encouraged.” Kittle working in team drills is a good sign. Now the 49ers will see how his body responds, and how much he can handle over the next couple of days. In George’s mind, it’ll be all systems go. Mike Evans remains sidelined with an adductor injury Lynch spoke about Evans’ fit in the offense, and how the 49ers have “never had a guy that tall, that big, who can run the route tree.” Evans continues to work on the side as he recovers from an adductor injury. Lynch said the hope is for Evans to return to practice early next week, “and if all goes well, he’ll be suiting up and making plays for us.”

title: Did the 49ers sign their Skyy Moore of 2026 on the practice squad?
summary: The most recent practice squad update for the San Francisco 49ers might end up being their most valuable. The team added Brandon Codrington, who spent the previous two seasons with the Buffalo Bills. On the surface, Codrington has modest defensive numbers, but was an all-rookie returner. Then you connect the dots after reading that Jacob […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NY - SEPTEMBER 18: Brandon Codrington #29 of the Buffalo Bills looks on from the field during an NFL football game against the Miami Dolphins at Highmark Stadium on September 18, 2025 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The most recent practice squad update for the San Francisco 49ers might end up being their most valuable. The team added Brandon Codrington, who spent the previous two seasons with the Buffalo Bills. On the surface, Codrington has modest defensive numbers, but was an all-rookie returner. Then you connect the dots after reading that Jacob Cowing — the 49ers returner — was working on the side of practice on Monday as he recovers from a groin injury, and it makes sense why the 49ers would want to invest in Codrington. This job belonged to Skyy Moore a year ago. Kyle Shanahan seemed enamored with Moore’s ability to, for lack of a better word, hit the hole recklessly. If Cowing isn’t ready for Week 1, that leaves Deebo Samuel and Jordan Watkins as the returners. Deebo has proven to be a fantastic option, but he also may be involved in the offense more than anticipated after all of the injuries suffered at the position over the past month. It would be special teams coordinator Brant Boyer’s call. He’s seen Watkins and Codrington return. Boyer witnessed Codrington have an explosive return during his tenure with the Jets. That year, Codrington had multiple returns that led him to being in the top 5 in both punt and kickoff return average: Codrington finished top 5 in the league in punt and kickoff return average in '24. He had 2 kickoff returns of 50+ yards and 4 punt returns of 20+ yards in the last 2 seasons. 1 of those came against Brant Boyer's Jets. If Jacob Cowing isn't ready, this could be the returner. https://t.co/DzxyehCUK2 pic.twitter.com/Qkf8zDVN9H — Kyle Posey (@KP_Show) September 1, 2026 That looks different than what we’ve seen, albeit in a smaller sample size, when Watkins has the ball in his hands as a returner. The team could elevate Codrington from the practice squad up to three times. If he’s impressed enough by then, the Niners would be forced to sign Codrington to the active roster. If not, ideally, Cowing is healthy, and you have your original returner back. You’re always evaluating and trying to improve your team. That’s what this move would be for the 49ers if they feel like Codrington offers more as a returner than Watkins — or Cowing, for that matter. The team bought low on Moore last year, and it paid off. A few years ago, they did the same with Tashaun Gipson, and that ended up being one of the most important moves of the year. They’re hoping for similar results this time around with Codrington.

title: Kyle Shanahan says plan for newly acquired OL is ‘to get him in the group right away’
summary: The San Francisco 49ers had a busy weekend as they cut down to 53 players on a day that always has a degree of roster politics around. While a majority of the team’s moves were expected, there was one surprise: the release of veteran guard Robert Jones, who signed a one-year deal in the offseason. […]
full_text: Sep 29, 2024; Houston, Texas, USA; Houston Texans center Jarrett Patterson (54) during the game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at NRG Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con The San Francisco 49ers had a busy weekend as they cut down to 53 players on a day that always has a degree of roster politics around. While a majority of the team’s moves were expected, there was one surprise: the release of veteran guard Robert Jones, who signed a one-year deal in the offseason. Jones had been a part of the competition at left guard, but that had been shifting towards rookie Carver Willis as training camp continued. Still, he could’ve been a depth piece for the 49ers after spending the whole offseason with the team. Well, questions were quickly answered as the 49ers traded for Houston Texans offensive lineman Jarrett Patterson, who was a sixth-round pick in 2023. Patterson, 27, has played in 39 games for the Texans, starting 21, with time at both center and guard. He played in all 17 games in 2025, starting five. San Francisco still hasn’t decided on a Week 1 starter at guard, but could also use some center depth with Willis now clearly being in the guard mix this season. What’s the plan for Patterson as he arrives in San Francisco, with Week 1 just over a week away? “To get him in the group right away,” head coach Kyle Shanahan said on Tuesday. “We love that he has some flex at center and guard. It’s still fluid in all our positions in there, so I want to see where he fits in the group in these three days. “That is the hard thing with not just going to Australia, but just not opening on a Sunday. The time that we’re usually used to making some of these decisions have all been sped up. So, I want to get him in the group, see where he fits, just see him in person, see how he can help us at guard, how he can help us at center, and how he stacks up to the other guys.” So, it seems the plan is to test Patterson out at both guard and center, although there isn’t much time to figure that out ahead of Week 1. Shanahan did add that he ‘does not know yet’ who the 49ers Week 1 starter at left guard is, pointing out that it’s fluid following the addition of Patterson. “Nope, [I don’t know the starter at left guard],” Shanahan said. “It’s the truth. Usually, we get all three of these practices, and then by that Monday is like when we come in and usually do leadership council, captains and, ‘all right, this is who we’re rolling with.’ But we haven’t had those three practices yet, and we just added a new guy to the group too. So, it’s truly fluid.”

title: Did the Titans get better by replacing Austin Deculus with James Hudson?
summary: After initially making four roster moves on Monday, one obvious to-do item remained for the Tennessee Titans. They claimed Owen Pappoe (LB), Melvin Smith (CB), and Nazir Stackhouse (DT) off waivers, and signed veteran safety Terrell Burgess. To make room, they waived Mo Diabate (LB), Erick Hallett II (CB), Jerrick Reed II (SS), and Xavier […]
full_text: Aug 22, 2021; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Cleveland Browns offensive tackle James Hudson (66) blocks against the New York Giants during the second quarter at FirstEnergy Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Scott Galvin-USA TODAY Sports After initially making four roster moves on Monday, one obvious to-do item remained for the Tennessee Titans . They claimed Owen Pappoe (LB), Melvin Smith (CB), and Nazir Stackhouse (DT) off waivers, and signed veteran safety Terrell Burgess. To make room, they waived Mo Diabate (LB), Erick Hallett II (CB), Jerrick Reed II (SS), and Xavier Restrepo (WR). Fans quickly noted the lack of a swing tackle, which everyone believed would be Mike Borgonzi’s biggest priority. The other shoe eventually dropped. Making a fifth move, the Titans signed offensive tackle James Hudson and waived Austin Deculus. Deculus struggled mightily throughout the preseason, allowing three sacks to backups. He was passed over on the depth chart by sophomore UDFA Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson. Now, Deculus is off the roster altogether, making room for Hudson. Hudson previously played for Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll with the New York Giants . His position coach was Titans OL coach Carmen Bricillo. He was even teammates with new starting center Austin Schlottmann. At least Hudson will be familiar with the scheme. Hudson played just 85 offensive snaps last season. He last played meaningful snaps in 2024, earning 207 reps at left tackle. Hudson wasn’t credited with allowing any sacks, but he did give up 15 pressures while earning a pass-blocking grade of 40.2 (PFF). The sample size was significantly larger in 2023, earning 493 snaps at right tackle. The former fourth-round selection out of Cincinnati forfeited five sacks and 36 pressures en route to a pass-blocking score of 48.4. He’s known as a powerful run blocker, but his pass-blocking grades have been better than Deculus’ (33.1 in 2025). Hudson represents an upgrade from Deculus, but the Titans’ offense could still be troublesome if he had to play meaningful snaps. At least Hudson has played both tackle positions, and knows Daboll/Bricillo from his past. The Titans still have a long-term problem, but at least he’s better than Deculus.

Hats, merch, from the line that set the standard for the offensive line and brought home three Super Bowls. https://t.co/3HZHO7HM22 — Joe Jacoby (@JoeJacoby66HOG) September 1, 2026 Articles Too Deep Zone Aaron Donald: Good. Commanders: Bad. Ravens … Confusing. (Mailbag Pt. 1) Commanders Questions It feels like Washington may be a sneaky contender for “worst team in the league” this year. We all know the Browns and Dolphins stink; why will Washington be worse? – Kevin Langstaff Reader Brutus Rugburn chimed in: Kevin, I agree completely. Looking at their schedule, 3 wins should be the over/under mark. The miracle of 2024 completely screwed up any reasonable, orderly rebuild. Mike, to add to Kevin’s query, how, if at all, could Washington have responded differently to their winning 2024 season with the clearly deficient roster they had? The Commanders are projected to win 7.7 games by DVOA. I think they have had a miserable offseason, despite adding Stefon Diggs. The cavalcade of 32-year old acquisitions I have been dunking on all summer leaves me with little faith about the quality of the front office and the lower tiers of the roster. Dire tales from joint practices make me wonder about the reconfigured coaching staff. So I think the Commanders could be the worst team in the NFL. It’s hard to project them with the worst record, because the Browns quarterback situation is so dire that the team could surrender at the trade deadline, while the Cardinals schedule is so brutal. Relitigating what the Commanders did after reaching the NFC Championship Game in 2024 is tricky. It’s easy to condemn the Laremy Tunsil and Deebo Samuel trades, but those moves made sense at the time. The Commanders got so little besides Jayden Daniels from the 2024 draft that the seeds of decline may have already been sewn. The Commanders needed to do a better job self-scouting the bottom half of their roster and creating competition among younger players in 2025 and this offseason. They should have stockpiled late-round picks and UDFAs and given the ones they did have better opportunities to win roster spots and roles. One or two come-from-nowhere contributors would make their roster look a lot less like the result of an end-of-free-agency shopping spree. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE ESPN 2026 NFL bold predictions: Potential surprises for 32 teams Washington Commanders Don’t be surprised if … quarterback Jayden Daniels struggles to regain his brilliant rookie-year form. What I’m hearing: This isn’t about Daniels himself. He’s an absolutely awesome player, and assuming he can get through the season healthy, I expect him to perform at a high level. It’s what’s around him that has me concerned. He has a thin and aging group of wide receivers. He has question marks at running back. And the offensive line issues, especially with left tackle Laremy Tunsil going down with a training camp injury , are too significant to overlook. Earlier in the offseason, I was high on the Commanders’ chances to rebound and contend in the NFC East. But the concerns that arose during camp are giving me pause. The fact that they have a young, first-time offensive coordinator in David Blough adds to the mystery (as, to be fair, it does with the first-time OC in Philadelphia and the first-time defensive coordinator in Dallas). There could be significant growing pains early in the season, if not longer. And even if things work out better than they look right now, Daniels’ 2024 rookie season was one of the best we’ve ever seen. Washington could be pretty good and still not bounce back to that level. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE The Athletic (paywall) NFL execs rank NFC teams: Rams, Seahawks clear favorites 13. Washington Commanders Votes: 13-12-13-14-9-13 | Avg: 12.3 | Median: 13 | Vegas wins: 7.5 (T-11th-NFC) Tier votes: Division contender: 1 | Sub-.500: 4 | Top-10 pick: 1 The voter highest on Washington thought Jayden Daniels’ return to health was enough to lift a Commanders team that has question marks entering coach Dan Quinn’s third season, including first-time coordinators on offense (David Blough) and defense (Daronte Jones). “They get Jayden back, and Terry McLaurin will be healthy,” this exec said. “They’ve added some really good parts defensively in free agency. They have to get the offensive line solidified.” Left tackle Laremy Tunsil’s season-ending injury will not help. “I think they are going to be bad,” another exec said. “The quarterback is talented, but his style of play, unless he changes it, is a concern. The weapons around him are OK, but I don’t think it’s a dynamic team offensively. Defensively, they plateaued.” To read more of this article, CLICK HERE The Athletic (paywall) Jayden Daniels is ready for a new offense. His first task: Learn how to huddle Last season the median NFL offense huddled about 82 percent of the time. When Daniels was on the field, the Commanders huddled about 32 percent of the time. If you remove the first play of the drive (when almost every team huddles), that number plummets to 20 percent. Taking away huddles after timeouts or penalties would drop it even more. For all intents and purposes, Daniels has never huddled play-to-play in his pro career. Kliff Kingsbury’s offense the last two seasons didn’t require it, but Daniels also didn’t do it in college. Without a huddle, there is less information a quarterback can communicate to the other 10 players. That lends itself to a less complex offense, one that’s easier for defenses to decipher. Tempo typically offsets some of that. Even if you have a simpler offense, going quickly can create an edge. Instead, the Commanders self-neutralized their inherent advantage. Last year, on average, there were 9.6 seconds remaining on the playclock when the Commanders snapped the ball, eighth-highest in the NFL and much closer to the league average (9 seconds) than the Dallas Cowboys’ league-leading 12 seconds. Commanders coaches know Daniels is going to run — they just don’t have to call it. Quinn estimates Daniels will have four or five rushing attempts off scrambles alone each game. Adding designed runs to that “is how you end up with 10,” Quinn says. The league’s average quarterback scramble rate the past two seasons is 5.5 percent. Daniels sits atop the NFL at 13.8 percent, multiple percentage points ahead of runners-up like Justin Fields, Tyler Huntley and Drake Maye. So Washington has to set up some guardrails. And this is the biggest reason why Daniels will be under center more often this year. Getting under center should, in theory, make defenses respect the play-action game more than shotgun, where sometimes defenders can see the entire exchange (or lack thereof). That will help Daniels as a passer, as defenses have to play the run more honestly, and help the run game be more explosive. Just like the huddle, no team the last two seasons has been under center less often than the Commanders. Last year Washington was under center just 13.1 percent of the time, and that dropped to 5.8 percent when Daniels was on the field. The Cincinnati Bengals had the second-lowest percentage of plays under center (18.4). With one training camp and three preseason snaps in the books, Daniels hasn’t decided on whether to stand up, hunch over or take a knee [in the huddle]. “It might depend,” Daniels tells…

title: What Commanders OL Nick Allegretti said about rehab, return to lineup
summary: Nick Allegretti has been the subject of more Commanders conversation than offensive linemen typically generate. A nagging calf strain that stole most of his training camp, a vital period for the presumptive starting center after playing guard most of his NFL career.   Washington’s backup plans proved faulty, with Julian Good-Jones struggling to provide stability […]
full_text: Nick Allegretti has been the subject of more Commanders conversation than offensive linemen typically generate. A nagging calf strain that stole most of his training camp, a vital period for the presumptive starting center after playing guard most of his NFL career. Washington’s backup plans proved faulty, with Julian Good-Jones struggling to provide stability and sixth-round rookie Matt Gulbin needing expected time to develop. That left the fan base up in arms, especially following Tyler Biadsaz’s unexpected release early in the offseason, as Allgretti’s absence kept getting extended. The Commanders didn’t go out and sign an experienced backup after final cuts, nor did they trade for an interior lineman beforehand. All those actions showed extreme faith in Allegretti, which general manager Adam Peters backed up with words after final cuts. “Not having Nick for most of camp was something we had to work through, but we have a ton of confidence in him,” Peters said in a Monday press conference . “He has played 3,000-some odd snaps in this league, and he has played good football for us before. He went through the whole offseason, so we’re really confident.” Allegretti worked through his rehab process, which allowed him to return to practice on Monday and again on Tuesday. “I felt good the last two days,” Allegretti told on-site reporters, via 7NewsDC’s Scott Abraham . “I felt good the four or five days prior to getting out to practice, so just continuing to stack good days in front of each other. We’ve got one more big one tomorrow before taking a couple days off. I’m looking forward to that.” Commanders starting center Nick Allegretti was the center of attention after today's practice. Here's what he had to say in the locker room ⬇️⬇️⬇️⬇️ pic.twitter.com/7F35tbL1WQ — Scott Abraham (@Scott7news) September 1, 2026 The veteran interior offensive lineman said that time away was difficult, especially with the conservative approach taken with the rehab, but he had to trust the process. “Missing time is not something I’m used to,” Allegretti said, via video from NOTUS reporter Martenzie Johnson . “Being cautious with it was something that I had to respect … It was frustrating at times. I think I missed more practice in this training camp than I have in my entire career combined. Trusting that process, that we need to be right for September, not August. I don’t ever plan on missing games. That obviously happens from time to time, but it would’ve been a faster timeline had it not happened in August.” Commanders center Nick Allegretti on finally returning to practice: "Missing time is hard for me." pic.twitter.com/cvADuESYdt — Martenzie Johnson (@10zJohnson) September 1, 2026 Allegretti also expressed trust in Gulbin, who remains the primary backup center and took significant reps with quarterback Jayden Daniels over the past few weeks. Washington might never have to enact a backup plan for Allegretti. Should he stay healthy, he’ll take every offensive snap of the regular season. Washington is all-in on him as a center at this point. All eyes are on him and expectations are high for a player with a demanding role in David Blough’s new offensive system. “I understand that’s part of the deal,” Allegretti said, via video from Abraham. “When you moved on from Tyler (Biadsaz), that’s something the media was going to grab onto. I appreciate the staff giving me and Matt the trust at that position. Matt has been doing an incredible job. “It’s a really good opportunity for him to be thrust in there, getting a ton of reps with Jayden (Daniels) at a young age. He’s doing one hell of a job. I’m just trying to help him, which also helps myself in turn. When I’m getting mental reps and then working back in and getting the physical reps – I know that center’s probably talked about a lot. I’m just trying to take care of myself, take care of Matt and everything else will take care of itself.”

full_text: The Washington Commanders are back at practice this week, and they’ve moved into regular season mode. Assistant general manager Lance Newmark spoke to reporters before Tuesday’s practice, and was asked about the two tight ends that were added to the practice squad. Fellow tight end Ben Sinnott has been dealing with an oblique injury, but was back at practice yesterday doing limited work. Newmark said signing them wasn’t about the four tight ends on the roster. Injuries have been a big storyline during this training camp, with several players like Laremy Tunsil (triceps) and Jer’Zhan Newton (pectoral) expected to miss most, or all of the season. Other players, like running back Bill Croskey-Merritt (groin) have been dealing with soft-tissue injuries, returned to practice today. Starting center Nick Allegretti has missed most of training camp due to a calf strain, but he was back on the practice field the last two days. He’s wearing sleeves over the injured leg, but has been snapping the ball with Jayden Daniels and Marcus Mariota. Two big names on the injured list are edge rushers Odafe Oweh (calf) and K’Lavon Chaisson (knee), who are still working to the side, and their Week 1 availability could be in question. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles The Athletic (paywall) Adam Peters and Dan Quinn are confident in the Commanders. Now, they have to be right This is Peters’ team. It is Quinn’s to coach. This is not a year to build. It is not a bridge to something in the future. It’s a year to produce. Harris has to be watching — and closely, right? The iffy vibes from the past couple of weeks stem from Tunsil’s injury, flat performances against Detroit and Baltimore, a largely shaky joint practice against the Ravens and the inability of center Nick Allegretti to practice because of a calf problem — which exposed a tissue-thin interior of the offensive line. Throw in another injury to cornerback Trey Amos, who will open the season on injured reserve, and it can be hard to find hope before a season that begins with an eight-game stretch that’s borderline cruel — the above-mentioned first three games followed by an anything-can-happen trip to London to face the Colts, a flight back home to play the Giants, a Monday night trip to San Francisco and out-of-the-bye dates against the Eagles and Rams. Yikes. This is not to say the season is over before it starts. Far from it. The Commanders still have Daniels, and a healthy Daniels lifts the floor of the entire operation. In Terry McLaurin, Stefon Diggs and tight end Chig Okonkwo, Daniels might have his most dangerous group of pass catchers in his three seasons as a pro. Plus, for those in freak-out mode about the state of the offensive line, there’s still time before the opener to make a move or two. The message Monday: deep breaths. September is just starting. This isn’t the time to panic. It is, however, time to take ownership. Adam Peters, Dan Quinn, the team you’re confident in is all yours. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE ESPN 2026 NFL Rank: Predicting top 100 players for this season 61. Jayden Daniels QB | Commanders Age: 25 2025 rank: 24 Daniels has posted arguably his best training camp, coming off an injury-filled season . He has been relaxed and appears comfortable in the offense, and offensive coordinator David Blough said the QB is “as accurate as he’s ever been.” It helps that he has a healthy WR Terry McLaurin and that the team signed Stefon Diggs. The big question for Daniels will be how his line protects him, especially with left tackle Laremy Tunsil sidelined after triceps surgery. — John Keim Signature stat: Last season, Daniels became the first player in NFL history to record 4,000 passing yards and 1,000 rushing yards in his first 20 career games. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Sports Illustrated Adam Peters Doubles Down on Washington’s Plan at Center After Roster Cuts While Washington’s confidence in Allegretti hasn’t changed , his lack of training camp work still leaves a legitimate question about how quickly the group can come together. Quinn also chimed in, saying Washington is still working through the center position while welcoming Allegretti back to practice. Peters added that Allegretti doesn’t need a large volume of reps from a mental standpoint. He also praised Gulbin’s development, while Quinn specifically praised the rookie’s strength, football intelligence, and ability to avoid repeating mistakes. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Heavy.com Stefon Diggs Might Return to His Old Form Before ACL Injury [London] Fletcher…noted that Diggs is about to be two full years removed from the torn ACL he suffered in October 2024 while with the Houston Texans. As a result, the former linebacker notes that the veteran has the same pep in his runs he had before the injury. “I went and looked back at his film at 24 before he got injured. He had some juice for the Houston Texans. He was making a lot of plays for them. And then when I saw him, I wanted to see which guy we were going to get when we signed him. I saw him in practice once he signed and he has his burst back. [Diggs] has his wheels; he’s running faster than he was in ’25. So he’s going to be able to do even more things. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Podcasts & videos Chiefs Got Their Answer on Esa Pole – Film Breakdown vs Texans Pole is reported to have agreed to be on the Commanders practice squad; his signing has not yet been announced by the team and he doesn’t yet appear on the team’s official roster page Commanders Preseason Recap | Booth Review Podcast | Washington Commanders | NFL NFC East links GQ Sports Can Anyone Decode Jalen Hurts, the NFL’s Most Cryptic Quarterback? Hurts is the rare athlete of his caliber and stature who doesn’t come with an easy-to-digest narrative: He wasn’t a first-round pick, but he wasn’t a fifth-round pick either; he has won more than quarterbacks who are generally considered “better,” and yet much of the discussion about him is about his limitations, real or perceived. If Hurts has feelings about any of this, he doesn’t share them. Hurts says he used to live by a typically Hurts-like mantra, which was: It’s not about proving anybody wrong, it’s about proving myself right. He says he’s updated that a bit to take all the proving out of it. Rightly or wrongly, the only response he knows to anything is to keep working. “It’s really about just continuing the mission. Continue the mission. Work, and continue the mission,” he says. A couple years ago, in 2024, Hurts gave a quote that has haunted him a bit since, and which has since been cited as a skeleton key, a rare moment of truth, from an athlete who doesn’t often reveal his own internal monologue. Asked about the sluggish offense then, he said: “It’s going to look how Jalen Hurts wants it to look.” Since then, this quote has been cited in arguments city-wide about Hurts, sometimes as proof that he is somehow uncoachable or at minimum very stubborn. I wondered if, given another chance, he might have wanted to say it differently, or not at all. title: 2026 NFL bold predictions: Potential surprises for 32 teams
summary: Jameson Williams leading the Lions' receivers? Xavier Worthy breaking out? Travis Hunter almost entirely at CB? We have 32 outside-the-box things to watch.
full_text:
I love surprises. They're my favorite part of sports. People sometimes ask if I'm upset that I got a prediction wrong, and I tend to answer no. If I knew what was going to happen ahead of time, I don't think I'd enjoy watching the games. I watch them because I know they can surprise me. I strongly believe that surprises are the main reason watching sports is fun.

 However, I recognize that not everyone feels this way. Many of you like to have some ability to predict what's going to happen for, let's say, profit-related reasons? Hey, I get it. I play a ton of fantasy football, and surprises can mess with that. I understand the appeal of any information that can help put me in the best possible position to at least anticipate what's likely to happen, if not get all the way to certainty.

 So every year, right before the start of the NFL season, we do this all-32 list in which I go through every team and pick out one potential surprise. This is based on the reporting I've done throughout training camp, talking to people with and around these teams and trying to figure out what the plan is for each franchise. They aren't predictions in the strictest sense. They're more tidbits that I think could signal things you might not be expecting. (They're also generally more informative for people who aren't fans of the specific team to whom they apply. I get that some people follow these teams far more closely than others, and that what might be a surprise to someone on the outside might not be to those who've been gobbling up every training camp play-by-play and news conference sound bite.)

 Anyway, that's enough with the disclaimers. Enjoy these. Come back in a few months and tell me where I was right and where I was wrong. I promise I won't mind even if it's the latter. That's the fun part of the NFL season , after all.

 
 Jump to a team: 
 ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN 
 CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND 
 JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN 
 NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SF 
 SEA | TB | TEN | WSH 

 
 

 

 NFC EAST 
 

 Dallas Cowboys 
 Don't be surprised if ... rookie safety Caleb Downs never leaves the field. 

 What I'm hearing:  OK, maybe that's a slight exaggeration, but the Cowboys believe they can use Downs in a ton of different ways. In their ideal world, he and veteran safety Jalen Thompson are interchangeable in the safety and nickel roles. Downs got a lot of work at nickel during camp, and Dallas has faith in his ability to play deep safety. The Cowboys believe in his ability to cover top receivers if that's what they need from him, and they think he will be instantly capable of communicating at a high level and helping keep things organized on the defense.

 The Cowboys drafted Downs hoping they could plug and play him on defense in Year 1, and to their absolute delight, he has shown himself to be just that in every situation they've thrown at him so far. They're counting on him to handle a key role in the revitalization of their defense under new coordinator Christian Parker, and I expect him to play a ton.

 

 
 

 

 New York Giants 
 Don't be surprised if ... tight end Isaiah Likely is a breakout star in New York. 

 What I'm hearing:  Giants coaches light up when talking about Likely, the free agent signee who came over from Baltimore with coach John Harbaugh. They believe he'll be a real asset for Jaxson Dart as a receiver and think he can win in both man and zone coverage. And they love the way he has embraced and evolved his relationship with Dart since he has been in New York. Likely is a regular visitor to the quarterback room, and the connection he has formed with Dart on and off the field could pay major dividends. Likely is a strong candidate to be the team's second-leading receiver this season and could be even more than that if top wideout Malik Nabers needs time to get up to speed coming off his injury .

 

 
 

 Philadelphia Eagles 
 Don't be surprised if ... they have the best defense in the NFL this season. 

 What I'm hearing:  The questions on offense in Philadelphia are myriad and totally legitimate. The new coordinator, Sean Mannion, is a first-time playcaller and in just his third year as a coach at any level. Longtime offensive line coach Jeff Stoutland's departure leaves a void, too. The Eagles also traded their best receiver to the Patriots in  A.J. Brown . And on and on. Regardless, the Vic Fangio defense should be an absolute monster.

 Sure, the Jonathan Greenard   pec strain  is a blow to the pass rush, but he shouldn't be out too long, and the Eagles expect guys such as  Moro Ojomo to contribute there in the meantime.  Jihaad Campbell should make an impact in his second season at linebacker, too. The secondary, fortified by the free agent addition of Riq Woolen , is ascending and already Super Bowl-tested. The interior defensive line duo of Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis is a strength. And the continuity under Fangio is a big reason to believe this unit will only be better. The Eagles look like the kind of defense that can carry a transitioning offense through early-season growing pains.

 

 
 

 Washington Commanders 
 Don't be surprised if ... quarterback Jayden Daniels struggles to regain his brilliant rookie-year form. 

 What I'm hearing: This isn't about Daniels himself. He's an absolutely awesome player, and assuming he can get through the season healthy, I expect him to perform at a high level. It's what's around him that has me concerned. He has a thin and aging group of wide receivers. He has question marks at running back. And the offensive line issues, especially with left tackle  Laremy Tunsil  going down with a training camp injury , are too significant to overlook.

 Earlier in the offseason, I was high on the Commanders' chances to rebound and contend in the NFC East. But the concerns that arose during camp are giving me pause. The fact that they have a young, first-time offensive coordinator in David Blough adds to the mystery (as, to be fair, it does with the first-time OC in Philadelphia and the first-time defensive coordinator in Dallas). There could be significant growing pains early in the season, if not longer. And even if things work out better than they look right now, Daniels' 2024 rookie season was one of the best we've ever seen. Washington could be pretty good and still not bounce back to that level.

 

 

 NFC NORTH 
 

 Chicago Bears 
 Don't be surprised if ... the Bears still trade for an edge rusher. 

 What I'm hearing:  Chicago is thin on defense, especially on the back end. But it's up front where the team is still looking for a strong edge presence opposite Montez Sweat . The Bears added veteran Marcus Davenport a couple of weeks ago, but that move doesn't appear to be working out; they let Davenport go in their initial cut down to 53 players over the weekend before bringing him back on the practice squad. Bears GM Ryan Poles has been an active and aggressive trader in his time with the team, and he'll turn over every rock he can looking for an impact player up front. The Bears' health issues on defense might be more concentrated on the back end, but improving the pass rush would help the secondary, too.

 

 
 

 Detroit Lions 
 Don't be surprised if ...  Jameson Williams is the team's leading receiver. 

 What I'm hearing:  No disrespect to Amon-Ra St. Brown , one of the most consistent pass catchers in the entire league. But I think this Lions offense is going to hum this season, and Williams is the player poised to take the biggest leap. For a few years now, the coaching staff has been pushing Williams to expand his route repertoire and contribute as more than just a deep threat. And in Drew Petzing's offense, Williams could be poised to do just that. The Lions' schedule of opposing defenses sets up well for Williams, and if he proves himself to be a trustworthy target for Jared Goff , he could be in for a career year.

title: 11 NFL players to watch next offseason -- if they don't sign extensions
summary: From C.J. Stroud to top cornerbacks, we go through players up for extensions who could also be on the move in 2027.
full_text:
Player contracts are accelerating at an Xavier Worthy -esque pace this offseason. The past six months have triggered an avalanche of market-topping deals, from a quarterback making $64 million per year ( Patrick Mahomes ) to an edge rusher earning an annual average of $50 million ( Will Anderson Jr. ).

 Five players have become positional cash kings this summer alone, with several more setting high marks back in the spring. Since June, five defensive tackles have earned deals worth at least $30 million per year.

 Some teams privately grumble over ballooning salaries and the inherent challenges of building a competitive team around star players who eat up much of their salary cap. But the soaring costs simply parallel a 44.7% increase in the NFL's cap over the past four years, from $208.2 million in 2022 to $301.2 million now.

 The previous four-year spike was 17.4%, from $177.2 million in 2018 to the 2022 number, and while the pandemic stalled progress, nothing is slowing down what's happening now. But many elite players still need new deals with Week 1 just days away. Some will get to the finish line before kickoff; some won't.

 ESPN made calls around the league to provide the latest information on many of the key contract extension candidates: Who gets paid and who will strategically wait things out until the offseason?

 
 Jump to a topic: 
 Lamar Jackson  | C.J. Stroud 
 Christian Gonzalez  | Joey Porter Jr. 
 DJ Turner  | Quenton Nelson 
 Tucker Kraft  | Detroit duo 

 
 

 

 

 Lamar Jackson , QB, Baltimore Ravens 
 Jackson, to his credit, is fiercely private about his negotiations. And as his own agent, he has proved to be a shrewd negotiator. Just look back at 2023, when Jackson remained patient, requested a trade after being franchise-tagged and finally landed a five-year, $260 million deal.

 It's no surprise this negotiation is void of many details. But the league sentiment is this: Jackson has massive leverage and appears ready to use it, which means the chances of him playing out 2026 without an extension could grow by the day.

 

 He is owed $52 million in cash in each of the next two seasons with an $84.3 million cap hit in 2027, which might as well be a poison pill. He has a no-franchise-tag provision and a no-trade clause. If he wants to entertain a new home outside of Baltimore in future years, he has full control of where it is -- especially if he has another banner season.

 Perhaps Baltimore gives Jackson an offer he can't refuse soon. But he can sit tight and let the market do the work for him next offseason, when several star quarterbacks from the 2024 draft class will be eligible for extensions.

 Perhaps then Jackson will become the NFL's first player to earn $70 million per year.

 

 

 

 C.J. Stroud , QB, Houston Texans 
 Several people with knowledge of the situation believe Stroud is prepared to play out this season without a new deal, despite Houston making what it considered a competitive offer.

 There's still time before kickoff to reach a deal -- and the Texans' front office is aggressive in re-signing core players -- but the current sentiment is Stroud will most likely not end up with a new deal.

 My understanding is Houston is prepared to put Stroud in what it feels is a strong place among the 12 quarterbacks in the $50 million club.

 But like Jackson, Stroud can let an exploding quarterback market do the work for him if he waits an additional six to eight months. By all accounts, Stroud had a strong training camp and believes he can rebound from last season's struggles. Houston is squarely in the Super Bowl discussion based on its talent level and elite defense. There's a lot for Stroud to gain -- and potentially lose -- by delaying a deal. He has had moments of brilliance since entering the league in 2023. Channeling that brilliance while properly managing the game will go a long way.

 On Tuesday, Texans general manager Nick Caserio set a Week 1 deadline for a deal with Stroud .

 

 "If we don't get it figured out before the season starts, then it'll be something we address in the offseason," Caserio said.

 

 

 Christian Gonzalez , CB, New England Patriots 
 On the surface, this deal feels like a no-brainer. Gonzalez was the No. 3 cornerback as ranked by executives, coaches and scouts , a true press-man coverage player who dominated late last season. He has an All-Pro and a Pro Bowl nod.  Seattle Seahawks corner Devon Witherspoon 's four-year, $132 million deal set the table.

 But this one is taking a while to reach a conclusion. Gonzalez did not appear thrilled when addressing local media members this summer. Perhaps that had something to do with team owner Robert Kraft floating publicly at the start of camp that New England offered to make Gonzalez the highest-paid cornerback in NFL history.

 My understanding of this situation is that if Gonzalez were to sign a market-setting deal -- and it will need to be just that -- then it has to be buttoned up. And the sides are not close on several elements of the deal.

 

 It's worth noting New England hasn't executed many recent top-line extensions from which to draw. Rob Gronkowski's six-year, $54 million extension in 2012 was the highest for a tight end at the time but was considered team friendly due to the number of years. Tom Brady was famously underpaid. New England has spent big on free agents but not necessarily on many market-resetting extensions. Gonzalez, who as of now does not plan to negotiate during the season, is testing that in a big way.

 

 

 Joey Porter Jr. , CB, Pittsburgh Steelers 
 This is probably the most complicated of them all. Momentum for a deal just hasn't been there. My sense is the player has been frustrated that, despite his status as a high-level man corner, he hasn't been made a priority. The 2023 draft picks getting paid by Pittsburgh -- linebacker  Nick Herbig and defensive tackle  Keeanu Benton , who received four-year extensions this summer -- play smaller roles.

 

 Sources say the Steelers' lack of a formal offer for weeks sent the clear message to Porter that they would like him to play out the final year of his rookie contract, which prompted him to consider the possibility of a trade or sitting out for an extended period. The 26-year-old stayed away from the practice field for weeks but returned Tuesday. Perhaps his participation ignites talks, but he's leaving that up to his agents .

 The semantics are this: The Steelers most likely would do a deal with Porter. But the mechanics of the cornerback market (as outlined above with Gonzalez) are hard to ignore. Five cornerbacks make $30 million or more per year. After that, there's a drop to $25 million (the  Carolina Panthers '  Jaycee Horn ). Porter essentially has to pick which group he thinks he belongs in, and all indications are it's not the latter. And the Steelers might not want him in the former on their dime.

 

 The Steelers don't negotiate during the season, which fuels the urgency over the coming week.

 I'm told the new coaching staff is not a deterrent here. They are all-in on his ability as a high-level cover man.

 Another hurdle: The 2027 franchise tag at cornerback is a below-market $23 million.

 

 

 DJ Turner , CB, Cincinnati Bengals 
 Like Porter, Turner is an underrated cover man out of the AFC North. But this deal has virtually no chance to get done before Week 1, barring a massive and unexpected uptick. It isn't close, and Turner is poised to play out his rookie deal.

 If Cincinnati follows its own blueprint, it will franchise-tag Turner as it did with another star defensive back, Jessie Bates III , in 2022. Bates had to play on the tag, before reaching a four-year deal with the  Atlanta Falcons  in free agency.

 

 Turner will be in line for a large payday in free agency, if he reaches it. But the franchise tag is a real possibility here.

 

 

 Quenton Nelson , G, Indianapolis Colts

title: 2026 NFL Rank: Predicting top 100 players for this season
summary: We predicted the top 100 NFL players for 2026. Which defender came in at No. 1? How many QBs made the list? Which team had the most players included?
full_text:
As we approach the start of the NFL season , it's time for our annual ranking of the league's top 100 players. Which players do we project to be the best in 2026?

 To create our list, we asked 12 NFL analysts and reporters -- Aaron Schatz, Ben Solak, Dan Graziano, Eric Moody, Field Yates, Jeff Legwold, Liz Loza, Matt Bowen, Mina Kimes, Mike Clay, Nick Wagoner and Seth Walder -- to rank players based on expected performance for the 2026 season. Their rankings are based on predicting potential greatness rather than past performance. We used those 12 sets of votes to come up with our consensus list.

 The Eagles lead the pack in players included (eight) for the second straight year , and the Lions and 49ers are next up with six players each. The Jets, meanwhile, are the only team without a single representative. By position, quarterbacks dominated the list with 16 mentions. Edge rushers followed with 13.

 Along with the top-100 ranking, our NFL Nation reporters weighed in on every player's outlook for the season, ESPN Research provided a stat to know and fantasy analyst Mike Clay projected 2026 stats. Here's our list, starting at No. 100 and working our way to No. 1.

 Note: Commanders offensive tackle Laremy Tunsil was not considered for this exercise due to his recent triceps injury ; again, this is predicting 2026 play. Rams defensive tackle  Aaron Donald , who came out of retirement Sunday, also was not considered. 

 

 Jump to: 
 100-76 | 75-51 | 50-26 | 25-1 

 More on NFL Rank: 
 Execs and scouts name snubs 

 

 

 100. Sam Darnold 
 QB | Seahawks 
Age: 29 
2025 rank: NR 

 No quarterback has more wins over the past two seasons than Darnold, who has 31 with the Vikings and Seahawks. He'd be higher on this list if not for his league-high 20 turnovers in 2025, though he went the final four games without one. One reason Darnold could be better in 2026: This is the first time since 2020 that he returns to the same team as its unquestioned starter. -- Brady Henderson 

 Signature stat: Last season, Darnold went 14-3 as a starter with the Seahawks after finishing the 2024 season with a 14-3 record for the Vikings. Darnold joined Tom Brady (2003-04) as the only QBs to record back-to-back 14-win seasons.

 99. Jessie Bates III 
 S | Falcons 
Age: 29 
2025 rank: 62 

 One of the premier ball hawks in the NFL, Bates has 27 interceptions and 11 forced fumbles (fifth most among defensive backs) since he entered the league in 2018.  Signature stat: Bates' 27 interceptions over the past eight seasons is the third most in the NFL behind Kevin Byard and Justin Simmons (both 28).

 98. Antoine Winfield Jr. 
 S | Buccaneers 
Age: 28 
2025 rank: 85 

 The Bucs were really intentional about bringing in some new players on defense who fit their type of attitude and instinct. Having linebacker Alex Anzalone -- one of the best cover inside linebackers in the league -- patrolling the middle of the field will be a huge assist to Winfield. So will another year of experience for Winfield's fellow safety Tykee Smith , as well as a revamped pass rush with rookie Rueben Bain Jr.   -- Jenna Laine 

 Signature stat: Winfield leads all safeties in forced fumbles (12) and fumble recoveries (10) since entering the league in 2020.

 2026 projections :  95 tackles, 8 PDs, 2 sacks, 2 INTs, 1 FF

 
 

 97. Jalen Hurts 
 QB | Eagles 
Age: 28 
2025 rank: 38 

 Hurts is coming off an up-and-down year and is now at the controls of a brand-new scheme designed by offensive coordinator Sean Mannion. Hurts has found ways to maneuver around obstacles in the past, though. He has a 57-25 record as a starting QB and ranks second to only Josh Allen in total touchdowns (138) since 2022. -- Tim McManus 

 Signature stat: Hurts recorded his fourth straight season with 30-plus combined passing and rushing touchdowns, the fourth-longest active streak behind Allen (six). That included his fewest rushing TDs (eight) since becoming the full-time starter in 2021.

 2026 projections :  3,779 passing yards, 24 TDs, 12 INTs; 106 carries, 438 rushing yards, 9 TDs

 
 

 96. Trevor Lawrence 
 QB | Jaguars 
Age: 26 
2025 rank: NR 

 It can't be coincidence that Liam Coen coached quarterback  Baker Mayfield and Lawrence to their best seasons in back-to-back years. Unlike 2025, Lawrence isn't learning a new offense or changing his footwork. So, it shouldn't take half of the season for him to get rolling the way he did over the final eight games of 2025 (19 TD passes and five rushing TDs). -- Michael DiRocco

 2026 projections :  3,932 passing yards, 25 TDs, 13 INTs; 73 carries, 335 rushing yards, 5 TDs

 Slater missed all of last season with a ruptured patellar tendon in his left knee. Slater has already missed practice time this offseason due to a flare-up, so it will be something to watch as he tries to reestablish himself as one of the best players at his position. -- Kris Rhim

 Horn will be more fluid in the defensive backfield in 2026. This summer, he has been used in the slot, which should take advantage of his blitzing ability. Over the offseason, Campbell inked a four-year, $81 million extension . Defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard is now giving him more leeway to run the defense in Year 4. "You've got to earn it every year," Campbell told ESPN. "No matter what, it's just my mindset to try to get a little better every single year." -- Eric Woodyard

Age: 23

title: Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett learning quickly under Mike LaFleur
summary: After an extended holdout/hold-in, Brissett is learning a new system and picking it up quickly.
full_text:
TEMPE, Ariz. -- During the early days of  Jacoby Brissett 's return to the field on July 26 after a contract standoff, he was just trying to survive.

 When the  Arizona Cardinals  quarterback first took the field early in training camp and started running new coach Mike LaFleur's offense for the first time, Brissett would stand in the huddle and tell the offense which play they were going to run based on what he called last season.

 "This is what we did last [year]," Brissett would say, according to tight end Trey McBride . "This is what we called it last year."

 Weeks later, those days are gone.

 It's been more than five weeks since Brissett returned from a monthslong holdout and hold-in as he waited for a reworked contract, and every day since has been one step closer toward mastering the offense.

 With Week 1 against the Los Angeles Chargers on the horizon, Brissett's grasp of the offense has grown by the day. At one point during camp, the 33-year-old described his progress as "leaps and bounds" beyond what his understanding of the scheme was when he first returned from his holdout.

 "I feel like it's significantly better than when he first started," McBride said. "Obviously he's played a lot of football in his career and you can only make so many football plays up. We're running the same stuff. Maybe it's called a little bit different.

 "He's kind of getting into the new terminology, and he's a fast learner. He's a smart guy. He spends a lot of time learning the game. So, it's been no issue for him. And I feel like right now he's very comfortable. He knows exactly what to do. And we're running and operating as a very good offense."

 

 How Brissett learned the offense was an example of his maturity as NFL veteran heading into his 11th season.

 Quarterbacks coach Matt Schaub didn't start from scratch when Brissett was ready to take the field for the first time in training camp after watching from the sidelines for the first three days as the final details of his new contract were hammered out.

 "We really didn't hold back with slowing things down or trying to go back to the beginning of camp or even OTAs with everything," Schaub said. "It's just like, we're just going to keep going and he's done a great job of extra meetings, extra time in the room, talking through things, extra walk-throughs to be able to just catch up, if you will."

 To get himself caught up as fast as he could, Brissett employed a variety of techniques to learn all the verbiage and information the coaches have thrown at him. The specific plays weren't necessarily new to Brissett, as LaFleur had proclaimed time and time again throughout Brissett's holdout. Everything else was, though.

 Brissett would go through the playcalls in his head whenever LaFleur was presenting in front of the offense or the team during camp. Then there were all the opportunities to run through the plays physically through walk-throughs, pre-practice walk-throughs and then in practice.

 "As you say it more and more and more, you get more comfortable with it and you kind of beat him to the punch on some of the plays," Brissett said. "So, it's finding new ways to learn the same stuff."

 A lot of that falls on Schaub, the 45-year-old in his first year of coaching who played 16 seasons for the Falcons, Texans, Raiders and Ravens.

 Schaub's approach to Brissett is quite different than if he were preparing rookie quarterback Carson Beck . Since Brissett has spent a decade in the NFL, Schaub talks things through with him more than younger quarterbacks, whom he would typically give a framework to and tell them to work within that.

 

 With Brissett, Schaub would ask him: "Hey, what have you done? What are you comfortable with? How do you see this?" Their conversations are more discussions with a heavy dose of give-and-take, from footwork to concepts and beyond. With all their conversations, Schaub said, the end goal is to find "common ground in what we're actually trying to get done."

 When Brissett takes the field at SoFi Stadium on Sept. 13, his work still won't be done. That'll be largely due to his still budding relationship with LaFleur. That's a work in progress.

 The two have been working overtime to get to know each other since they didn't spend a second on the field together during OTAs or minicamp. Yet, from the moment that head coach-playcaller-quarterback relationship began in earnest on July 28, Brissett has been all in on building a rapport with LaFleur.

 But like Brissett is still learning the nuances of the offense, he is still learning LaFleur. Brissett has picked up the most about his coach in specific practice situations such as first down, second down, third down and red zone.

 Every day, Brissett said he learns something new about LaFleur.

 "We're still learning each other and what he likes to call, what do I like and stuff like that," Brissett said. "So, being able to be vulnerable enough to say like, 'Man, I don't like that.' And him say like, 'Oh, I messed up,' or, 'I like this right here because of this.' And that part of the learning part of the relationship I think is cool.

 "I wouldn't say we're best friends because that'll be a lie. But I do like where our relationship is and his willingness and my willingness to merge our relationship and what he's doing with all the players on the team. He's building his own relationship with guys and it's been a joy to work with him."

title: How to bet the 2026 NFL season: Three bets to make on each team
summary: Will your NFL team beat its projected win total? What props should you target? Tyler Fulghum offers his three favorite bets for each team.
full_text:
The NFL season offers an almost unlimited amount of betting opportunities, from seasonlong win totals to individual player props and everything in between. It can be daunting.

 Don't worry. I've got you covered.

 Here are three wagers for each of the 32 franchises. Some picks look at the big picture, such as Super Bowl futures or division odds. Others zoom in on specific players, highlighting yardage totals, touchdown props or award chances. And for those who like long shots, we have a few of those too.

 Whether you're a futures-focused bettor mapping out the entire season or someone who prefers to target specific markets, this guide gives you a broad menu of options for every team. Consider it your all-in-one starting point for betting the 2026 NFL season.

 Note: Odds by DraftKings   and subject to change .

 Jump to: ARI  | ATL  | BAL  | BUF  | CAR 
 CHI  | CIN  |  CLE  | DAL  | DEN  | DET  | GB 
 HOU | IND  |  JAX  | KC  | LAC  | LAR  | LV 
 MIA | MIN  |  NE  | NO  | NYG  | NYJ  | PHI 
 PIT | SEA  |  SF  | TB  | TEN  | WAS 

 

 

   Arizona Cardinals 
 •  UNDER 4.5 wins (-186)  
•  Trey McBride  receiving yards UNDER 999.5 (-110) 
•  Jeremiyah Love rushing TDs UNDER 5.5 (+100) 

 The Cardinals have the hardest schedule in the league this year, and I expect their record to reflect that. If Arizona struggles to stay competitive, McBride's receiving prop becomes difficult to clear because of statistical regression and a likely lack of consistent quarterback play. The under on Love adds another attractive fade of touchdown production. The rookie running back already suffered an ankle injury in training camp.

 

 
   Atlanta Falcons 

 • UNDER 6.5 wins (+130) 
• Fewest regular-season wins (15-1) 
• Bijan Robinson rushing TDs UNDER 8.5 (+100) 

 

 Atlanta could struggle to find consistency because of questions at quarterback and a suspect defense. Under 6.5 wins is the primary value play, while a bet on the fewest regular-season wins provides significant upside if the Falcons completely bottom out. The Robinson play complements the team unders by fading Atlanta's ability to consistently finish drives. Robinson can still post strong yardage numbers while falling short of this touchdown threshold.

 

 
   Baltimore Ravens 
 •  UNDER 11.5 wins (-140) 
•  Zay Flowers receiving TDs UNDER 5.5 (-120) 
•  Trey Hendrickson sacks UNDER 12.25 (-125) 

 The under on wins doesn't require a disastrous season, it simply requires the Ravens to fall short of an extremely high bar. Flowers' under on receiving touchdowns fits that thesis. He has been a productive receiver but has never scored more than five receiving TDs in a season, as his size limits his chances in the red zone. The Hendrickson under is another bet against elite individual production for a really good player. That's just a massive number to clear, even if he does stay healthy the entire season.

 

 
   Buffalo Bills 

 •  OVER 10.5 wins (-120) 
•  Win AFC East (-136) 
•  James Cook III rushing yards UNDER 1,224.5 (-110) 

 Buffalo is lined as the co-AFC favorite with Baltimore, and I agree that the team is going to be very good this season. I'm comfortable with the pricing on over 10.5 wins and an AFC East title. Those bets are closely correlated. If the Bills reach 11 or more victories, they're in excellent position to take back the division from the Patriots. The under on Cook's rushing yards is a bet against a massive number. Buffalo should have an elite rushing attack, but missing even one or two games makes this a difficult threshold to clear.

 

 
   Carolina Panthers 
 •  OVER 6.5 wins (-166) 
• OVER 2.5 division wins (-165) 
• Bryce Young passing TDs UNDER 20.5 (-110) 

 After last season's playoff appearance, Carolina feels poised to take a meaningful step forward. Over 6.5 wins is the anchor wager, while over 2.5 division wins suggests Carolina can capitalize on a mediocre NFC South and a solid home-field advantage. The under on Young's passing touchdowns can coexist with both bets if the Panthers lean on their running game and defense, which I fully expect Dave Canales to do, following the script from a season ago.

 

 
   Chicago Bears 

 • OVER 9.5 wins (+105) 
• Highest-scoring team in NFL (+900) 
•  Caleb Williams 30+ TD passes (+275) 

 Chicago's three bets are built around an offense that coach Ben Johnson has openly said he wants to break scoring records this year. The price betting the over on wins provides value on a team that could make a significant leap, while a bet on highest-scoring team in the NFL offers a much bigger payoff if Johnson's proclamations prove prophetic. Williams throwing 30-plus touchdown passes directly correlates with that outcome. If Williams takes a jump alongside Luther Burden III , Rome Odunze and Colston Loveland , watch out.

 

 
   Cincinnati Bengals 
 •  OVER 9.5 wins (-160) 
•  Win AFC North (+184) 
• Zac Taylor to win Coach of the Year (28-1) 

 

 Cincinnati feels like a sleeper team in the AFC. The bets on wins and the AFC North depend on the Bengals remaining healthy on offense, while Taylor winning Coach of the Year at these odds provides substantial upside if the revamped defense helps the Bengals become a more complete contender in the conference. The additions of DT Dexter Lawrence II , DT Jonathan Allen and DE Boye Mafe should pay immediate dividends on that side of the ball.

 

 
   Cleveland Browns 
 

 • UNDER 5.5 wins (+115) 
•  Fewest regular-season wins (+1050) 
•  Deshaun Watson passing yards UNDER 1,749.5 (-120) 

 Cleveland's portfolio of wagers is a straightforward assessment that this team is bad . The under bet on wins provides value if the Browns struggle to find stability, while a play on the fewest regular-season wins offers significant leverage on a true collapse. The under on Watson's passing yards prop fits particularly well because the number can be threatened simply by injury and/or ineffectiveness. Stocked up with bonus draft capital for 2027 and beyond, the Browns are actually incentivized to quietly tank this season.

 

 
   Dallas Cowboys 

 •  OVER 9.5 wins (+100) 
•  Division finishing position: 1 (+235) 
• Earn No. 1 seed in NFC (+1550) 

 On paper, Dallas looks like a legit contender entering this season. Bets on wins and winning the division are particularly attractive. We know the offense should be capable, but the upgraded personnel on the defensive side of the ball has me really intrigued with the ceiling of this team. title: How Ravens' Henry is driven to rank among NFL's best backs
summary: Henry has made it clear this summer that this season will not be his last. But this season will likely be a momentous one nonetheless.
full_text:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- In a sideline interview during the Baltimore Ravens ' preseason game at the  Minnesota Vikings , running back  Derrick Henry  was asked how his body feels going into his 11th NFL season. 
 
 "Let's do 11 more," Henry said with a chuckle. 
 
 Henry has made it clear this summer that this season will not be his last. But this season will likely be a momentous one nonetheless. 
 
 Henry, who ranks 10th on the NFL's all-time rushing list, is 994 yards away from leapfrogging his way to No. 6. He could surpass four Hall of Fame running backs -- Eric Dickerson, Jerome Bettis, LaDainian Tomlinson and Curtis Martin -- who combined for 11 first-team All-Pro selections and seven single-season rushing titles. 
 
 
 
 If Henry can rush for 1,811 yards this season, which he has surpassed twice in his career (most recently in his debut season with the Ravens in 2024), he would move past Adrian Peterson for No. 5 on the list. 
 
 Running back Justice Hill , who is Henry's primary backup, smiled when asked whether Henry knows how many yards he needs to climb the league's career rushing ranks. 
 
 "He's well aware of where he stands right now," Hill said. "And he's well aware of what he needs to get to get in the top five because we talk about it." 
 
 Hill added, "When you go into a season, you always talk about your goals and things you're trying to achieve. And even though he's not going to talk about it out here, it's definitely a striving factor for him." 
 
 Henry made a big jump last season, going from No. 19 on the all-time rushing list to No. 10. When Henry eclipsed Tony Dorsett to move into the top 10 in December, he said, "It's a surreal moment for me and something that I always cherish." 
 
 
 
 In Henry's two seasons in Baltimore, he has led the NFL in rushing yards (3,516) and carries (632). This season, Henry will be playing in a new offensive system, but that is nothing new for him. 
 
 Declan Doyle, who replaced Todd Monken as the playcaller in Baltimore, is Henry's eighth offensive coordinator of his 11-year career. Doyle wouldn't commit to Henry getting over 300 carries for a third straight year but indicated Henry will have "an immense role." 
 
 "He's going to have a pretty large workload," Doyle said. "I was telling the offensive staff how cool it is when you call a run play [as a] first-time playcaller and Derrick Henry is the running back, and you're like, 'The odds of this working are a lot higher.'" 
 
 Other attainable milestones for Henry include: 
 
 He needs two rushing touchdowns to surpass Marcus Allen (123) for third on the NFL's all-time list. 
 He can tie Tomlinson for the most consecutive seasons and most total seasons with at least 10 rushing touchdowns in NFL history (10). 
 He can surpass Barry Sanders (five) for the most seasons with at least 1,500 rushing yards in league history. 
 
 
 
 
 Henry's teammates believe his work ethic is even more impressive than his numbers. 
 
 "What this guy has been able to do, we all know -- first-ballot [Hall of Famer]. Who he is as a person -- I've never seen the guy complain," linebacker Roquan Smith said. "[He] comes in day in, day out, grinds, never takes the easy route. I am just truly happy to have him on my team now and not have to worry about going against him." 
 
 When Smith previously had to go head-to-head with Henry, Smith acknowledged that all you think about all week is going against "The King." 
 
 "Like, he's -- 6-foot-3, 6-4, 260 [pounds], whatever he weighs -- [and he looks like] a Greek god," Smith said. "So, you were definitely going down there making sure you had your chin strap maybe a little tight, a little extra air in your helmet and everything like that." 
 
 In addition to ascending the NFL's career rushing yards, Henry has become the benchmark for durability among running backs. He's the active leader with 2,662 career carries, which are 822 more than any other current running back. 
 
 Henry scoffed this summer when asked about whether he has contemplated retirement. When he recently told a podcast that he would like to finish his career with the Ravens, he felt it got misconstrued that he was soon calling it quits. 
 
 Henry wrote on social media: "I never said anything about retiring lol , I'm enjoying being a Raven . I'll worry about that retirement s--- later ." 
 
 Ravens offensive tackle Ronnie Stanley said no one should try to predict when Henry is walking away from the game. 
 
 "As long as he is having fun and he feels good, he could play as long as he wants because they do not build humans like that," Stanley said. 
 
 
 
 So could Henry eventually become the NFL's all-time rushing champion? He's 5,337 yards behind Emmitt Smith, who ran for a league-best 18,355 in his 15-year career. 
 
 If Henry plays five more seasons (including this one) to equal Smith, he would need to average 1,068 yards each year to capture the No. 1 spot. 
 
 Hill thinks Henry can do it. 
 
 "There's no end in sight for him," Hill said. "You talk to some guys, and they're like, 'I get one more good season, maybe two more.' You couldn't tell that with Derrick . He might play another five years."
